Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

A **symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group** consists of a finite nonempty index set $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ ([[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[def-symmetrizable-generalized-cartan-matrix]]) and a chosen diagonal symmetrizer $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ with $d_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and $d_i a_{ij}=d_j a_{ji}$ for all $i,j$; free abelian groups $P^\vee$ and $P$ ([[def-free-abelian-group]]) with an integer-valued bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^\vee\to\mathbb Z$; simple coroots $h_i\in P^\vee$ that are linearly independent in $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$; and simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ that freely generate the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]) and satisfy $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ for all $i,j$ ([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

The index set is finite and $A$ need not be nonsingular. We do not require the simple coroots to span $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$, and the pairing is not required to be perfect; choosing $P$ and $P^\vee$ is part of the datum, not something determined by the matrix alone.

We fix an indeterminate $q$ over $\mathbb Q$, work over $\mathbb Q(q)$, and set $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $h\in P^\vee$, $\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ is the exponent in $q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}$. We use the row convention $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ throughout. No fundamental weights with prescribed values on all $h_i$ are part of this definition.

A ring homomorphism whose kernel contains a two-sided ideal factors uniquely through the quotient ring.

If $I\mathrel{\trianglelefteq}R$, $f:R\to S$ is a ring homomorphism, and
$I\subseteq\ker f$, there is a unique ring homomorphism $\bar f:R/I\to S$ such
that $\bar f(r+I)=f(r)$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, step 2.2).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

derivations.claim: Finite rank-one orbits. Fix $i$ and $v\in V$. Then $W:=\operatorname{span}\{F_i^aE_i^bK_i^cv:a,b\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z\}$ is a finite-dimensional $A_i$-stable subspace, where $A_i$ is the algebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$: the toral operator $K_i$ acts diagonally on the finitely many nonzero label components of $v$, so the vectors $K_i^cv$ span a finite-dimensional subspace; by [A3] there is $B$ with $E_i^bv=0$ for $b\ge B$; the mixed relation of [A2] rewrites any word in $E_i,F_i$ as a linear combination of words $F_i^aE_i^b$ with coefficients in the algebra generated by $K_i$; and one may choose finitely many $K_i^cv$ spanning the toral orbit and use local nilpotence of $F_i$ on their finitely many $E_i^b$-images to bound $a$. The span of the resulting finite set is stable under $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$.

The second finite module. Fix $i\ne j$ and set $W':=\operatorname{span}\{F_i^aE_i^bK_i^cF_jw:w\in W,\ a,b\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z\}$. Since $W$ is finite-dimensional, step 1.1 applied to each of the finitely many vectors $F_jw$ exhibits $W'$ as a finite union of finite-dimensional $A_i$-stable subspaces; hence $W'$ is a finite-dimensional $A_i$-stable subspace of $V$ containing $F_jW$.

The rank-one adjoint module. On the finite-dimensional space $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ define operators by $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)(T)=K_iTK_i^{-1}$, $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)(T)=(E_iT-TE_i)K_i$ and $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)(T)=F_iT-K_iTK_i^{-1}F_i$. Substituting these formulas, using $K_iE_i=q_i^2E_iK_i$, $K_iF_i=q_i^{-2}F_iK_i$ and $E_iF_i-F_iE_i=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ on $W,W^{\prime}$, gives $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)^{-1}=q_i^2\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)$, $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)^{-1}=q_i^{-2}\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ and $[\mathrm{Ad}(E_i),\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)]=(\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)-\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Thus these formulas give a rank-one module directly. Moreover $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)$ is diagonalizable because $K_i$ acts diagonally on $W$ and $W'$, and $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i),\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ are locally nilpotent: $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)$ raises and $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ lowers the $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)$-weight by $2$, the weights of $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ form a finite set, and decomposing any $T$ into weight components each orbit is supported on distinct weights and hence terminates.

$F_j$ is a highest vector of weight $m$. Since $F_jW\subseteq W'$, the restriction $T:=F_j|_W$ lies in $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$. By [A2], $E_iF_j=F_jE_i$ for $i\ne j$, so $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)(T)=(E_iT-TE_i)K_i=0$; and by [A1], $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)(T)=K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}T$, because $\langle\alpha_j,d_ih_i\rangle=d_ia_{ij}$. Put $m:=-a_{ij}\ge0$, the off-diagonal Cartan entries being nonpositive. Thus $T$ is annihilated by $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)$ and has $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)$-weight $q_i^m$ with $m\ge0$.

The rank-one string bound. Assume $T\ne0$. In the rank-one module $\operatorname{Hom}(W,W')$ of steps 3.1-4.1 let $t\ge1$ be minimal with $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^tT=0$; it exists by the local nilpotence of step 3.1. For $b\ge1$ the divided-power formula of [F3] gives $\mathrm{Ad}(E_i)\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{(b)}(T)=\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{(b-1)}\Theta_{i,b}(T)$, and $\Theta_{i,b}$ acts on $T$ by the scalar $\frac{1}{q_i^b-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}(q_i^{m-2s}-q_i^{-m+2s})=\frac{q_i^{m-b+1}-q_i^{-m+b-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}=[m-b+1]_i$, by summing the two geometric progressions. Taking $b=t$ and using $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^tT=0$ together with $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{(t-1)}T=[t-1]_i!^{-1}\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{t-1}T\ne0$ gives $[m-t+1]_i=0$, hence $m-t+1=0$ by [F2], that is $t=m+1$; therefore $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^{m+1}T=0$.

The Serre sum. By induction on $n\ge0$, using $\mathrm{Ad}(K_i)(T)=q_i^mT$ and the Pascal recurrence of [F4], the powers of the adjoint action expand as $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)^n(T)=\sum_{r=0}^{n}(-1)^rq_i^{r(m-n+1)}\binom{n}{r}_iF_i^{n-r}TF_i^r$: the case $n=0$ is clear, and applying $\mathrm{Ad}(F_i)$ to the formula for $n$, conjugating $K_iF_i^{n-r}TF_i^rK_i^{-1}=q_i^{m-2n}F_i^{n-r}TF_i^r$ and comparing the coefficient of $F_i^{n+1-r}TF_i^r$ uses exactly $C_{n+1,r}=q_i^rC_{n,r}+q_i^{r-n-1}C_{n,r-1}$, the second form of [F4]. At $n=m+1=1-a_{ij}$ every Laurent exponent $r(m-n+1)$ is zero, so step 5.1 gives $\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r=0$ on $W$. Since every $v\in V$ lies in such a $W$ by step 1.1, the negative Serre relation holds as an operator on all of $V$.

The positive Serre relation. Put $E_i':=F_i$, $F_i':=E_i$ and $K_h':=K_{-h}$ for all $i$ and $h$. The primed data again satisfies the toral, toral-action, mixed and local-nilpotence hypotheses [A1]-[A3]: for instance $K_h'E_i'K_h'^{-1}=K_{-h}F_iK_h=q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i=q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i'$, while $E_i'F_i'-F_i'E_i'=F_iE_i-E_iF_i=-(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})=(K_i'-K_i'^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Applying steps 1.1-6.1 to the primed data gives $\sum_{r}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r=0$ on $V$, which is the positive Serre relation for the original data.

Conclusion. By [A1]-[A3] the operators satisfy all the defining relations of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$: the toral and toral-action relations, the mixed commutators, and both Serre families by steps 6.1 and 7.1. Hence the universal property [F1] equips $V$ with a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure; it is unique because $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is generated by these operators, and it is a chosen $P$-graded type-one weight module by construction. Local nilpotence is exactly [A3], so the module is integrable, and by [F5] the admissible $i$-string decomposition applies to every vector; step 1.1 supplies the finite rank-one $U_i$ orbit. No finite-dimensionality of the full weight spaces is asserted or used.

and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is

If the prefix of length $\ell$ contains at least $k$ letters $i$ it has at most $b-1$ non-$i$ letters and length $\ell=(b-1)+L_{b-1}$, so it is zero by the induction hypothesis and $w=0$. derivations.claim: Conventions and PBW coordinates. Put $\kappa_a=-\tau_a$ for every color pair, so $\kappa_w=(-1)^{\ell(w)}\tau_w$ has the same degree and is a PBW basis with the source dot and braid signs. For $n\ge1$, embed $R(n)$ on positions $1,\ldots,n$ and $R_1(n)=\xi_nR(n)$ on positions $2,\ldots,n+1$; their overlap is $R_1(n-1)$ on positions $2,\ldots,n$. Write $k^I=\bigoplus_{j\in I}k\epsilon_j$ for the color algebra. Choosing reduced words adapted to the cosets gives the left PBW decomposition $R(n+1)=\bigoplus_{a=1}^{n+1}R(n,1)\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_a$ and the right PBW decomposition $R(n+1)=\bigoplus_{a=1}^{n+1}\kappa_a\cdots\kappa_n(k^I[x_{n+1}]\otimes_kR(n))$, where the product for $a=n+1$ is $1$. These are labelled decompositions: polynomial and idempotent coefficients keep the transferred color, and crossing degrees are summed on the actual word. PBW independence follows by using those reduced coset words followed by a reduced word in $S_n$; the resulting products have additive lengths and are precisely the chosen PBW basis.

The empty-word case. At $\beta=0$ the KLR presentation gives $R(0)=k$ and $R(\alpha_j)=k[x_1]e(j)$ with $\deg x_1=2d_j$. The empty word has no last strand, so its $E_i$-restriction is zero on the weight-graded category, without introducing a negative-height algebra. Both append inductions of a graded $k$-module $M$ are $k[x_1]e(j)\otimes_kM$. Orthogonality of $e(i),e(j)$ gives $E_iF_jM=E_i\bar F_jM=0$ for $i\ne j$, whereas $E_iF_iM=E_i\bar F_iM\cong M\otimes_kk[t_i]$ by $x_1^a\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes t_i^a$, naturally and in degree zero. Thus (a) is zero-to-zero, (b) has precisely the polynomial summand with coefficient $1$, and (c) is $0\to0\to M\otimes_kk[t_i]\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}M\otimes_kk[t_i]\to0$, since $(\alpha_i\mid0)=0$. The uncolored overlap formula involving $R_1(n-1)$ below is used only for $n\ge1$.

The same-end double cosets. For $n\ge1$ define $T:R(n)\otimes_{R(n-1)}R(n)\to R(n+1)$ by $x\otimes y\mapsto x\kappa_ny$, with both outer algebras embedded on the first $n$ positions. It is balanced because $\kappa_n$ commutes with the generators on positions $1,\ldots,n-1$. Decompose the first factor as the right $R(n-1)$-module $\bigoplus_{a=1}^n\kappa_a\cdots\kappa_{n-1}(k^I[x_n]\otimes_kR(n-1))$. For a polynomial/color coefficient $f(x_n)$, the dot move gives $f(x_n)\kappa_n=\kappa_nf(x_{n+1})+c$, where $c$ lies in the polynomial/idempotent algebra on the first $n+1$ positions and its last-color projector equals its adjacent-color projector; consequently $\kappa_a\cdots\kappa_{n-1}c\,y$ lies in $R(n,1)$. Modulo $R(n,1)$ the image is therefore exactly $\kappa_a\cdots\kappa_nf(x_{n+1})y$. These are the right PBW cosets $a=1,\ldots,n$, bijectively, with coefficient $1$, so the induced quotient map is an isomorphism. Inclusion of $R(n,1)$ then gives the actual bimodule isomorphism $T\oplus\mathrm{incl}:R(n)\otimes_{R(n-1)}R(n)\oplus R(n,1)\to R(n+1)$: injectivity and surjectivity follow by first passing to the quotient and then to the included summand. This retains all nonidentity cosets, rather than discarding cosets $a>1$.

The opposite-end overlap map. For $n\ge1$, multiplication defines a balanced $(R(n),R_1(n))$-bimodule map $U:R(n)\otimes_{R_1(n-1)}R_1(n)\to R(n+1)$, $x\otimes y\mapsto xy$. The PBW decomposition in the last $n$ positions is $R_1(n)=\bigoplus_{a=2}^{n+1}(R_1(n-1)\otimes_kk^I[x_{n+1}])\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_a$. Tensoring this displayed free decomposition identifies the domain of $U$ with $\bigoplus_{a=2}^{n+1}R(n,1)\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_a$. Multiplication maps each basis element to the identically named PBW element, so $U$ is injective and its image $J$ is exactly those cosets. Using the opposite PBW decomposition gives also $J=\bigoplus_{a=0}^{n-1}\kappa_a\cdots\kappa_1R(1,n)$, where $a=0$ is the empty product. Thus $J$ is the overlap bimodule, not a two-sided ideal, and the quotient has the sole remaining transfer coset $R(n,1)\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_1$, equivalently $\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_1R(1,n)$.

Correct same-end colored kernels. For an input weight $ eta$ set $\delta= eta-\alpha_i$ and $\gamma=\delta+\alpha_j$. When $\delta\in Q_+$, the kernel of $E_iF_j$ is $e(\gamma,i)R( eta+\alpha_j)e( eta,j)$, an $(R(\gamma),R( eta))$-bimodule. Cutting the isomorphism of step 2.1 by these idempotents gives the image under $T$ of $R(\gamma)e(\delta,j)\otimes_{R(\delta)}e(\delta,i)R( eta)$, the kernel of $F_jE_i$. The factors project onto the two colors interchanged by $\kappa_n$, so its degree is exactly $-b_{ij}$, and the image is the domain shifted by $-b_{ij}$. If $\delta
otin Q_+$, $E_i$ has zero restriction on the input weight because no word of weight $ eta$ ends in $i$; the transfer summand is zero, without writing any algebra at a negative weight. For $i
e j$ the one-strand-enlarged word then also has no $i$ endpoint, so $E_iF_j$ is zero. The other summand $R(n,1)$ preserves the last color, so it vanishes exactly for $i
e j$; for $i=j$ its corner is $R( eta)\otimes_kk[t_i]$, with $\deg t_i=2d_i$. Hence the bimodule maps give (a)'s same-end isomorphism and (b), with coefficient $1$ on the polynomial summand. Tensoring an actual bimodule isomorphism with any graded input module preserves it; no exactness or flatness assumption is needed for this passage.

The quotient and its right splitting. Put $w=\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_1$. Move a dot or crossing along $w$ by the local relations. Modulo $J$ these moves give $x_aw=w x_{a+1}$ for $1\le a\le n$, $x_{n+1}w=w x_1$, and $\kappa_aw=w\kappa_{a+1}$ for $1\le a<n$. Dot corrections remove one crossing and braid corrections remove the three-crossing braid block; in each case the surviving permutation fails to transfer the first endpoint all the way to the last endpoint, so its PBW coset is among $a=2,\ldots,n+1$ and lies in $J$. Idempotents simply follow the same cyclic permutation. These generator identities prove $a f(x_{n+1})w=w\xi_n(a)f(x_1)$ in the quotient. Taking the coefficient of $w$ therefore identifies the underlying bimodule quotient with $R(n)\otimes_kk^I[t]$, the right $R(n)$ action being through $\xi_n$, and both indicated endpoint dots becoming $t$. The color algebra is retained because the transferred endpoint can have any color. Its right PBW expression $w(k^I[x_1]\otimes_kR_1(n))$ provides a right $R_1(n)$-linear section of the quotient map by choosing those same PBW representatives. It need not be a bimodule section. Hence the sequence defined by $U$ and this coefficient map is right-split before any tensoring.

Opposite-end colored kernels and degrees. With $\delta,\gamma$ as in step 3.1 and $\delta\in Q_+$, the kernel of $E_i ar F_j$ is $e(\gamma,i)R( eta+\alpha_j)e(j, eta)$, with right $R( eta)$ action through $\xi_n$. Cutting $U$ identifies its overlap submodule with $R(\gamma)e(j,\delta)\otimes_{R(\delta)}e(\delta,i)R( eta)$, the kernel of $ ar F_jE_i$, by the plain multiplication map; this map adds no crossing and has degree zero. The quotient transfer word $w$ takes bottom $(j,
u)$ to top $(
u,j)$, so this quotient corner vanishes for $i
e j$ and gives the unshifted opposite-end isomorphism in (a). For $i=j$ and $
u$ of weight $ eta$, $w e(i,
u)$ has degree $-\sum_a b_{i
u_a}=-(\alpha_i\mid eta)$. Thus the quotient corner is $q^{-(\alpha_i\mid eta)}R( eta)\otimes_kk[t_i]$, with the label $i$ fixed and $\deg t_i=2d_i$. The right section in step 3.2 respects these color projectors and this degree shift, so the colored sequence is split as right $R( eta)$-modules. Tensoring with any graded $M$ retains its injective first map and exact quotient and gives precisely (c), functorially, with the stated shift. If $\delta
otin Q_+$ the overlap corner is zero; at $ eta=0$ this agrees with step 1.2.

Conclusion. Steps 1.2 and 3.1 establish the same-end mixed isomorphisms, and step 4.1 establishes the opposite-end isomorphism and exact sequence for every weight. All maps are the explicit homogeneous PBW corner maps above; the opposite-end sequence is right-split before tensoring, and the uncolored expression retains its transferred-color labels and uses $n\ge1$. The dots, crossing signs and shifts are those of the fixed native grading, with the source normalization $\kappa=-\tau$ affecting only unit PBW coefficients. No quotient flatness, uniform shift for all labelled cosets, or negative-height algebra is assumed.

derivations.claim: Monic splitting and the vertex ring. Over the universal coefficient ring $S=k[c_1,\dots,c_N]$, adjoin roots of the monic framing polynomial one at a time and divide by the root: at step $s$ the residual polynomial is monic of degree $N-s+1$, so ordinary monic division preserves monicity. This produces the Artin basis $X_1^{a_1}\cdots X_N^{a_N}$, $0\le a_k\le N-k$, of the full root algebra; the pairing that reads the top coefficient has Gram matrix zero below the anti-diagonal and unit anti-diagonal in reversed order, hence is perfect over $S$, with no factorial division and no characteristic hypothesis. Block decomposition into the $r$ roots of $c_r$ and the $N-r$ roots of $b_{N-r}$ makes $L_m$ finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$, and $L_m=0$ for $r>N$ because then $p_m$ has degree below $r$.

The vertex ring as a matrix quotient. Representing $\mathrm{NH}_r$ as the matrix algebra on its Artin module (step 1.1, [F2]) shows that the two-sided ideal generated by a monic $p(X_1)$ is the matrix ideal of the coefficients of the remainder of $p$ modulo $c_r$, and monic division makes these coefficients a unit triangular change from the consecutive relations; hence $\mathrm{NH}_r/(p(X_1))$ is the matrix algebra over the monic factor ring $L_m$ of the Statement. The same computation shows the $i$-flag $B_m$ is free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over $L_{m+i}$, giving the two root extensions of the model.

The four coefficient maps and their triangles. For a monic $f$, the polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ is defined before imposing $f(X)=f(Y)=0$ and satisfies $(X-Y)K_f=f(X)-f(Y)$ and $\tau_XK_f=1$; therefore $\tau_X(X^aK_f)=Y^a$ for every $a$, which identifies $K_f$ with the dual-power-basis Casimir of the two monic coefficient forms. The two Casimirs of $b_{N-r}$ and $c_{r+1}$ give the four displayed cups and caps; their contractions are the identities $\sum_av_a\tau(z^ab)=b$ and $\sum_a\tau(bv_a)z^a=b$ for dual Artin bases, and substituting them into the tensor composites proves both triangles of each of the two adjunctions. Degrees: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$; $\tau_{\mathrm{new}}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$; the first maps have degree $0$ after the $B\{-2d_ir\}$ shift; the second cap has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)+2d_ir=-2d_i(h_m-1)$, with inverse degree on its unit. Restoring the normalized $H_i$ at its input weight produces exactly the four formal degrees of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]].

The rank-one intertwiner and its inverse. Splitting off one extra $i$-strand by the two-coset PBW decomposition [F3] gives the transfer term $\kappa_rb$ and the new-dot algebra as its complement; the rank-one intertwiner $g=(u-X)-(u-X)^2\kappa$ is verified to satisfy its quadratic and dot-commutation identities by expanding $\kappa X_{r+1}-X_r\kappa=1$ and $\kappa^2=0$. Multiplying these intertwiners along the extra strand and the other transfer by $p(X_1)$, then projecting to the polynomial complement, yields a coefficient map $A$ with $A(u^kS_r)=(-1)^ru^kp(u)$ where $S_r(u)=\prod_{a\le r}(u-X_a)^2$, and the same mixed relation gives $\phi_{k+1}(u)=u\phi_k+E(\psi_k)$; hence $A(u^k)=(-1)^r\operatorname{quo}_{S_r}(u^kp)$ by uniqueness of monic division, with no cyclotomic commutator theorem used as a supplier. If $h_m\ge0$ the quotients have distinct leading degrees $h_m+k$ and unit leading coefficients $(-1)^r$, so $\rho$ is the displayed (transfer, dot-power unit) map from $F_iE_i\{-2d_i\}$ plus the $h_m$ identity columns to $E_iF_i$, and its inverse subtracts the section and inverts the transfer. If $h_m\le0$ the map $A$ is surjective with kernel $\mathrm{span}\{1,u,\dots,u^{-h_m-1}\}$, and the connecting images have an anti-triangular dot/cap matrix with unit anti-diagonal, whose successive solution gives the negative-branch inverse. This verifies the rank-one matrix and both inverse equations of the formal definition.

Same-color crossing, curl and bubble identities. Equal crossings act by $\kappa=(s-1)/(X-Y)$, so $\kappa^2=0$, the braid relation holds and the two mixed dot equations follow from the rational divided-difference expansion; $K_f$ is symmetric, so its divided-difference correction vanishes and $(X-Y)K_f=f(X)-f(Y)$ gives the dot-mate equations. Contracting a crossing against either Casimir and using the rank-one block inverse of step 4.1 produces the cross-and-cap/curl equations: expanding $(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the power bases and taking the top-coefficient rows gives the four signed sums over $a+b=-1$ and $a+b+c=-1$ with the stated orientation signs. The resulting oriented bubble Laurent series is $\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ of leading degree $h_m=N-2r$; its reciprocal is the opposite series with product $1$ coefficient by coefficient, forced by composing the two flag coefficient pairings, since each existing $i$ root contributes one factor from each side of the cap. Appending an $i$ root $z$ changes $\Phi_i$ to $\Phi_i/(u-z)^2$ and appending a spectator $j$ root $y$ changes it to $\Phi_iQ_{ij}(u,y)/t_{ij}$; expanding at infinity gives every finite bubble-slide coefficient equation. At a monic vacuum, $a_i(x)x^{\ell-1}=0$ gives $h_\ell+\sum_jc_{\lambda_i-j}h_{\ell-j}=0$ with $h_0=1$, $h_{<0}=0$, so $H(t)a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)=1$. All coefficients use only addition, multiplication and monic formal inversion.

Downward $Q$-relations and exact word grading. Give every flag the ordered shift $s_j(m)$ of the Statement. For $j<k$ the increasing word $(j,k)$ maps to the word $(k,j)$ by a quotient/switch of underlying degree $0$, with target-minus-source unit shift $-b_{jk}$; the reverse operator has underlying degree $-2b_{jk}$ and unit-shift $+b_{jk}$, so both have actual degree $-b_{jk}$, and same-color divided differences have degree $-2d_j$. Native operators are the negatives of the source operators, so their degrees and two-crossing composites are unchanged. The ordinary polynomial operators satisfy the idempotent, dot, far-commutation and quadratic $Q$-relations directly; expanding a three-strand composition gives zero difference for distinct outer colors and the divided difference of $Q$ for equal outer colors, and the global substitution $\kappa=-\tau$ changes all cubic signs to the native numerator. The quotient relations descend: on an $i,j$ pair $D_1$ has $bq=0$ and $D_0$ has $b=0$, and $Qb=t_{ij}bq$ makes multiplication by $Q$ well defined while the other crossing is the literal quotient.

Mixed cups and caps with their constants. In $D[z]/p$ versus $D[z]/(pq)$ the coefficient form satisfies $\tau_{pq}(Qf)=t_{ij}\tau_p(f)$, because $Q=t_{ij}q$ and the leading coefficient of $Qf$ is $t_{ij}$ times that of $f$. For a full existing $i$-string use the ordered residue form $t_r^p(z)=(-1)^{r(N-r)}\operatorname{Res}\bigl(\Delta_r(X)X_1^{r-1}\cdots X_{r-1}\operatorname{Tr}(z)/\prod_ap(X_a)\bigr)$, in which no $1/r!$ occurs; expanding parabolic divided differences verifies this over the universal integral coefficient ring, and over its generic-root fraction field the sum over root orderings is the Vandermonde determinant whose two factors cancel the internal root-difference denominator, so the identity is an integral polynomial identity and specializes to every field. With $p'=pq$ and $U_r=\prod_aQ_{ij}(X_a,y)$, cancellation gives $t_r^{p'}(U_rz)=(-1)^{rA_{ij}}t_{ij}^rt_r^p(z)$, and perfectness of the model forms makes $U_r$ injective on the old quotient. Testing the relative cap against these forms gives $\pi_r\varepsilon_r^{p'}(Q(X_{r+1},y)\operatorname{lift}(z))=(-1)^{A_{ij}}t_{ij}\varepsilon_r^p(z)$ for every nil-Hecke coset element. Normalizing the second maps by the global weight sign $(-1)^{h+1}$ — legitimate because $N$ and $h$ have the same parity and the new $N$ changes by $A_{ij}$ — cancels that sign and gives the exact constant $t_{ij}$; dual-power-basis contraction gives the mixed-unit equation, and reversing colors gives $t_{ji}$ with the stated double-mate ratio. Native minus signs occur twice in these composites, so the scalars persist.

Conclusion. Steps 3.1-6.2 verify every defining relation of [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]] on the explicit flag modules: the generators and their degrees, both adjunction triangles, the rank-one matrices in both branches with their inverses, the bubble series and slides, the cross-and-cap equations, the mixed isomorphism with its scalars, and the downward $Q$-relations. Monic extensions, their Casimirs, the finite rank-one inverses and the coefficient identities survive arbitrary monic specialization as ungraded maps, and the construction is choice-free. This proves only the formal MODEL relations; faithfulness and the cyclotomic word-corner transfer belong to separate suppliers.

The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$, with $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$, and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
$$\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}.$$
Thus the second adjunction reverses the two blocks and has the displayed shift; same-ordered unshifted biadjunction is not asserted. The formula is an isomorphism of functors and holds on arbitrary graded $B$-modules after interpreting the right side with the block-flip equivalence. This is distinct from the cyclotomic $E_i/F_i$ biadjunction theorem. Moreover $eR(\beta+\gamma)e'$ has a finite Mackey filtration indexed by nonnegative four-block weight matrices with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, whose subquotient is the corresponding composite four-block restriction, flip of the middle blocks and induction bimodule, shifted by $-(b\mid c)$; the same statement holds for arbitrary numbers of blocks.

derivations.claim: Nil-Hecke branching. Put $z=t_r$ and write $E_a$ for the elementary symmetric polynomials in $t_1,\dots,t_{r-1}$. The relations $e_a=E_a+zE_{a-1}=0$ give $E_a=(-z)^a$ for $1\le a\le r-1$, and the top relation gives $z^r=0$; hence $C_r=k[t_1,\dots,t_{r-1}]\otimes_{k[E_1,\dots,E_{r-1}]}k[z]/(z^r)$ with $E_a$ acting by $(-z)^a$. The polynomial representation of $\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}$ is free of rank $(r-1)!$ over its symmetric center and identifies $\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}$ with the matrix algebra over that center; after the specialization its image on $C_r$ is $\mathrm{Mat}_{(r-1)!}(k[z]/(z^r))$ with standard column $C_r$. Therefore the graded socle and head of $C_r$ are each one shifted copy of the nil-Hecke simple, the simple composition coefficient is a shift of $[r]_i$, multiplication by $z$ has nilpotence index exactly $r$, the socle is the column over $z^{r-1}k$ and the head the column modulo $z$. For $r=1$ this reads $C_1=k$, $z=0$. The same computation with the first variable distinguished gives first-end branching, and matrix units plus a monic Artin basis make it valid in every characteristic. More generally, induction of $L(i^r)\boxtimes L(i^n)$ is killed by the positive symmetric center: each total elementary symmetric function restricts to a sum of products of the positive elementary functions in the two blocks. Its dimension is $\binom{r+n}{r}r!n!=(r+n)!$ by the shuffle basis. The augmentation quotient of $\mathrm{NH}_{r+n}$ is the full matrix algebra with simple column dimension $(r+n)!$, so this induced module is one shifted copy of $L(i^{r+n})$.

Simple socle of one-step restriction. Let $S$ have $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$ and let $U\subseteq E_iS$ be a simple subobject with $t=\epsilon_i(U)$. The final dot $z$ commutes with $R(\beta-\alpha_i)$ and acts nilpotently on $E_iS$ (positive dot degree and finite graded support), preserving the socle and its ungraded isotypic components; on the isotypic component containing $U$ a nonzero power of $z$ has a nonzero kernel copy of the same simple type killed by $z$, and absolute simplicity and the finite graded semisimple decomposition let that copy be chosen homogeneously with the appropriate shift. Adjunction therefore produces a nonzero map $\operatorname{Ind}(U,L_1)\to S$, hence a surjection, and the shuffle bound [F4] gives $r\le t+1$ while the exact defining corners give $t\le r-1$; so $t=r-1$.

The maximal corner. Apply the maximal $(r-1)$-tail corner $p$ to $E_iS$, retaining $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)\otimes\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}$. By [F3], $\Delta_i^rS\cong N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$, so $p(E_iS)=N\boxtimes\operatorname{Res}_{\mathrm{NH}_{r-1}}L(i^r)$; by step 1.1 and the absolute simplicity of $N$ this has a single simple socle. Every simple subobject $U$ of $E_iS$ has $t=r-1$ by step 1.2, so [F3] makes $pU$ a nonzero simple object; exactness of $p$ makes $p(\operatorname{soc}E_iS)$ semisimple and injects it into the one-simple socle of $p(E_iS)$. Hence $\operatorname{soc}E_iS$ is a single simple object, once, with $\epsilon_i=r-1$; moreover every nonzero submodule of $E_iS$ contains a simple graded submodule whose $p$-image is nonzero (detection).

Simple head, detection and the dot index. Finite graded duality $D$ is exact, takes simples to simples, fixes corner idempotents and commutes with restriction, so applying step 2.1 to $DS$ (same $\epsilon_i$) and dualising gives a single simple head of $E_iS$, once; the maximal corner of its head is the head of $N\boxtimes\operatorname{Res}L(i^r)$, while the maximal corner of its socle is that tensor's socle. By step 1.1 these are shifts of the same $N\boxtimes L(i^{r-1})$. The unique-head recursion of [F3] therefore identifies their simple shift orbits. On $p(E_iS)$, step 1.1 gives $z^r=0$ and $z^{r-1}\ne0$; the image of $z^r$ on all of $E_iS$ is a graded submodule with zero $p$-corner, so detection in step 2.1 forces it to be zero, while nonvanishing of $z^{r-1}$ in the corner forces it to be nonzero globally. Hence the last-dot nilpotence index on $E_iS$ is exactly $r$; repeating with the first variable gives first-dot index exactly $\epsilon_i^L(S)$.

Nonreduced induction and its unique head. Put $M_n=\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))$, $n\ge1$. Its maximum tail is at most $r+n$ by the shuffle bound; at tail $r+n$ the Mackey filtration retains exactly all $n$ added $i$-strands together with $r$ terminal $i$-strands of $S$, its surviving corner is $N\boxtimes\operatorname{Ind}_{\mathrm{NH}_r\otimes\mathrm{NH}_n}^{\mathrm{NH}_{r+n}}(L(i^r)\boxtimes L(i^n))$. The final computation of step 1.1 makes this $N\boxtimes L(i^{r+n})$ up to the fixed shift. Every simple quotient $T$ of $M_n$ has that maximum tail: adjunction gives a nonzero injection $S\boxtimes L(i^n)\hookrightarrow\Delta_i^nT$, and restricting the first factor to the maximal $r$-tail retains a nonzero corner of $T$'s maximal corner, so $\epsilon_i(T)\ge r+n$, and the shuffle bound gives equality. Hence the finite semisimple head of $M_n$ has only constituents detected by its simple maximal corner, so it is one simple constituent, once; the kernel of $M_n\to\operatorname{hd}M_n$ has zero maximal corner, so every other composition factor has smaller $\epsilon_i$ and the head occurs exactly once in the whole composition series. Write $f_iS:=\operatorname{hd}M_1$.

Partial inverses, iterates and the cyclotomic criterion. Adjunction realises $S$ in $E_i(f_iS)$, so step 2.1 gives $\operatorname{soc}E_if_iS=S$ with shifts restored; conversely $S=\operatorname{soc}E_iT$ implies $T$ is a simple quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(S,L_1)$, hence $T=f_iS$. Thus one-step socle and head are partial inverses, $f_i$ raises $\epsilon_i$ by one and $\operatorname{soc}E_i$ lowers it by one; iterating the one-strand argument gives $\operatorname{hd}\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))=f_i^nS$. Let $J^\Lambda$ be generated by $x_1^{\lambda_i}$ on every word beginning with $i$; it annihilates a simple $S$ exactly when each first-$i$ corner has first-dot index at most $\lambda_i$, which by step 3.1 is $\epsilon_i^L(S)$, so $J^\Lambda S=0$ iff $\epsilon_i^L(S)\le\lambda_i$ for every $i$; if a generator is nonzero, simplicity forces $J^\Lambda S=S$. Right restriction preserves first strands, hence the cyclotomic subcategory; for induction, the generic unique head either survives, in which case the quotient induction has the same head, or dies, in which case the quotient induction is zero because every nonzero finite module has a simple quotient. The maximal-$\epsilon$ composition part is the same simple shift orbit as the head and socle, with coefficient a shift of $[r]_i$ by step 1.1. No choice and no self-dual representative is used.

Fix a color $i$ and the formal proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], on a symmetrizable real
Cartan datum with finite index set and arbitrary field $k$. Use the native KLR
parameters of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], degrees of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], the PBW convention of
[[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], and the nil-Hecke matrix/idempotent convention
of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Then the polynomial
flag construction described below realizes all the defining graded diagram
relations of that formal category, including its rank-one cross/cap,
bubble-slide/inversion and mixed-color cup/cap relations; it asserts a
representation of the formal proof category, not faithfulness or a cyclotomic
quotient identification.

**The model.** Choose a color order with $i$ last. For spectator alphabets
$Y_j$ of sizes $m_j$ ($j\ne i$) put $C=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}k[Y_j]^{S_{m_j}}$,
$r=m_i$, $A_{ij}=-a_{ij}$,
$t_{ij}=[u^{A_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$,
$q_{ij}=Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$, and choose a monic framing polynomial $a_i(u)$ of
degree $\lambda_i$; initially its coefficients have their universal homogeneous
degrees, so all formulas are graded, and the standard specialization is
$a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. Set
$$p_m(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}q_{ij}(u,y),\qquad N=\lambda_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j,\qquad h_m=N-2r,$$
and $c_r(u)=u^r-e_1u^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^re_r$. The vertex ring $L_m$ is the
monic factor ring for $p_m=c_rb_{N-r}$, equivalently $C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$ modulo
all coefficients beyond degree $N-r$ of the monic expansion $p_m/c_r$; it is
finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$ and is zero for $r>N$. Its $i$ flag is
$B_m=L_m[z]/b_{N-r}(z)$, free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over
$L_{m+i}$, with the target root alphabet obtained by adjoining $z$. The
underlying spectator flag is $C_m^j=L_m[y]$; its target action appends $y$ to
$Y_j$ and replaces $p_m$ by $p_mq_{ij}(u,y)$.

**The shifts and generators.** Every downward generator carries the ordered
shift $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$. Thus
$G_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the $B_m\{-2d_ir\}$ tensor functor; $G_j$ for
$j\ne i$ is the $C_m^j\{s_j(m)\}$ tensor functor. The basic reversed $i$ flag
is $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}=B_m\otimes_{L_{m+i}}-$ without a shift, whereas the
formal upward generator at INPUT vertex $m$ is
$H_i(m)=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(m)\{-d_i(1+h_m)\}$. These are distinct
conventions. The basic flags have degree-zero
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\{t_i(m)\}\dashv F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$, where
$t_i(m)=-2d_i(h_m-1)$. At vertex $m$ the formal first unit and second cap have
degree $d_i(1-h_m)$, and the formal first cap and second unit have degree
$d_i(1+h_m)$.

**The four maps and the Casimir.** All four maps are the explicit dual-basis
maps of the two monic coefficient forms on $B_m$: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}:B_m\to
L_m$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$;
$\tau_{\mathrm{new}}:B_m\to L_{m+i}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$.
The first cap is $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto\tau_{\mathrm{new}}(b_1b_2)$ and the
first cup is its dual-power-basis Casimir; the second cap and cup use
$\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$. For a monic polynomial $f$ their Casimir is the
polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the two-root quotient.

**Crossings, colors and bubbles.** Source crossings are
$\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for EVERY color pair. Source equal-color
operators are $(s-1)/(X-Y)$; source unequal operators are the switch/quotient
in the increasing-color direction and switch times $Q$ in the reverse
direction. Thus native operators are their negatives, and both actual crossing
degrees are $-b_{jk}$ with the ordered shifts above. On the $i,j$ pair the
successive underlying rings are
$D_1=L_m[y,z]/(b(z)q_{ij}(z,y))$ and $D_0=L_m[y,z]/b(z)$, with source maps
$\pi:D_1\to D_0$ and $f\mapsto Q_{ij}(z,y)f:D_0\to D_1$; their normalized
opposite-sideways composites have the scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$, and in the
NE/SW-$i$, NW/SE-$j$ source orientation the double-mate ratio is
$t_{ji}/t_{ij}$. Native minus signs leave the two-crossing scalars and the
ratio unchanged. The basic isomorphism $E_iG_j\cong(G_jE_i)\{-b_{ij}\}$ holds,
and the normalized formal $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$ is unshifted.

**Realized equations.** The canonical rank-one $\rho$ and its inverse, the
same-color cross/cap equations, the bubble series
$\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ and its reciprocal, and the finite-coefficient
bubble-slide identities are realized by the stated polynomial maps. In
particular the normalized positive $h$ identity columns have degrees
$d_i(1-h+2k)$ for $0\le k<h$, and the negative branch uses the inverse
crossing plus the dot/cap rows. All polynomial pairings and relations persist
after arbitrary monic coefficient specialization as UNGRADED identities; such
a specialization does not assert nilpotence, a homogeneous trace degree, or a
highest-weight $K_0$ claim. No geometry, characteristic restriction, or
one-dimensional-Hom hypothesis is imposed.

**Ground ring and graded algebras.** Fix a commutative ring $k$. A **graded
$k$-algebra** is a $k$-algebra $A$ in the sense of
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], together with a direct sum
decomposition of $k$-modules

$$A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}A_i$$

such that $A_iA_j\subseteq A_{i+j}$ for all $i,j\in\mathbb Z$ and
$1_A\in A_0$. It is **unital and associative** when its underlying ring is;
every graded algebra on this page is unital and associative. Since
$\eta_A(r)=r\,1_A$ and $A_0$ is a $k$-submodule containing $1_A$, the structure
map has image in $A_0$, so each $A_i$ is a $k$-submodule and the scalars act
centrally on $A$.

**Graded modules and bimodules.** A **graded left $A$-module** is a left
$A$-module $M$ with a decomposition $M=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}M_d$ of
$k$-modules such that

$$A_iM_d\subseteq M_{i+d}\qquad\text{for all }i,d\in\mathbb Z .$$

A **graded right $A$-module** is a right $A$-module with a decomposition
$M=\bigoplus_dM_d$ such that $M_dA_i\subseteq M_{d+i}$ for all $i,d$. A
**graded $(B,A)$-bimodule** is a $(B,A)$-bimodule ([[def-bimodule]]) that is
graded as a $k$-module and homogeneous under both actions, the two actions
continuing to commute. Both induced $k$-actions must agree with the given
$k$-module structure: $\eta_B(t)m=tm=m\eta_A(t)$ for $t\in k$ and $m\in M$. Elements of $M_d$ are **homogeneous of degree $d$**, and
the decomposition expresses every $m\in M$ uniquely as a finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components.

**Degree-zero maps.** A map $f:M\to N$ of graded left $A$-modules is
**degree-zero**, or a **graded map**, when it is $A$-linear and
$f(M_d)\subseteq N_d$ for every $d$. The category $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$
has the graded left $A$-modules as objects and the degree-zero maps as
morphisms, with composition of maps. Every $M$ is an object of
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ by its own grading, and $A$ is a graded
$(A,A)$-bimodule under left and right multiplication.

**Graded submodules.** A **graded submodule** of a graded left $A$-module $M$ is
a submodule $S\le M$ with $S=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(S\cap M_d)$. Such an $S$
is itself a graded left $A$-module with homogeneous pieces
$S_d:=S\cap M_d$, because $A_iS_d\subseteq A_iM_d\cap S\subseteq M_{i+d}\cap S=S_{i+d}$;
equivalently, $S$ is generated by its homogeneous elements. In particular a
graded submodule is determined by its homogeneous pieces: if
$S=\bigoplus_dS_d$ and $T=\bigoplus_dT_d$ are graded submodules with $S_d=T_d$
for every $d$, then $S=T$.

**Internal shift.** For $r\in\mathbb Z$ and a graded module $M$, the
**internal shift** $M\{r\}$ is the module with

$$(M\{r\})_d:=M_{d-r}\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z),$$

carrying the same scalar action as $M$. Its components are additive subgroups
of $M$ whose sum is direct, so $M\{r\}$ is a $k$-module; and $M\{r\}$ is
graded because

$$A_i(M\{r\})_d=A_iM_{d-r}\subseteq M_{i+d-r}=(M\{r\})_{i+d}$$

for all $i,d$. For a graded bimodule both actions are unchanged, remain
homogeneous and still commute, so $M\{r\}$ is again a graded bimodule. The
shift is invertible: $(M\{r\})\{-r\}=M$, and $M\{0\}=M$. For a graded algebra
$A$, the shifts $A\{r\}$ of the regular bimodule are the modules denoted
$A\{r\}$ elsewhere on this page.

**Dictionary with the published twist.** In the published nonnegative
commutative convention ([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]) the twist $M(a)$
is the graded module with $M(a)_d=M_{d+a}$ for every integer $a$. Substituting
$a=-r$ gives

$$(M\{r\})_d=M_{d-r}=M(-r)_d ,$$

so $M\{r\}=M(-r)$ as graded modules: the internal shift **reverses** the sign of
the published twist parameter. For $r=0$ both conventions agree with $M$.

**No super signs.** The internal degree is a genuine $\mathbb Z$-grading, not a
$\mathbb Z/2$-parity. No sign is inserted into the multiplication, the scalar
action or a degree-zero map merely because elements have nonzero degree; the
balancing relation of the tensor product below is likewise signed by nothing.
These are the unsigned associative conventions for this page; no differential
or signed symmetry on tensor products is part of this definition. They do not
exclude Koszul sign conventions in other categories of graded objects.

derivations.claim: Bubble slides on the model. For an $i$ root $x$ the normalized bubble series changes by $(1-xt)^{\pm2}$, and for a spectator $j$ root $y$ it changes by $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)^{\pm1}$ with $q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$ of constant coefficient $1$. These hold directly because the model series is $p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2$, adjoining an $i$ root multiplies $c_r$ by $u-x$, and adjoining a spectator root multiplies $p$ by $Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$; every fixed inverse coefficient is a finite polynomial recursion. These are the specified formal relations, checked on the model and not derived from the faithfulness being proved.

Straightening to normal form. Move dots to fixed component positions using cyclicity and the KLR dot moves; an equal-color correction has one fewer crossing. Sort each $i$ cup/cap towards a boundary or the far-left closed-component position using the specified mate equations: a main term passes one of its finitely many crossing obstacles, and a correction term removes an unsorted open-component extremum or such an obstacle. Rank-one cross-and-cap sums are finite because open dot counts are nonnegative and negative-degree bubbles vanish, bounding the indices at each fixed total degree; adjacent opposed cup/cap pairs cancel by the triangles. Induct on the lexicographic pair (unsorted extrema, remaining crossing obstacles) and on crossing length for correction terms. Closed components have color $i$; cancel extra extrema, slide them left by the finite coefficient equations, and express the reverse family by bubble inversion. Coxeter deletion plus the KLR braid and quadratic straightening then reduce every open matching to the selected reduced diagram, all braid defects being shorter. This gives a finite spanning family of reduced matchings with dot monomials and far-left bubble monomials.

All-downward boundaries. At an all-downward boundary every open arc joins bottom to top, so it is a colored permutation; the reduced matching together with its dots is exactly a KLR PBW monomial, and the morphism space is the PBW corner tensored with the polynomial ring in the positive bubble family, whose opposite family is the coefficientwise reciprocal by bubble inversion. For general boundaries the two triangles give invertible Hom correspondences bending the upward $i$-endpoints to the other boundary, and the straightening of step 2.1 has unit leading matching coefficients, so the same normal form transfers.

Independence by degree separation. Fix the physical source weight $\mu$ and write $\mu_i=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$; choose spectator background counts $m_j$ with $A_{\mathrm{spect}}=\sum_{j\ne i}(-a_{ij})m_j$ and for an increasing background $i$-count $r$ set $N=\mu_i+2r$, $\lambda_i=N-A_{\mathrm{spect}}$, so the physical weight $N-2r=\mu_i$ is fixed. Use the universal monic framing $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}+z_1u^{\lambda_i-1}+\cdots+z_{\lambda_i}$ with independent $\deg z_a=2d_ia$, put $p=a_i\prod_{j\ne i}Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $c_r=\prod_a(u-x_a)$; the normalized series $\mathcal B(t)=p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2=a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}U(t)$ with $U_0=1$ has coefficients $\mathcal B_a=z_a+\sum_{1\le\ell<a}z_\ell U_{a-\ell}+U_a$, unit triangular in the framing variables, with reciprocal coefficients $-z_a$ plus lower framing indices. Hence the first $D$ bubble coefficients are independent whenever $\lambda_i\ge D$, in every characteristic and at every physical weight; no unit old-root coefficient is claimed, since $\mathcal B_1=p_1+2e_1$ can lose its root term in characteristic two. A nonzero finite PBW/bubble combination remains nonzero after this triangular substitution over the independent polynomial coefficient domain; the generic KLR polynomial representation has a distinct nonzero leading permutation for each selected crossing word, so a polynomial test vector with nonzero output exists after clearing a finite denominator. Let $D$ bound the bubble indices and $B$ the actual internal degrees of that vector and its output, both finite in the untruncated polynomial ring, and let $L$ bound the number of added $i$-flags tested. Every monic flag relation and factor-ring coefficient relation after those flags has degree at least $2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)$, spectator appends only increase $N$, all variables are nonnegatively graded and all dot degrees are positive; choosing $r\ge0$ and $\lambda_i\ge D$ with $2d_i(\mu_i+r-L+1)>B$ (possible at fixed $\mu$) separates all model relations from degree $\le B$, so the nonzero PBW output survives in that flag model.

Conclusion. The family of step 2.1 spans every morphism space by a finite straightening, and step 4.1 shows that no nonzero combination of its reduced matchings, dot monomials and independent bubble monomials vanishes in some graded flag model, so the family is a basis and the stated models are jointly faithful. The model's ordered word shifts with $i$ last make every crossing homogeneous of degree $-b_{jk}$, and the formal upward generator is the normalized $H_i$, so the witness is a witness in the specified graded model; the assertion concerns the formal proof category before any cyclotomic quotient transfer.

derivations.claim: Comparison modules and their projectivity. Put $n=|\beta|$ and let $R_1(\beta)=\xi_nR(\beta)$ act on positions $2,\ldots,n+1$. For $n>0$ set $J_0=Sa(x_1)R(\beta)e_R$ and $J_1=Sa(x_2)R_1(\beta)e_L$; for $n=0$ set $J_0=J_1=0$, since the old block has no cyclotomic relation. Put $K_0=Se_R/J_0$, $K_1=Se_L/J_1$. The right action of $A[t]$ on $K_0$ uses the first $n$ strands and $t=x_{n+1}$; on $K_1$ it uses $\xi_n$ and $t=x_1$. The labelled PBW cosets make $Se_R$ and $Se_L$ finite projective over the corresponding separated-block algebras $R(\beta)[t]$: each homogeneous coset summand is a shifted principal word-idempotent module. Tensoring these summands with $A[t]$ gives precisely $K_0,K_1$, so both are finite projective over $A[t]$. At $n=0$ both are $k[t]$.

Monic annihilators and projectivity, locally. Let $0\to P_1\xrightarrow{j}P_0\to M\to0$ be an exact sequence of right $A[t]$-modules with finite projective $P_0,P_1$, and suppose a central monic $f$ annihilates $M$. Multiplication by $f$ is injective on a free $A[t]$-module by its unit leading coefficient, hence on its projective summands. On a finite free module monic division gives an $A$-linear operator $p_{\mathrm{free}}$ taking a polynomial to its quotient by $f$, with $p_{\mathrm{free}}(xf)=x$. Choose split inclusion $u:P_1\to A[t]^N$ and projection $v:A[t]^N\to P_1$; then $p=vp_{\mathrm{free}}u$ satisfies $p(xf)=x$ on $P_1$, since $u$ is $A[t]$-linear and $vu=1$. Since $fM=0$, multiplication by $f$ on $P_0$ has image in $j(P_1)$, defining $h:P_0\to P_1$ by $jh=f$. Injectivity of $j$ gives $hj=f$ on $P_1$, so $phj=1$. Thus $j$ has the $A$-linear retraction $ph$, and $M$ is a direct summand of the $A$-projective module $P_0$ and is $A$-projective. Equivalently, $P_r/fP_r$ is a summand of $(A[t]/fA[t])^N\cong A^{mN}$ and is $A$-projective, which is the monic-quotient reason for the splitting. This argument uses finite projective presentations and division and does not assume $f$ invertible or the target $M$ projective.

The cyclotomic ideal and the map $P$. Throughout put $\kappa_a=-\tau_a$. The first-position PBW cosets give $S=\sum_{r=0}^n(k^I[x_1]\otimes R_1(n))\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_r$. Since $a(x_1)$ commutes with this coefficient algebra, $Sa(x_1)S=\sum_{r=0}^nSa(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_r$. After multiplying by $e_R$, terms $r<n$ lie in $J_0$; the remaining term is the image of $\widetilde P:Se_L\to K_0$, $u\mapsto ua(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_n$. Thus its image is the kernel of $K_0\to Be_R$, where $B=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$. To check right linearity, move $x_{a+1}$ through $a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_n$ to $x_a$ and move $x_1$ to $x_{n+1}$. Each mixed-relation correction omits one transfer crossing and has the form, up to its color projector and sign, $(\kappa_{a+1}\cdots\kappa_n)a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_{a-1}$, hence belongs to $J_0$. Moving $\kappa_{a+1}$ to $\kappa_a$ introduces only the braid correction $a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_{a-1}D_a\kappa_{a+2}\cdots\kappa_n$, with $D_a$ a dot polynomial; the far crossings can be moved left and the last-dot powers commute with the shorter word, again putting it in $J_0$. Idempotents follow the cyclic transfer. These generator identities prove $\widetilde P$ is right $R(\beta)[t]$-linear. It therefore kills $J_1$, and induces an $(S,A[t])$-map $P:K_1\to K_0$ with the same image.

Intertwiners and the map $Q$. Define $g_a=\kappa_a$ on unequal adjacent colors and $g_a=(x_{a+1}-x_a)-(x_{a+1}-x_a)^2\kappa_a$ on equal colors. The source mixed relations give $x_{s_a(b)}g_a=g_ax_b$ for every $b$. They also give $\kappa_ag_{a+1}g_a=g_{a+1}g_a\kappa_{a+1}$: subtract the two sides and use the mixed relations to see that the difference intertwines $x_a$ with $x_{a+2}$ and fixes $x_{a+1}$. In the faithful localized polynomial realization [F4], its longest-permutation coefficients cancel, since both products cross the same three color pairs with the same factors. All remaining permutations have length at most two, and none interchanges $a$ and $a+2$ while fixing the middle variable. Independence of the permutation operators then forces every coefficient to vanish. Consequently right multiplication by $g_n\cdots g_1$ intertwines old dots/crossings with their shifted copies and $x_{n+1}$ with $x_1$. It descends to $Q:K_0\to K_1$: the first-position cosets write $J_0$ as the sum of the terms $Sa(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_r e_R$, $r<n$, and the intertwining identities send each such term to $Sg_n\cdots g_1a(x_2)\kappa_2\cdots\kappa_{r+1}e_L\subseteq J_1$. Thus $Q$ is an $(S,A[t])$-map; at $n=0$ it is the identity.

Projectivity of the cyclotomic bimodules. The appended dot on $M=Be_R$ is annihilated by a central monic scalar-coefficient polynomial by [F2]. Apply step 1.2 to the projective $A[t]$-resolution in step 5.1, with $M=Be_R$, to conclude that $Be_R$ is right $A$-projective. This module is finitely generated over $A$: its finite $A[t]$-generators together with dot powers below the degree of the annihilator generate it over $A$. In the homogeneous standard case the resolution and $M$ are graded; decompose the resulting $A$-linear splitting into homogeneous components on finite homogeneous generators, and take its degree-zero component to get a graded splitting. The left $B$-module $Be_R$ is a direct summand of $B$, hence induction sends any projective $A$-module, presented as a summand of a free module, to a projective $B$-module; finite generators remain finite under induction. A finitely generated projective $B$-module is a summand of a finite direct sum of shifts of $B$, and its restriction is consequently a summand of the corresponding finite direct sum of shifts of $e_RB$. Left $A$-projectivity and finite generation of $e_RB$ from step 6.1 therefore show that restriction preserves finitely generated projectives. These arguments apply ungraded to monic deformations as well.

The exact sequence (c). Tensor the bimodule resolution $0\to q^sK_1\xrightarrow{P}K_0\to Be_R\to0$ of step 5.1 over $A$ with a left $A$-module $M$. It remains exact because its cokernel $Be_R$ is right $A$-projective by step 6.1, so the original sequence is split as a sequence of right $A$-modules. By their definitions in step 1.1, $K_1\otimes_A M$ is the left-append generic induction $\bar F_iM$ and $K_0\otimes_A M$ is the right-append generic induction $F_iM$, while $Be_R\otimes_A M=F_i^\Lambda M$. The map $P$ is left $R(\beta+\alpha_i)$-linear and has homogeneous degree $s=(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)$, giving exactly the functorial sequence in (c) in the declared target category. On the ungraded monic-deformation branch the same sequence is interpreted without a grading shift.

Conclusion. The projectivity, preservation and exact-sequence arguments prove (a), (b) and (c) with the displayed shift, in the graded standard case with graded projectives and verbatim ungraded for a monic deformation; the comparison is monic and no filtered-colon citation is used.

Fix a color $i$ and the formal proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], on a symmetrizable real
Cartan datum with finite index set and arbitrary field $k$. Use the native KLR
parameters of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], degrees of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], the PBW convention of
[[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], and the nil-Hecke matrix/idempotent convention
of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Then the polynomial
flag construction described below realizes all the defining graded diagram
relations of that formal category, including its rank-one cross/cap,
bubble-slide/inversion and mixed-color cup/cap relations; it asserts a
representation of the formal proof category, not faithfulness or a cyclotomic
quotient identification.

**The model.** Choose a color order with $i$ last. For spectator alphabets
$Y_j$ of sizes $m_j$ ($j\ne i$) put $C=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}k[Y_j]^{S_{m_j}}$,
$r=m_i$, $A_{ij}=-a_{ij}$,
$t_{ij}=[u^{A_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$,
$q_{ij}=Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$, and choose a monic framing polynomial $a_i(u)$ of
degree $\lambda_i$; initially its coefficients have their universal homogeneous
degrees, so all formulas are graded, and the standard specialization is
$a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. Set
$$p_m(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}q_{ij}(u,y),\qquad N=\lambda_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j,\qquad h_m=N-2r,$$
and $c_r(u)=u^r-e_1u^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^re_r$. The vertex ring $L_m$ is the
monic factor ring for $p_m=c_rb_{N-r}$, equivalently $C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$ modulo
all coefficients beyond degree $N-r$ of the monic expansion $p_m/c_r$; it is
finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$ and is zero for $r>N$. Its $i$ flag is
$B_m=L_m[z]/b_{N-r}(z)$, free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over
$L_{m+i}$, with the target root alphabet obtained by adjoining $z$. The
underlying spectator flag is $C_m^j=L_m[y]$; its target action appends $y$ to
$Y_j$ and replaces $p_m$ by $p_mq_{ij}(u,y)$.

**The shifts and generators.** Every downward generator carries the ordered
shift $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$. Thus
$G_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the $B_m\{-2d_ir\}$ tensor functor; $G_j$ for
$j\ne i$ is the $C_m^j\{s_j(m)\}$ tensor functor. The basic reversed $i$ flag
is $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}=B_m\otimes_{L_{m+i}}-$ without a shift, whereas the
formal upward generator at INPUT vertex $m$ is
$H_i(m)=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(m)\{-d_i(1+h_m)\}$. These are distinct
conventions. The basic flags have degree-zero
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\{t_i(m)\}\dashv F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$, where
$t_i(m)=-2d_i(h_m-1)$. At vertex $m$ the formal first unit and second cap have
degree $d_i(1-h_m)$, and the formal first cap and second unit have degree
$d_i(1+h_m)$.

**The four maps and the Casimir.** All four maps are the explicit dual-basis
maps of the two monic coefficient forms on $B_m$: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}:B_m\to
L_m$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$;
$\tau_{\mathrm{new}}:B_m\to L_{m+i}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$.
The first cap is $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto\tau_{\mathrm{new}}(b_1b_2)$ and the
first cup is its dual-power-basis Casimir; the second cap and cup use
$\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$. For a monic polynomial $f$ their Casimir is the
polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the two-root quotient.

**Crossings, colors and bubbles.** Source crossings are
$\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for EVERY color pair. Source equal-color
operators are $(s-1)/(X-Y)$; source unequal operators are the switch/quotient
in the increasing-color direction and switch times $Q$ in the reverse
direction. Thus native operators are their negatives, and both actual crossing
degrees are $-b_{jk}$ with the ordered shifts above. On the $i,j$ pair the
successive underlying rings are
$D_1=L_m[y,z]/(b(z)q_{ij}(z,y))$ and $D_0=L_m[y,z]/b(z)$, with source maps
$\pi:D_1\to D_0$ and $f\mapsto Q_{ij}(z,y)f:D_0\to D_1$; their normalized
opposite-sideways composites have the scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$, and in the
NE/SW-$i$, NW/SE-$j$ source orientation the double-mate ratio is
$t_{ji}/t_{ij}$. Native minus signs leave the two-crossing scalars and the
ratio unchanged. The basic isomorphism $E_iG_j\cong(G_jE_i)\{-b_{ij}\}$ holds,
and the normalized formal $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$ is unshifted.

**Realized equations.** The canonical rank-one $\rho$ and its inverse, the
same-color cross/cap equations, the bubble series
$\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ and its reciprocal, and the finite-coefficient
bubble-slide identities are realized by the stated polynomial maps. In
particular the normalized positive $h$ identity columns have degrees
$d_i(1-h+2k)$ for $0\le k<h$, and the negative branch uses the inverse
crossing plus the dot/cap rows. All polynomial pairings and relations persist
after arbitrary monic coefficient specialization as UNGRADED identities; such
a specialization does not assert nilpotence, a homogeneous trace degree, or a
highest-weight $K_0$ claim. No geometry, characteristic restriction, or
one-dimensional-Hom hypothesis is imposed.

Fix a color $i$. In the formal graded minimal-parabolic proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], the reduced
perfect-matching diagrams, dot monomials on their open components, and
monomials in the independent far-left normalized $i$-bubble coefficients form
a basis of every morphism space. In particular, at all-downward boundaries of
weight difference $\beta$, the morphism space is the corresponding KLR PBW
corner tensored with the polynomial ring in one positive bubble family; the
opposite/fake family is its coefficientwise reciprocal. The graded polynomial
flag models of
[[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]],
with universal monic framing and arbitrarily large auxiliary framing at each
fixed physical source weight, are jointly faithful. The assertion is about this
formal proof category before cyclotomic quotient transfer.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set $I$ and no imaginary
simple roots, a KLR datum $Q=(Q_{ij})_{i\ne j}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4), and a
field $k$ placed in degree zero
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]); let
$R=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R(\beta)$ be the resulting graded KLR algebra, with
its idempotents $e(\nu)$, dots $x_a$, crossings $\tau_a$ and degrees
$\deg x_a=2d_{\nu_a}$, $\deg\tau_a=-b_{\nu_a\nu_{a+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). Let $\Lambda$ be a
dominant integral weight and put $\lambda_i:=\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle\ge0$
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

**Cyclotomic data.** For every color $i$ choose a monic polynomial
$a_i(u)\in k[u]$ of degree exactly $\lambda_i$
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]); the standard choice made
below is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. For $n\ge1$ write
$$a(x_s)=\sum_{\nu\in I^n}a_{\nu_s}(x_s)e(\nu)\qquad(1\le s\le n),$$
the element of $R_n(Q)$ that acts on the $\nu$-component by the monic
polynomial $a_{\nu_s}$ in the dot at position $s$.

**The cyclotomic quotient.** For $\beta\in Q_+$ define $J_a(\beta)$ to be the
two-sided ideal of $R(\beta)$ generated by the first-strand elements
$a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)$, $\nu\in I^\beta$; equivalently
$$J_a(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}R(\beta)\,a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)\,R(\beta),$$
and put
$$R_a^\Lambda(\beta):=R(\beta)/J_a(\beta),\qquad R_a^\Lambda(0):=k .$$
The **cyclotomic KLR algebra** is the direct sum
$R_a^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$; it carries the
local units $e(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu)$, which act as the identity
on $R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$ and annihilate the other summands, and it is a
$k$-algebra with these orthogonal idempotents.

**Standard choice and grading.** The STANDARD choice $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$ is
used throughout the graded categorification, duality-normalization and based
statements below; for it we write $R^\Lambda:=R^\Lambda_a$. Under the standard
choice each individual first-strand generator
$x_1^{\lambda_{\nu_1}}e(\nu)$ is homogeneous of degree
$2d_{\nu_1}\lambda_{\nu_1}$ in the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], so the ideal $J_a(\beta)$
and the quotient $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ are graded, and $R^\Lambda$ is a
$\mathbb Z$-graded algebra with local units. The sum $a(x_1)$ itself need not
have one common degree across different colors, and no single degree is
assigned to it.

**Boundary of the definition.** Arbitrary monic polynomials with lower
coefficients in degree-zero $k$ give an UNGRADED deformation $R_a^\Lambda$;
nilpotent dots, homogeneous trace degree and the highest-weight graded $K_0$
identification are not asserted for that branch, and the ungraded branch is
used only where a statement explicitly says so. Finite dimension, finite root
strings, ordinary projectivity and symmetry of the standard quotient have the
separately stated monic conclusions below. The cyclotomic relation is imposed
on the FIRST strand, and cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]); this convention
fixes the side on which the quotient map acts throughout the page.

This definition uses no choice.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix a reduced-expression system: for each $w\in S_n$ one reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_r}$, and for $
u\in I^n$ put $	au_w:=	au_{i_1}\cdots	au_{i_r}\in R_n(Q)$. Then the monomials $	au_wx_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}e(
u)$, over all $w\in S_n$, $a_1,\dots,a_n\ge0$ and $
u\in I^n$, form a $k$-basis of $R_n(Q)$; equivalently $R_n(Q)$ is a free $k$-module on these monomials, and $R( eta)$ has the corresponding basis. Moreover each $R( eta)$ has finite-dimensional homogeneous components, and the graded dimension of the summand $e(
u)R_n(Q)e(
u')$ is the formal Laurent Hilbert series counting the monomials (bounded below, equivalently the finite sum of the corresponding rational geometric series), so the graded ranks are independent of the parameters $Q$: for each fixed $ eta$, $\dim_kR( eta)_m<\infty$ for all $m$ and $R( eta)_m=0$ for $m\ll0$; if $I$ is finite the same holds for $R_n(Q)$. In particular $R( eta)$ is a locally finite graded algebra; its degree-zero part need not be one-dimensional (already $x_1	au_1\in R(2\alpha_i)_0$ is a nontrivial idempotent).

The rank-one identities give $h_\ell=0$ for $\ell<0$ and $h_0=1$. Closing $a_i(x)x^{\ell-1}=0$ for $\ell\ge1$ is lawful in the defining ideal because the exponent $\ell-1$ is nonnegative even when some resulting bubble indices are negative, and gives $h_\ell+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}h_{\ell-1}+\cdots+c_{i,0}h_{\ell-\lambda_i}=0$. Hence $H(t)=\sum_{\ell\ge0}h_\ell t^\ell$ is the inverse of $a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)=1+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}t+\cdots+c_{i,0}t^{\lambda_i}$, and bubble inversion gives $A(t)=H(t)^{-1}=a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}(t)$; each coefficient uses only a finite recurrence.
