Let $k$ be any field and $R(Q)$ the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum and any homogeneous $Q$ satisfying the standing symmetry and
nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared
up to internal shift. For a simple $S$ of root weight $\beta$ and
$r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, its ordinary one-step last-$i$ restriction has a single
simple graded socle and a single simple graded head, each once and of the same
shift orbit, with $\epsilon_i=r-1$; its maximum-$\epsilon$ composition part has
coefficient a grading shift of $[r]_i$. The last-dot nilpotence index on that
restriction is exactly $r$. The first-end statements hold with
$\epsilon_i^L$ and the first dot. For every $n\ge1$,
$\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))$ has a unique simple graded head
$f_i^nS$, occurring once in its whole composition series, with
$\epsilon_i=r+n$ (also when $r=0$); all other constituents have smaller
$\epsilon_i$. One-step simple socle and simple induction head are partial
inverses. A simple $S$ survives the first-strand cyclotomic quotient with
exponents $\lambda_i$ exactly when $\epsilon_i^L(S)\le\lambda_i$ for all $i$.
Right restriction preserves surviving simples, while projected right induction
has the same simple head when that generic head survives and is zero
otherwise. These are shift-orbit assertions and do not assert factorial socle
multiplicity.

Let $R$ be any graded KLR datum in this page over any field $k$. For a finite-dimensional graded module $M$ of weight $\beta$ set $\epsilon_i(M)=\max\{r:e(\beta-r\alpha_i,r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$. If $S$ is simple and $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, there is a simple graded $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)$-module $N$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$ such that $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$, where $L(i^r)$ is the unique nil-Hecke simple up to shift. Conversely, for any such $N$, $\mathrm{Ind}(N\boxtimes L(i^r))$ has a unique simple graded head $S$, appearing once as a composition factor, with $\epsilon_i(S)=r$ and $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$; every other composition factor has smaller $i$-tail. The graded simples of every $R(\beta)$ remain simple without grading and are absolutely simple; all ordinary endomorphisms are $k$ and nonzero homogeneous endomorphisms have degree $0$. The classes of normalized simples and their projective covers are therefore unscaled dual shift-orbit bases for the projective/simple Hom pairing. For each $\beta$ there is a finite family of ordered divided-power words $Y_b$ whose normalized projective classes pair triangularly with the simple classes, with diagonal entries $1$ after choosing the simple grading shifts. Thus the selected $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$; arbitrary divided words span, but need not be a basis. The identical statements hold for maximal FIRST-color blocks, with $\epsilon_i^L(M)=\max\{r:e(r\alpha_i,\beta-r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$, restriction $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}$ and induction $\mathrm{Ind}(L(i^r)\boxtimes N)$.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta,\gamma\in Q_+$. Put $A=R(\beta+\gamma)$, $B=R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)$, $e=e(\beta,\gamma)$ and $c=(\beta\mid\gamma)$. The bimodules $eA$ and $Ae$ are ungraded free respectively as left and right $B$-modules, of rank $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$. As GRADED modules they are finite projective direct sums of the appropriate principal idempotent $B$-modules with labelled shuffle shifts: for each concatenated word $\xi=\nu\ast\eta$ the right-module summand $e(\xi)B$ has shift $\delta_R(w,\xi)=\deg(\tau_we(\xi))$ and the left-module summand $Be(\xi)$ has shift $\delta_L(w,\xi)=\deg(e(\xi)\tau_w)=\delta_R(w,w^{-1}\xi)$, using respectively the corresponding right and left minimal shuffle representatives $w$; these degrees depend on the labels, and no common shift for an entire $B$ copy is asserted. The functors $\mathrm{Ind}=Ae\otimes_B-$ and $\mathrm{Res}=e(-)$ of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] are exact, commute with internal shifts, and preserve finitely generated graded projectives. $\mathrm{Ind}$ is left adjoint to $\mathrm{Res}$. The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$, with $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$, and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
$$\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}.$$
Thus the second adjunction reverses the two blocks and has the displayed shift; same-ordered unshifted biadjunction is not asserted. The formula is an isomorphism of functors and holds on arbitrary graded $B$-modules after interpreting the right side with the block-flip equivalence. This is distinct from the cyclotomic $E_i/F_i$ biadjunction theorem. Moreover $eR(\beta+\gamma)e'$ has a finite Mackey filtration indexed by nonnegative four-block weight matrices with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, whose subquotient is the corresponding composite four-block restriction, flip of the middle blocks and induction bimodule, shifted by $-(b\mid c)$; the same statement holds for arbitrary numbers of blocks.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let $M$ be a
$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) whose support is contained in
a finite union of cones,

$$\operatorname{supp}M\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{s}(\lambda_j-Q_+)\qquad(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s\in P),$$

where $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Choose a finite free direct
coordinate summand $X_f\subseteq P$ (with respect to a free basis of $P$,
[[def-free-abelian-group]]) containing all $\lambda_j$ and all $\alpha_i$, and
set

$$Y_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb ZH_i\Bigr)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z),\qquad X_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\operatorname{Hom}(Y_{\mathrm{aux}},\mathbb Z),$$

with the evaluation pairing $X_{\mathrm{aux}}\times Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\to\mathbb Z$.
Define $j\colon X_f\to X_{\mathrm{aux}}$ by $j(x)(H_i):=\langle x,h_i\rangle$ and
$j(x)(f):=f(x)$ for $f\in\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)$, and put
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}:=j(\alpha_i)$. Then:

(i) $(I,A,D,X_{\mathrm{aux}},Y_{\mathrm{aux}},q)$ with the simple roots
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ and simple coroots $H_i$ is a symmetrizable Cartan
datum for a quantum group with the same generalized Cartan matrix $A$ and the
same symmetrizer $D$; its pairing is perfect, the $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ are
linearly independent, the $H_i$ are primitive and independent, and integral
fundamental weights $\Lambda_j$ ($\Lambda_j(H_i)=\delta_{ij}$) exist. Here
$\langle\alpha_j^{\mathrm{aux}},H_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ is the original convention
([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]],
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

(ii) $M$ carries a unique structure of $X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one
quantum weight module for the auxiliary datum with
$\operatorname{supp}M^{\mathrm{aux}}\subseteq j(X_f)$, namely
$$M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{j(x)}:=M_x\quad(x\in X_f),\qquad M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{\xi}:=0\quad(\xi\notin j(X_f)),$$
$$K_{(n,f)}\ \text{acts on}\ M_x\ \text{by}\ q^{\sum_in_i\langle x,h_i\rangle+f(x)}\qquad\bigl((n,f)\in\textstyle\bigoplus_i\mathbb ZH_i\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)\bigr),$$
with the actions of $E_i$, $F_i$ and of the simple coroots
$K_{d_iH_i}$ unchanged. In particular the old $K_h$ action is recovered from
the label $x$ as $q^{\langle x,h\rangle}$, and the old and auxiliary $E_i,F_i$
actions agree.

(iii) The two recipes are inverse on objects and grading-preserving morphisms:
on $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules with labels in $X_f$ and support as above, the
identity on underlying vector spaces is an equivalence between the category of
$P$-graded type-one modules and the corresponding full subcategory of
$X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one modules with labels in $j(X_f)$. This is not
an embedding of the old torus algebra into the new one and is asserted only
inside this finite-support category.

(iv) The construction applies simultaneously to Verma modules and highest weight
modules (supported in $\lambda-Q_+$) and to finite tensor products of such
modules (labels add), by choosing one $X_f$ containing all participating upper
weights and all simple roots; the tensor-product $E_i,F_i$ formulas of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]] are unchanged because only the diagonal toral characters change.

(v) Rationally, $h_{\mathrm{aux}}:=Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$
decomposes as $h_{\mathrm{aux}}=H_{\min}\oplus Z$, where $H_{\min}$ is a
minimal realization of $A$ (of dimension $2n-r$, $n=|I|$, $r=\operatorname{rank}A$)
and $Z\subseteq\ker\alpha$ is a complement on which all $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$
vanish, so the elements of $Z$ are central in the correspondingly extended
Kac–Moody algebra; hence the classical Cartan and multiplicity comparisons of
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]] apply to
$H_{\min}$.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta\in Q_+$.
(i) Every finitely generated graded left $R(\beta)$-module has a decomposition into finitely many indecomposable graded modules, unique as a finite multiset of degree-zero graded isomorphism classes, including the actual shifts of their summands; in particular the category $\mathrm{GrMod}_0R(\beta)$ of finitely generated graded modules has the Krull-Schmidt property.
(ii) Every simple graded $R(\beta)$-module is finite-dimensional, killed by the augmentation ideal $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ of the CENTRAL color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$; up to isomorphism and shift there are finitely many, and each has a projective cover which is finitely generated.
(iii) The split Grothendieck group $K_0(R(\beta))$ of finite graded projective modules is a free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module: the classes of the indecomposable finitely generated graded projectives, modulo grading shifts, form a basis with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$; equivalently the classes of all finitely generated indecomposable graded projectives form a shift-orbit basis. Similarly $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of simple modules, and the Hom pairing of projective covers and simples has diagonal entries $\dim_k\operatorname{End}^0(S_b)$, with the selected cover/simple shifts, under the Hom convention of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]].

Let $R$ be any graded KLR datum in this page over any field $k$. For a finite-dimensional graded module $M$ of weight $\beta$ set $\epsilon_i(M)=\max\{r:e(\beta-r\alpha_i,r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$. If $S$ is simple and $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, there is a simple graded $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)$-module $N$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$ such that $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$, where $L(i^r)$ is the unique nil-Hecke simple up to shift. Conversely, for any such $N$, $\mathrm{Ind}(N\boxtimes L(i^r))$ has a unique simple graded head $S$, appearing once as a composition factor, with $\epsilon_i(S)=r$ and $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$; every other composition factor has smaller $i$-tail. The graded simples of every $R(\beta)$ remain simple without grading and are absolutely simple; all ordinary endomorphisms are $k$ and nonzero homogeneous endomorphisms have degree $0$. The classes of normalized simples and their projective covers are therefore unscaled dual shift-orbit bases for the projective/simple Hom pairing. For each $\beta$ there is a finite family of ordered divided-power words $Y_b$ whose normalized projective classes pair triangularly with the simple classes, with diagonal entries $1$ after choosing the simple grading shifts. Thus the selected $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$; arbitrary divided words span, but need not be a basis. The identical statements hold for maximal FIRST-color blocks, with $\epsilon_i^L(M)=\max\{r:e(r\alpha_i,\beta-r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$, restriction $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}$ and induction $\mathrm{Ind}(L(i^r)\boxtimes N)$.

Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)-(Q4) for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree
$\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the
resulting ordinary quotient. Then: every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic
annihilator in each fixed block; every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over
$k$; and, for fixed $\beta$ and $i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all
sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In
the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is
nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded
functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are
ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $K_0(R):=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}K_0(R(\beta))$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective modules with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$ ([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]).
(i) The induction product $[P][P']:=[\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}(P\boxtimes P')]$ for $P\in K_0(R(\beta)),P'\in K_0(R(\gamma))$ makes $K_0(R)$ a unital associative $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebra, and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ makes it a coassociative counital $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-coalgebra; with the twisted multiplication on $K_0(R)\otimes K_0(R)$ defined by $(x_1\otimes x_2)(x_1'\otimes x_2')=q^{-(|x_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ on homogeneous elements, $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism ([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]]).
(ii) With the divided-power projectives $P_{i,n}$ of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], the classes $[P_{i,n}]$ satisfy, for all $i\ne j$, the divided-power quantum Serre relation
$$\sum_{a+b=-a_{ij}+1}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}]\,[P_{j,1}]\,[P_{i,b}]=0\qquad\text{in }K_0(R),$$
with the convention $[P_{i,0}]=1$, and satisfy $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$ when $a_{ij}=0$; these are the defining relations of the negative half.
(iii) Consequently the assignment $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$ extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism $\gamma:Af\to K_0(R)$ of the divided-power form of the negative half, with $\gamma(\theta_i^{(n)})=[P_{i,n}]$ and $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$; $\gamma$ is compatible with the coproducts ($r$ on $Af$ and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ on $K_0(R)$) and with the bar involutions, and it is $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear.

derivations.claim: Work on the finite support supplied by [F2], prescribing the cyclotomic labels independently there. Write $L_r=L(i^r)$, $c_i=\epsilon_i^L$, and write $\operatorname{Ind}(A,B)$ for induction of the external tensor product; all module identifications below are on shift orbits. Two consequences of exact induction will be used. A surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(A,H)\to T$ with $T$ simple induces a surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(A,U)\to T$ for some simple composition factor $U$ of $H$: take the first nonzero image in an induced composition series. If $\epsilon_i(A)=0$, a nonzero map $\operatorname{Ind}(A,U)\to T$ with $A,U,T$ simple forces $\epsilon_i(T)=\epsilon_i(U)$, since the shuffle bound gives the upper bound and adjunction injects $A\boxtimes U$ into the defining restriction, giving the lower bound. More particularly, a surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(A,B,L_h)\to T$ with $\epsilon_i(A)=0$ factors through $\operatorname{Ind}(A,f_i^hB)\to T$: its tail is $\epsilon_i(B)+h$, whereas every constituent of the kernel of $\operatorname{Ind}(B,L_h)\to f_i^hB$ has smaller tail by [F1], so an induced composition series of that kernel has zero image in $T$.

Here is the rank-two structure needed below, including its parameter calculation. Fix $j\ne i$, put $a=-a_{ij}$ and $t=[u^a]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$. For $p+q\le a$, define $L(i^pji^q)$ to have only the word $i^pji^q$ in its support, with column $L_p\boxtimes L(j)\boxtimes L_q$, the $j$-dot zero and both crossings adjacent to $j$ zero. All relations hold: $Q_{ij}(u,0)=tu^a$, which kills either neighbouring column, and the native $i,j,i$ braid correction is $-t\sum_{r=0}^{a-1}x^rz^{a-1-r}$. Each monomial kills the column since $r\ge p$ or $a-1-r\ge q$ when $p+q\le a$. The other mixed and braid equations have zero terms or are internal nil-Hecke equations. This module is simple by the matrix-column calculation in [F1], with right tail $q$, first tail $p$ and ungraded character $p!q!i^pji^q$. These are all simples of weight $ci+j$ when $c\le a$: induct on $c$; a simple with positive right tail is the unique $f_i$-image of its predecessor, whose tail identifies the constructed column; a simple of right tail zero is supported only on $i^cj$, and the same column argument gives $L(i^cj)$. For $c>a$ no simple can have right tail zero: such a module would again be the column $L_c\boxtimes L(j)$ supported only on $i^cj$, but the last mixed crossing has square $t x_c^a$, nonzero on $L_c$ since its dot index is $c$. This contradicts its zero crossing.

Adjunction and the shuffle bound give $c_i(M)\le c_i(f_jM)\le c_i(M)+\delta_{ij}$; first-end symmetry gives $\epsilon_j(f_i^LM)=\epsilon_j(M)$ for $j\ne i$. If $c_i(f_iM)=c_i(M)+1$, then $f_iM=f_i^LM$: the two orders of induction have the same character at $q=1$ and hence the same ungraded composition multiplicities, while the first order's factor with maximum first tail is uniquely $f_i^LM$, once. The character implication here follows from the triangular divided-word/projective pairing in [F1]: divided-word corner dimensions are obtained from ordinary word-corner dimensions by dividing the corresponding nil-Hecke block factorials at $q=1$, and their triangular matrix with diagonal $1$ remains invertible there. Conversely, equality of the two simple heads forces the increase. The coinduction formula in [F1], together with maximal-tail restriction, gives $\operatorname{soc}\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_h)=(f_i^L)^hM$ and $\operatorname{soc}\operatorname{Ind}(L_h,M)=f_i^hM$: coinduction has only one simple socle, since every simple subobject has the maximum tail by adjunction and its simple maximum corner detects it. Thus $f_iM=f_i^LM$ forces $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_1)$ simple: its head and socle agree and this factor occurs once; in a nonsimple module the socle would lie in the radical and supply a second occurrence. Conversely simplicity forces its socle and head to agree. Commuting $M$ successively past the $h$ single-colour factors, and using $\operatorname{Ind}(L_r,L_s)=L_{r+s}$, gives $\operatorname{Ind}(M,L_h)=\operatorname{Ind}(L_h,M)$; its simple head equals its simple socle and occurs once, so it too is simple. Hence one increase forces increases at all later steps.

Put $D_n=L(i^{a-n}ji^n)$ for $0\le n\le a$. The module $\operatorname{Ind}(D_n,L_1)$ has only two word corners, $i^{a-n}ji^{n+1}$ and $i^{a-n+1}ji^n$, each a simple product of nil-Hecke columns by [F1]. Its simple head has the first corner nonzero. The linear divided restriction Serre relation forces the second corner nonzero too: when applied to that head at weight $(a+1)i+j$, all terms $E_i^{(a+1-s)}E_jE_i^{(s)}$ vanish except $s=n,n+1$, and the $s=n+1$ term is nonzero. The relation is available on finite modules by applying homogeneous Hom to the split projective Serre identity; exact projective Hom and the unscaled pairing in [F1] identify these Hom spaces with the divided corners. Thus the head fills both simple corners and induction is simple, so $f_iD_n=f_i^LD_n$. Step 2.1 proves $\operatorname{Ind}(D_n,L_h)=\operatorname{Ind}(L_h,D_n)$ simple for every $h$. For $c\ge a$, induction on $c$ now classifies all simples of weight $ci+j$ as $\operatorname{Ind}(D_n,L_{c-a})$, $0\le n\le a$, with right tail $n+c-a$: step 1.2 excludes right tail zero for $c>a$, and the one-step partial inverse identifies every positive-tail simple from the preceding weight. For $a=0$, $Q_{ij}$ is a nonzero constant, the mixed crossing is invertible, and $\operatorname{Ind}(L(j),L_h)=\operatorname{Ind}(L_h,L(j))$ is the unique simple, giving the same classification. No characteristic, splitting-field or special binomial-parameter assumption was used.

Define $v_i^\lambda(M)$ as the number of surviving right-$i$ lowering steps in a quotient with labels $\lambda$ containing $M$. It is finite by [F4]. Choose such labels with $\lambda_l\ge c_l(M)$, possible by [F2] and [F1]. If $c_i(f_i^nM)$ never increased, step 2.1 would keep every first tail within those labels for every $n$, contrary to [F4]. Hence $J_i(M)$ is finite; more explicitly, the bound $B_i(\beta,\lambda)$ of [F4] with $R^\lambda(\beta+B_i\alpha_i)=0$ gives $J_i(M)<B_i(\beta,\lambda)$. Step 2.1 gives, for all $h\ge0$, $c_i(f_i^hM)=c_i(M)+\max(0,h-J_i(M))$, and the other first tails are unchanged. The survival criterion in [F1] therefore gives $ v_i^\lambda(M)=J_i(M)+\lambda_i-c_i(M)$. In particular differences $v_i^\lambda(X)-v_i^\lambda(Y)$ for two surviving simples are independent of the containing labels, and $J_i(f_iM)=\max(0,J_i(M)-1)$. This proves finiteness and the recurrence without using the numerical jump formula.

For extraction put $c=c_i(M)$ and $U=(e_i^L)^cM$, so $M=(f_i^L)^cU$ and $c_i(U)=0$. If $c_i(f_jM)=c$, then $(e_i^L)^cf_jM=f_jU$. Indeed induce $L_c,U,L(j)$ onto $f_jM$ and apply maximal first-$i$ restriction, then its simple quotient. In the Mackey filtration the $U$-contribution of first $i$'s is zero; for $j
e i$ the only surviving factors after forgetting the first column are shifts of $\operatorname{Ind}(U,L(j))$. Thus the target is its unique simple head. For $j=i$ there can also be shifts of $\operatorname{Ind}(L(i),U)$, but these have no nonzero map to the extracted target of first tail zero, by adjunction; the same unique-head conclusion follows. If $c_i(f_iM)=c+1$, step 2.1 instead gives $e_i^Lf_iM=M$ and therefore extraction yields $U$. For $j
e i$, $\epsilon_j(U)=\epsilon_j(M)$ because first-$i$ lowering preserves the right $j$-tail (step 2.1). The preceding lowering compatibility and partial inverses then give extraction compatibility with $e_j$ whenever $e_jM
e0$; when $e_jM=0$, the equality of tails makes $e_jU=0$ too.

We record the two containing-weight annihilation tests, with their proofs. If $A$ survives and $k=v_i^\lambda(A)$, then the quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(A,L_{k+1})$ is zero: its only simple head is the killed $f_i^{k+1}A$, while any nonzero finite quotient has a simple head. Appending any further block preserves zero, since a cyclotomic relation on an initial block is also a relation on the larger initial block. Consequently $\operatorname{Ind}(A,B)$ has zero quotient if $c_i(B)>k$, by the surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(L_{c_i(B)},(e_i^L)^{c_i(B)}B)\to B$. Conversely suppose $\epsilon_i(A)=\epsilon_j(A)=0$, $B$ has weight $ci+dj$, and $\operatorname{Ind}(A,B)\to T$ is surjective and simple. If $b=c_i(B)\le k$, write $C=(e_i^L)^bB$ and induce $A,L_b,C$. Its map to $T$ factors through $f_i^bA,C$: all other constituents $U$ of $\operatorname{Ind}(A,L_b)$ have $\epsilon_i(U)<b$. The defining corner of $T$ with an initial block of weight $\operatorname{wt}_{\rm root}(A)$ followed by a suffix of colours $i,j$ and beginning with $i^b$ is nonzero by adjunction. Every word in any such $U$ has a non-$i,j$ letter after the original $A$-block length: otherwise its last $A$-letter, necessarily different from $i,j$, would already lie in that initial block and all $b$ added $i$'s would be a tail, contradicting $\epsilon_i(U)<b$. Shuffling with $C$ preserves that non-$i,j$ letter in the suffix, so this corner vanishes on $\operatorname{Ind}(U,C)$. Thus no such factor maps onto $T$, proving the factorisation. The shuffle bound gives $c_i(T)\le c_i(f_i^bA)+c_i(C)\le\lambda_i$. Taking $\lambda_j$ larger than the total root-height of the finitely many modules being considered makes the $j$ inequality automatic; other first tails of $T$ are at most those of $A$. Hence this converse guarantees survival. In these comparisons we may enlarge every label except $\lambda_i$ to cover the fixed non-$i$ content of all the $i$-strings, so no assertion of a converse for a small $\lambda_j$ is needed.

First calculate the containing-length change in rank two. Any simple $N$ of weight $ci+dj$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$ is a quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(L(i^{b_1}j),\ldots,L(i^{b_r}j))$ with $0\le b_s\le a$: strip one right $j$, then its maximal $i$-tail, and repeat. A positive-height $N$ has a right $j$ since its right $i$ is zero; the factors of $\operatorname{Ind}(L_b,L(j))$ are classified by step 3.1, so tail zero forces $b\le a$ and the unique factor $L(i^bj)$. This justifies each factor selection by step 1.1 and decreases height, so the process terminates. For arbitrary $M$, put $m=\epsilon_i(M)$ and strip that tail to obtain such an $N$. The simple $f_jM$ is a quotient induced from $N$ and a factor $U$ of $\operatorname{Ind}(L_m,L(j))$. Step 1.1 determines its tail $\gamma=\epsilon_i(U)$; by step 3.1 it equals $m-a+n$ for some $0\le n\le a$ and $ f_i^aU=\operatorname{Ind}(D_n,L_m)$. This holds also for $m<a$, where $U=L(i^{a-n}ji^{m-a+n})$ and $m-a+n\ge0$.

For any simple $B$, every simple quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(B,D_n)$ has right tail $\epsilon_i(B)+n$: strip the right tail $L_{\epsilon_i(B)}$ of $B$, commute it past $D_n$ by step 3.1, and split $D_n$ as the head of $L(i^{a-n}j),L_n$. The resulting surjection with terminal block $L_{\epsilon_i(B)+n}$ gives the lower bound by adjunction; the shuffle bound gives the upper bound. This also holds for a string of $D_n$ factors by iteration. Let $d_s=a-b_s$ and $D=\sum_s d_s$. For $m+h\ge D$, the surjection from the factors in step 4.2 to $f_i^hM$ can be rewritten as a surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(D_{d_1},\ldots,D_{d_r},L_{m+h-D})\to f_i^hM$. To verify it, start at the rightmost $L(i^{b_r}j)$: the unique constituent of $\operatorname{Ind}(L(i^{b_r}j),L_{m+h})$ with tail $m+h$ is $\operatorname{Ind}(D_{d_r},L_{m+h-d_r})$ by step 3.1. Every other constituent has smaller tail and cannot map to the target through the preceding tail-zero factors by step 1.1. Commute this $D_{d_r}$ past the remaining pure-colour block using step 3.1 and repeat with $r-1,\ldots,1$. Each suffix of the $d_s$ has sum at most $D$, so all consumed block lengths are nonnegative. If a simple $Q$ is a quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(D_{n_1},\ldots,D_{n_r},L_g)$, its right and first tails are exactly $g+\sum_s n_s$ and $g+\sum_s(a-n_s)$. Indeed commute $L_g$ past each $D_{n_s}$, split $D_{n_s}$ as the head of $L(i^{a-n_s}j),L_{n_s}$, and move its $L_{n_s}$ to the right; adjunction gives the lower right-tail bound, the shuffle bound the matching upper bound. Repeat with the first-end split to obtain the first-tail bound. Therefore, with $C=m-ar+2\sum_s b_s$, we have $c_i(f_i^hM)=h+C$ for $h$ sufficiently large. For $f_i^hf_jM$ first absorb $a$ pure strands into $U$ using step 4.2 and the factorisation of step 1.1, and perform the same replacements on the preceding factors. For $h\ge a+D$ this gives a quotient of $\operatorname{Ind}(D_{d_1},\ldots,D_{d_r},D_n,L_{m+h-a-D})$, whose first tail is $h+C-n$. Choose $h$ still larger so both these tails are nonnegative and take the containing $i$ label to be $\omega_i=h+C$, with other labels large. The next first tail of $M$ is $\omega_i+1$, whereas $f_jM$ survives exactly $h+n$ steps. Thus $v_i^\omega(f_jM)-v_i^\omega(M)=n$; label independence in step 3.2 gives for every quotient containing both $ v_i^\lambda(f_jM)-v_i^\lambda(M)=n=\epsilon_i(f_jM)-\epsilon_i(M)+a$. This is the rank-two containing-length calculation, with an actual finite saturation threshold.

Reduce an arbitrary $M$ and $f_jM$ to that calculation. First strip the right $i$-tail of $M$, then alternately strip maximal right $j$- and $i$-tails until the remaining simple $A$ has $\epsilon_i(A)=\epsilon_j(A)=0$; each nonzero stripping decreases root-height. Group the removed blocks into a simple rank-two factor $B_0$ with a surjection $\operatorname{Ind}(A,B_0)\to e_i^{\epsilon_i(M)}M$, by step 1.1. Append the removed $i$-tail and apply the factorisation of step 1.1 to get $\operatorname{Ind}(A,B)\to M$ with $B=f_i^{\epsilon_i(M)}B_0$. For both $l=i,j$, the corner lower bound and shuffle upper bound give $\epsilon_l(B)=\epsilon_l(M)$. Appending $j$ and applying step 1.1 with colour $j$ gives $\operatorname{Ind}(A,f_jB)\to f_jM$, also with $\epsilon_i(f_jB)=\epsilon_i(f_jM)$. The same factorisation gives $\operatorname{Ind}(A,f_i^hB)\to f_i^hM$ and $\operatorname{Ind}(A,f_i^{h'}f_jB)\to f_i^{h'}f_jM$ for all $h,h'$. Choose containing labels $\omega$ for these initial modules with all non-$i$ labels large, and set $h=v_i^\omega(M)$, $h'=v_i^\omega(f_jM)$ and $k=v_i^\omega(A)$. The two annihilation tests in step 4.1 imply $c_i(f_i^hB)\le k<c_i(f_i^{h+1}B)$ and $c_i(f_i^{h'}f_jB)\le k<c_i(f_i^{h'+1}f_jB)$. Step 2.1 makes the inequalities equalities at the surviving endpoints and gives zero jump there. Step 3.2, applied to $B$ and $f_jB$, now gives $v_i^\omega(B)=h+\omega_i-k$ and $v_i^\omega(f_jB)=h'+\omega_i-k$. Their difference equals $h'-h$; step 5.1 evaluates it as $\epsilon_i(f_jM)-\epsilon_i(M)+a$. Label independence in step 3.2 transfers this to any quotient containing $M,f_jM$.

The initial value is now fixed, not inferred from a decrement recurrence. On the vacuum, $f_i^n\mathbf1=L_n$ has $c_i=n$, so its containing length is exactly $\lambda_i$ by [F1]. Every nonvacuum simple has some positive right tail (choose the last letter of any nonzero word corner), so write $M=f_jN$ with $N=e_jM$ of lower height. Both survive whenever $M$ survives by [F1]. If $j=i$, surviving length decreases by one, right tail increases by one and $\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$ increases by two. If $j\ne i$, step 6.1 gives the change in surviving length as $\epsilon_i(M)-\epsilon_i(N)-a_{ij}$. Induction on height from the vacuum therefore yields $ v_i^\lambda(M)=\lambda_i+\epsilon_i(M)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$. Combining this with the independently proved formula in step 3.2 gives $J_i(M)=\epsilon_i(M)+c_i(M)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$. In particular the initial zero-jump test is precisely $\epsilon_i(M)+c_i(M)=\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$; its value follows from the rank-two/annihilation calculation and the vacuum base, rather than the recurrence alone. The formula is symmetric in the two ends, so the corresponding first-end jump and its decrement formula also hold.

Define the elementary crystal $B_i$ by $\operatorname{wt}(b_i(n))=n\alpha_i$, $\epsilon_i(b_i(n))=-n$, $\phi_i(b_i(n))=n$, $e_ib_i(n)=b_i(n+1)$, $f_ib_i(n)=b_i(n-1)$; other-colour epsilon and phi are $-\infty$ and other-colour operators zero. On a tensor $X\otimes Y$, epsilon is $\max(\epsilon_l(X),\epsilon_l(Y)-\langle h_l,\operatorname{wt}(X)\rangle)$; $e_l$ acts on $X$ iff $\phi_l(X)\ge\epsilon_l(Y)$ and $f_l$ acts on $X$ iff $\phi_l(X)>\epsilon_l(Y)$, otherwise on $Y$. To check the $i$-data and both branches set $s=J_i(U)=\epsilon_i(U)+\langle h_i,\operatorname{wt}(U)\rangle\ge0$. Along the first-$i$ string from $U$, the symmetric jump recurrence and step 2.1 give $\epsilon_i(M)=\epsilon_i(U)+\max(0,c-s)$. This is exactly $\max(\epsilon_i(U),c-\langle h_i,\operatorname{wt}(U)\rangle)$, the tensor epsilon. Weight is also preserved since $\operatorname{wt}(U)=\operatorname{wt}(M)+c\alpha_i$. For lowering, if $s>c$ then $J_i(M)=s-c>0$, $c_i(f_iM)=c$, and step 3.3 gives extracted factor $f_iU$; if $s\le c$ then $J_i(M)=0$, $c_i(f_iM)=c+1$ and its extracted factor is $U$. These are precisely the strict $f_i$ branches. For raising, if $s<c$ then the predecessor $(f_i^L)^{c-1}U$ has zero jump, so $e_iM=e_i^LM$, first tail $c-1$ and extracted factor $U$. If $s\ge c>0$, that predecessor has positive jump; a zero jump at $e_iM$ would force $e_iM=e_i^LM$ by step 2.1 and contradict that positive jump. Hence $c_i(e_iM)=c$ and step 3.3 applied to $e_iM$ gives extracted factor $e_iU$. When $c=0$ the same first branch holds directly. If $e_iM=0$, the epsilon formula forces $e_iU=0$ and $s\ge c$, so the tensor operator is also zero. Thus both raising branches, including equality and zero cases, agree. For $j\ne i$, step 3.3 gives the epsilon equality and both operator compatibilities; phi equality follows from epsilon and weight. Finally $U,c$ recover $M=(f_i^L)^cU$, giving injectivity. Every nonvacuum has a nonzero word corner and therefore positive first tail at its first letter, while right-tail stripping decreases height to the unique vacuum and its partial inverse recovers every lowering word. All generic $f_i$ are nonzero by [F1].

Step 7.1 proves the actual surviving right lowering length in every containing first-strand quotient, including zero length and the vacuum. The linear divided restriction Serre relation is the Hom-dual of the projective Serre identity used in step 3.1; it is a statement about the exact linear $G_0$ operators, and makes no linear Serre assertion about the simple-socle operators. All containing labels and support reductions used [F2], so no new original-weight-lattice hypothesis has been imposed. Steps 2.1, 3.2 and 7.1 give every jump assertion, and step 8.1 gives strict injective elementary embeddings and lowering generation, completing the stated claims.

citations.quote:
Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], and let
$E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]. For every $i\in I$
and $\beta\in Q_+$:

(a) the bimodule $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)$ is a projective right
$R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module, and $e(\beta,i)R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ is a
projective left $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module;

(b) consequently $E^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_i$ are exact and send finitely
generated graded projectives to finitely generated graded projectives;
moreover $F^\Lambda_i$ preserves all projectives and $E^\Lambda_i$ preserves
finitely generated ones;

(c) there is a functorial exact sequence in
$\mathrm{Mod}(R(\beta+\alpha_i))$
$$0\longrightarrow q^{(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)}\bar F_iM\longrightarrow F_iM\longrightarrow F^\Lambda_iM\longrightarrow 0,\qquad M\in\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta)),$$
where $F_i$ is the right-append and $\bar F_i$ the left-append generic
induction of
[[lem-generic-klr-induction-and-restriction-mixed-relations]], regarded on
$R^\Lambda$-modules through the quotient, and the exponent is the Cartan
pairing $(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)=2(\alpha_i\mid\Lambda)
-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] records the
normalization of the powers of $q$).

Let $R=\bigoplus_\beta R(\beta)$ be a KLR algebra on a symmetrizable Cartan datum
with no imaginary simple roots
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]) and let
$E_i$ denote restriction $e(\beta,i)(-)$ and $F_i$, $\bar F_i$ the right-append
and left-append inductions of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]
(so that $\bar F_i(M)=R(\beta+\alpha_i)e(i,\beta)\otimes_{R(\beta)}M$ with
$e(i,\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(i\ast\nu)$). Let $t_i$ be an indeterminate of
degree $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2d_i$. Then:

(a) for $i\ne j$ there are natural isomorphisms
$E_iF_j\cong q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_j)}F_jE_i$ and
$\bar F_jE_i\cong E_i\bar F_j$;

(b) for $i=j$ there is a natural isomorphism
$E_iF_i\cong q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)}F_iE_i\oplus(\mathrm{Id}\otimes_kk[t_i])$,
where $(\mathrm{Id}\otimes_kk[t_i])(M)=M\otimes_kk[t_i]$ with $t_i$ homogeneous
of degree $2d_i$;

(c) the opposite-end corner comparison gives a functorial exact sequence in
$\mathrm{Mod}(R(\beta))$
$$0\longrightarrow \bar F_iE_iM\longrightarrow E_i\bar F_iM\longrightarrow q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)}M\otimes_kk[t_i]\longrightarrow 0,$$
where $\otimes_kk[t_i]$ is understood in the graded sense. For $n\ge1$, the underlying uncolored bimodules have the exact sequence
$0\to R(n)\otimes_{R_1(n-1)}R_1(n)\to R(n+1)\to R(n)\otimes_kk^I[t]\to0$,
where $k^I=\bigoplus_{j\in I}k\epsilon_j$ retains the transferred strand color,
and the right $R(n)$ action is through the shift embedding $\xi_n$.
The quotient grading is the degree of the full transfer word on each labeled
corner; its fixed-color $i$ corner is the shifted polynomial term of (c). All shifts are computed in the fixed grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]; the functors are exact
([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]]).

Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)-(Q4) for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree
$\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the
resulting ordinary quotient. Then: every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic
annihilator in each fixed block; every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over
$k$; and, for fixed $\beta$ and $i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all
sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In
the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is
nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded
functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are
ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

**Ground ring and graded algebras.** Fix a commutative ring $k$. A **graded
$k$-algebra** is a $k$-algebra $A$ in the sense of
[[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]], together with a direct sum
decomposition of $k$-modules

$$A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbb Z}A_i$$

such that $A_iA_j\subseteq A_{i+j}$ for all $i,j\in\mathbb Z$ and
$1_A\in A_0$. It is **unital and associative** when its underlying ring is;
every graded algebra on this page is unital and associative. Since
$\eta_A(r)=r\,1_A$ and $A_0$ is a $k$-submodule containing $1_A$, the structure
map has image in $A_0$, so each $A_i$ is a $k$-submodule and the scalars act
centrally on $A$.

**Graded modules and bimodules.** A **graded left $A$-module** is a left
$A$-module $M$ with a decomposition $M=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}M_d$ of
$k$-modules such that

$$A_iM_d\subseteq M_{i+d}\qquad\text{for all }i,d\in\mathbb Z .$$

A **graded right $A$-module** is a right $A$-module with a decomposition
$M=\bigoplus_dM_d$ such that $M_dA_i\subseteq M_{d+i}$ for all $i,d$. A
**graded $(B,A)$-bimodule** is a $(B,A)$-bimodule ([[def-bimodule]]) that is
graded as a $k$-module and homogeneous under both actions, the two actions
continuing to commute. Both induced $k$-actions must agree with the given
$k$-module structure: $\eta_B(t)m=tm=m\eta_A(t)$ for $t\in k$ and $m\in M$. Elements of $M_d$ are **homogeneous of degree $d$**, and
the decomposition expresses every $m\in M$ uniquely as a finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components.

**Degree-zero maps.** A map $f:M\to N$ of graded left $A$-modules is
**degree-zero**, or a **graded map**, when it is $A$-linear and
$f(M_d)\subseteq N_d$ for every $d$. The category $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$
has the graded left $A$-modules as objects and the degree-zero maps as
morphisms, with composition of maps. Every $M$ is an object of
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ by its own grading, and $A$ is a graded
$(A,A)$-bimodule under left and right multiplication.

**Graded submodules.** A **graded submodule** of a graded left $A$-module $M$ is
a submodule $S\le M$ with $S=\bigoplus_{d\in\mathbb Z}(S\cap M_d)$. Such an $S$
is itself a graded left $A$-module with homogeneous pieces
$S_d:=S\cap M_d$, because $A_iS_d\subseteq A_iM_d\cap S\subseteq M_{i+d}\cap S=S_{i+d}$;
equivalently, $S$ is generated by its homogeneous elements. In particular a
graded submodule is determined by its homogeneous pieces: if
$S=\bigoplus_dS_d$ and $T=\bigoplus_dT_d$ are graded submodules with $S_d=T_d$
for every $d$, then $S=T$.

**Internal shift.** For $r\in\mathbb Z$ and a graded module $M$, the
**internal shift** $M\{r\}$ is the module with

$$(M\{r\})_d:=M_{d-r}\qquad(d\in\mathbb Z),$$

carrying the same scalar action as $M$. Its components are additive subgroups
of $M$ whose sum is direct, so $M\{r\}$ is a $k$-module; and $M\{r\}$ is
graded because

$$A_i(M\{r\})_d=A_iM_{d-r}\subseteq M_{i+d-r}=(M\{r\})_{i+d}$$

for all $i,d$. For a graded bimodule both actions are unchanged, remain
homogeneous and still commute, so $M\{r\}$ is again a graded bimodule. The
shift is invertible: $(M\{r\})\{-r\}=M$, and $M\{0\}=M$. For a graded algebra
$A$, the shifts $A\{r\}$ of the regular bimodule are the modules denoted
$A\{r\}$ elsewhere on this page.

**Dictionary with the published twist.** In the published nonnegative
commutative convention ([[def-graded-ring-and-graded-module]]) the twist $M(a)$
is the graded module with $M(a)_d=M_{d+a}$ for every integer $a$. Substituting
$a=-r$ gives

$$(M\{r\})_d=M_{d-r}=M(-r)_d ,$$

so $M\{r\}=M(-r)$ as graded modules: the internal shift **reverses** the sign of
the published twist parameter. For $r=0$ both conventions agree with $M$.

**No super signs.** The internal degree is a genuine $\mathbb Z$-grading, not a
$\mathbb Z/2$-parity. No sign is inserted into the multiplication, the scalar
action or a degree-zero map merely because elements have nonzero degree; the
balancing relation of the tensor product below is likewise signed by nothing.
These are the unsigned associative conventions for this page; no differential
or signed symmetry on tensor products is part of this definition. They do not
exclude Koszul sign conventions in other categories of graded objects.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

derivations.claim: The comparison square. Write $n=|\beta|$, $s=(\alpha_i\mid2\Lambda-\beta)$, $\kappa=-\tau$, and use $K_0,K_1,P,Q$ from the proved comparison in [F1]. Put $C_0=e(\beta,i)K_0$ and $C_1=e(\beta,i)K_1$. If $\delta=\beta-\alpha_i\in Q_+$ put $D_0=R(\beta)e(\delta,i)\otimes_{R(\delta)}e(\delta,i)A$ and $D_1=R(\beta)e(i,\delta)\otimes_{R(\delta)}e(\delta,i)A$; otherwise both are zero. Restricting the comparison at $\beta$ and applying the comparison at $\delta$ to $E_iA$ give exact rows $0\to q^sD_1\xrightarrow{P'}q_i^{-2}D_0\to q_i^{-2}F_i^\Lambda E_i^\Lambda A\to0$ and $0\to q^sC_1\xrightarrow{P}C_0\to E_i^\Lambda F_i^\Lambda A\to0$. The vertical maps are $U:D_1\to C_1$, $x\otimes y\mapsto x\xi_n(y)$, and $T:D_0\to C_0$, $x\otimes y\mapsto x\kappa_ny$, with the indicated shifts. Here $P'$ multiplies the first factor by $a(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_{n-1}$; right bilinearity of $P$ gives $PU=TP'$ on elementary tensors, both represented by $xa(x_1)\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_ny$. The generic PBW maps of [F1] make $U,T$ injective, with cokernels $q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)}A[t]$ and $A[t]$ respectively, retaining the transferred color $i$. The induced coefficient map $\mathcal A:q_i^{2h}A[t]\to A[t]$ is therefore defined by $\mathcal A B=CP$, where $B$ takes the full-transfer coefficient in $C_1$ and $C$ projects $C_0=T(D_0)\oplus A[t]$ onto its polynomial summand. The square consists of $(R(\beta),A)$-bimodule maps; its coefficient map and snake sequence are $A$-bimodule maps. Only $B,P$ commute with their endpoint-dot actions, and no $A[t]$-linearity of $\mathcal A$ is asserted. The snake lemma gives $0\to\ker\mathcal A\to q_i^{-2}F_i^\Lambda E_i^\Lambda A\to E_i^\Lambda F_i^\Lambda A\to\operatorname{coker}\mathcal A\to0$.

Applying $\mathcal AB=CP$ to $Q(t^k)$ and using $PQ=Z$ proves $\mathcal A(t^kS)=\gamma^{-1}t^kW$ for every $k\ge0$.

The coefficient recurrence and division. Let $u_k=e(\beta,i)\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_1x_1^ke(i,\beta)\in C_1$. It satisfies $B(u_k)=t^k$. In the same-end direct sum write $P(u_k)=T(\psi_k)+\phi_k$, with $\psi_k\in D_0$ and $\phi_k=\mathcal A(t^k)\in A[t]$. Since $P(u_{k+1})=P(u_k)x_{n+1}$ and $T(z)x_{n+1}=T(z(x_n\otimes1))+E(z)$, where $E(x\otimes y)=xy\in A$, comparison of the summands gives $\psi_{k+1}=\psi_k(x_n\otimes1)$ and $\phi_{k+1}=t\phi_k+E(\psi_k)$. These identities use the source $\kappa$ mixed relation and the actual multiplication counit. In particular $\mathcal A(at)-\mathcal A(a)t\in A$ for all $a\in A[t]$. Induction on the degree of $f$, using $\mathcal A(atg)-\mathcal A(a)tg=[\mathcal A(atg)-\mathcal A(at)g]+[\mathcal A(at)-\mathcal A(a)t]g$, gives $\deg_t(\mathcal A(af)-\mathcal A(a)f)<\deg_t f$. With $f=S$ and step 2.1, this says $t^kW=(\gamma\phi_k)S+r_k$, $\deg_t r_k<2p$. Thus $\gamma\phi_k$ is exactly the monic-division quotient, zero when $h+k<0$ and monic of degree $h+k$ otherwise.

The positive branch. If $h\ge0$, the values $\gamma\phi_k$ have distinct unit leading degrees $h+k$. Finite triangular elimination over $A$ makes $\mathcal A$ injective and identifies its cokernel with $\bigoplus_{k=0}^{h-1}At^k$. The inclusion of these polynomial classes in $C_0$, followed by $C_0\to E_i^\Lambda F_i^\Lambda A$, is a bimodule section of the last snake map. It is the ordinary adjunction unit followed by $k$ endpoint dots, of degree $2d_ik$. Hence $E_i^\Lambda F_i^\Lambda A\cong q_i^{-2}F_i^\Lambda E_i^\Lambda A\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{h-1}A\{2d_ik\}$. At $h=0$ the sum is empty.

The negative branch. If $h=-r\le0$, division makes $\mathcal A$ surjective with kernel $q_i^{-2r}\bigoplus_{j=0}^{r-1}At^j$. Its snake inclusion sends $t^j$ to the image of $\psi_j$ in $q_i^{-2}F_i^\Lambda E_i^\Lambda A$. The multiplication counit and its dotted versions descend from $D_0$ to this quotient. On the included kernel, their coefficient matrix is $E(\psi_{j+k})$ for $0\le j,k<r$. Step 3.1 gives $E(\psi_m)=0$ for $m<r-1$ and $E(\psi_{r-1})=\gamma^{-1}$, since $\phi_m=0$ for $m<r$ and $\phi_r=\gamma^{-1}$. Reversing column order therefore makes this matrix triangular with invertible scalar diagonal. Its finite recursive inverse, consisting of bimodule maps, supplies a retraction of the snake inclusion and splits the sequence. The dotted counit at index $k$ has target shift $-2d_i(k+1)$ after the $q_i^{-2}$ shift on $D_0$, so $q_i^{-2}F_i^\Lambda E_i^\Lambda A\cong E_i^\Lambda F_i^\Lambda A\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{r-1}A\{-2d_i(k+1)\}$. At $r=0$ this agrees with step 4.1. At the vacuum the direct calculation is $E_i^\Lambda F_i^\Lambda k=k[t]/t^{\lambda_i}$ and $F_i^\Lambda E_i^\Lambda k=0$; it gives the positive branch without any negative-height algebra.

Unequal-color descent and functoriality. For $i\ne j$ let $S_n=R(n+1)$, $L=R(n)$ on the first $n$ positions, $L[t]=R(n,1)$, $w=\kappa_1\cdots\kappa_n$ and $w'=\kappa_n\cdots\kappa_1$. Expanding the first-strand cyclotomic ideal by the right cosets and then the left cosets of [F1] gives $S_na(x_1)S_n=S_na(x_1)L+La(x_1)S_n+L[t]w'a(x_1)wL[t]$: all partial transfer words lie in the first two summands, and only the full transfer remains. In its $(i,j)$ last-color corner the last summand is zero, because $w'$ transfers its top color to the first position and $w$ transfers its bottom color there, giving $e(i,n)a(x_1)e(j,n)=0$. Thus the corner ideal is exactly the sum of the source and target induced cyclotomic ideals. Quotienting the generic same-end corner isomorphism gives $E_i^\Lambda F_j^\Lambda\cong q^{-b_{ij}}F_j^\Lambda E_i^\Lambda$. For equal colors, tensor the split bimodule isomorphisms of steps 4.1 and 5.1 with any graded $A$-module: split bimodule maps remain inverse under tensoring. They give precisely (a) and (b), naturally, with the stated bimodule form on $A$. No flatness of a quotient or separability assumption is used.

Rebuilt the actual (R(beta),A) comparison square: defined D0,D1,C0,C1,P-prime, shifted multiplication U and same-end transfer T, and specified polynomial coefficient B/C and the induced A-bimodule snake map. Proved PQ=Z from QP, P injectivity and monic torsion-freeness; defined gamma and central monic S/W; leading transfer coefficient gives A(t^kS)=gamma^-1 t^kW. The displayed psi/phi decomposition and source-kappa dot identity give the recurrence and division. Explicit unit columns split h>=0; the E(psi_(j+k)) matrix has invertible anti-diagonal and dotted counits split h<=0. Both h=0 branches have empty sums; beta=0 is directly k[t]/t^lambda_i. Bimodule splitting gives natural functor isomorphisms for all inputs. No diagram/cap-off premise is used. Expanded the cyclotomic ideal with both PBW coset systems to S a L + L a S + L[t] w-prime a w L[t]. citations.quote:
Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with real simple roots (so $a_{ii}=2$ for
every color $i$), a field $k$ placed in degree zero, and weighted-homogeneous
KLR polynomials $Q_{jk}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4) as in
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]; write
$b_{jk}=d_j a_{jk}=b_{kj}$. Fix a color $i$. The **minimal-parabolic KLR
diagram proof category** $\mathcal P_i$ is the additive graded $k$-linear
category of weighted oriented diagrams described by the generators, objects
and equations below.

**Generators and composition.** The objects are the weights
$\mu\in P$. The generating $1$-morphisms are the downward generators
$G_j:\mu\to\mu-\alpha_j$, one for every color $j$, and the single upward
generator $H_i:\mu\to\mu+\alpha_i$. Horizontal composition reads chronological
negative words from the vacuum outward. Take additive sums of objects and
grading shifts, and use idempotent completion when speaking of word
projectives. The generator $H_i$ denotes **normalized projective
restriction**: in the polynomial flag realization at input weight $h=\langle
h_i,\mu\rangle$ it is basic reversed flag restriction shifted by
$-d_i(1+h)$; it is distinct from unshifted basic restriction.

**Degrees and the native crossing.** Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward
crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$, matching the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. The native crossing is
$\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference
$(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put
$\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$.
Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source
numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR
relations of the cited Definition.

**Adjunctions and the rank-one matrix.** At input $i$-weight $h$, the first
unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and the second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree
$d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and the second unit
$1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with
their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$
prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix
$$H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\};$$
for $h<0$ prescribe
$$G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}.$$
The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap
transfer, and the identity columns and rows are the indicated dotted
units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse
equations; the dotted dual rows and columns are the finite triangular
coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing
block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$,
if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, then $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and
$p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion and projection with product
$1_{H_iG_i}$.

**Bubble series and slides.** The normalized far-left bubble series
$A_\mu(t),\mathsf H_\mu(t)$ have constant coefficient $1$ and satisfy
$A_\mu(t)\mathsf H_\mu(t)=1$. Genuine negative-degree bubbles vanish. The $A$
coefficient with index $m$ is the clockwise bubble with $-h-1+m$ dots when
this count is nonnegative, extended by formal inverse coefficients otherwise;
its degree is $2d_im$. The other family has dot count $h-1+\ell$ and degree
$2d_i\ell$. Impose the finite-coefficient slides verified on the monic flag
model: adjoining an $i$ root $z$ divides $A$ by $(1-zt)^2$ and multiplies
$\mathsf H$ by that factor; adjoining a spectator root $y$ of color $j\ne i$
multiplies $A$ by
$q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$, where $t_{ij}$
is the nonzero extremal coefficient, and divides $\mathsf H$ by it. Every
reciprocal coefficient is defined by the finite recursion with constant
coefficient $1$.

**Cross-and-cap equations.** Impose the rank-one cross-and-cap equations: the
two oppositely oriented single-crossing curls are the signed sums of a dotted
uncrossed cap and an opposite bubble over indices $a+b=-1$; the two
opposite-crossing cancellations are the straight pair plus the dotted
cup--bubble--cap sums over $a+b+c=-1$, with the corresponding
opposite-orientation signs. A negative dot count on an open strand is zero.
These are the four source $\kappa$ equations, converted globally by
$\kappa=-\tau$. For $j\ne i$, the two sideways crossings, defined as the two
adjunction mates of the downward crossing, cancel in the two orders with the
nonzero scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$; scale the reverse mate by the
corresponding inverse to obtain the mixed isomorphism
$H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$, commuting with the $j$ dot.

**Status of the relations.** These equations are relations of this proof-tool
category. Their consistency and homogeneous realization are established by
the polynomial flag model
([[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]]),
rather than assumed for the actual cyclotomic induction/restriction action; no
claim about the latter is made here. This definition uses no choice: it is a
presentation by generators and homogeneous equations, and every sl(2) infinite
family appearing in the matrix and bubble clauses is a finite coefficient
recursion from a constant coefficient $1$.

Fix a color $i$ and the formal proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], on a symmetrizable real
Cartan datum with finite index set and arbitrary field $k$. Use the native KLR
parameters of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], degrees of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], the PBW convention of
[[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], and the nil-Hecke matrix/idempotent convention
of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Then the polynomial
flag construction described below realizes all the defining graded diagram
relations of that formal category, including its rank-one cross/cap,
bubble-slide/inversion and mixed-color cup/cap relations; it asserts a
representation of the formal proof category, not faithfulness or a cyclotomic
quotient identification.

**The model.** Choose a color order with $i$ last. For spectator alphabets
$Y_j$ of sizes $m_j$ ($j\ne i$) put $C=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}k[Y_j]^{S_{m_j}}$,
$r=m_i$, $A_{ij}=-a_{ij}$,
$t_{ij}=[u^{A_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$,
$q_{ij}=Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$, and choose a monic framing polynomial $a_i(u)$ of
degree $\lambda_i$; initially its coefficients have their universal homogeneous
degrees, so all formulas are graded, and the standard specialization is
$a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. Set
$$p_m(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}q_{ij}(u,y),\qquad N=\lambda_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j,\qquad h_m=N-2r,$$
and $c_r(u)=u^r-e_1u^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^re_r$. The vertex ring $L_m$ is the
monic factor ring for $p_m=c_rb_{N-r}$, equivalently $C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$ modulo
all coefficients beyond degree $N-r$ of the monic expansion $p_m/c_r$; it is
finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$ and is zero for $r>N$. Its $i$ flag is
$B_m=L_m[z]/b_{N-r}(z)$, free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over
$L_{m+i}$, with the target root alphabet obtained by adjoining $z$. The
underlying spectator flag is $C_m^j=L_m[y]$; its target action appends $y$ to
$Y_j$ and replaces $p_m$ by $p_mq_{ij}(u,y)$.

**The shifts and generators.** Every downward generator carries the ordered
shift $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$. Thus
$G_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the $B_m\{-2d_ir\}$ tensor functor; $G_j$ for
$j\ne i$ is the $C_m^j\{s_j(m)\}$ tensor functor. The basic reversed $i$ flag
is $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}=B_m\otimes_{L_{m+i}}-$ without a shift, whereas the
formal upward generator at INPUT vertex $m$ is
$H_i(m)=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(m)\{-d_i(1+h_m)\}$. These are distinct
conventions. The basic flags have degree-zero
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\{t_i(m)\}\dashv F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$, where
$t_i(m)=-2d_i(h_m-1)$. At vertex $m$ the formal first unit and second cap have
degree $d_i(1-h_m)$, and the formal first cap and second unit have degree
$d_i(1+h_m)$.

**The four maps and the Casimir.** All four maps are the explicit dual-basis
maps of the two monic coefficient forms on $B_m$: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}:B_m\to
L_m$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$;
$\tau_{\mathrm{new}}:B_m\to L_{m+i}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$.
The first cap is $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto\tau_{\mathrm{new}}(b_1b_2)$ and the
first cup is its dual-power-basis Casimir; the second cap and cup use
$\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$. For a monic polynomial $f$ their Casimir is the
polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the two-root quotient.

**Crossings, colors and bubbles.** Source crossings are
$\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for EVERY color pair. Source equal-color
operators are $(s-1)/(X-Y)$; source unequal operators are the switch/quotient
in the increasing-color direction and switch times $Q$ in the reverse
direction. Thus native operators are their negatives, and both actual crossing
degrees are $-b_{jk}$ with the ordered shifts above. On the $i,j$ pair the
successive underlying rings are
$D_1=L_m[y,z]/(b(z)q_{ij}(z,y))$ and $D_0=L_m[y,z]/b(z)$, with source maps
$\pi:D_1\to D_0$ and $f\mapsto Q_{ij}(z,y)f:D_0\to D_1$; their normalized
opposite-sideways composites have the scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$, and in the
NE/SW-$i$, NW/SE-$j$ source orientation the double-mate ratio is
$t_{ji}/t_{ij}$. Native minus signs leave the two-crossing scalars and the
ratio unchanged. The basic isomorphism $E_iG_j\cong(G_jE_i)\{-b_{ij}\}$ holds,
and the normalized formal $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$ is unshifted.

**Realized equations.** The canonical rank-one $\rho$ and its inverse, the
same-color cross/cap equations, the bubble series
$\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ and its reciprocal, and the finite-coefficient
bubble-slide identities are realized by the stated polynomial maps. In
particular the normalized positive $h$ identity columns have degrees
$d_i(1-h+2k)$ for $0\le k<h$, and the negative branch uses the inverse
crossing plus the dot/cap rows. All polynomial pairings and relations persist
after arbitrary monic coefficient specialization as UNGRADED identities; such
a specialization does not assert nilpotence, a homogeneous trace degree, or a
highest-weight $K_0$ claim. No geometry, characteristic restriction, or
one-dimensional-Hom hypothesis is imposed.

Fix a color $i$. In the formal graded minimal-parabolic proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], the reduced
perfect-matching diagrams, dot monomials on their open components, and
monomials in the independent far-left normalized $i$-bubble coefficients form
a basis of every morphism space. In particular, at all-downward boundaries of
weight difference $\beta$, the morphism space is the corresponding KLR PBW
corner tensored with the polynomial ring in one positive bubble family; the
opposite/fake family is its coefficientwise reciprocal. The graded polynomial
flag models of
[[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]],
with universal monic framing and arbitrarily large auxiliary framing at each
fixed physical source weight, are jointly faithful. The assertion is about this
formal proof category before cyclotomic quotient transfer.

Let $\Lambda$ be dominant, $\lambda_j=\langle h_j,\Lambda\rangle$, and let
$\mathcal P_i$ be [[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], with
its homogeneous polynomial realization and PBW/bubble normal form. Fix monic
$a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}+\sum_{r<\lambda_j}c_{j,r}u^r$; for the standard graded
cyclotomic quotient take $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$ as in
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]. More generally first take
universal graded coefficients of degree $2d_j(\lambda_j-r)$; arbitrary monic
specializations over the field are interpreted as ungraded.

In the representable category $\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)$, let $J$ be the ideal
generated by $1_{H_iv_\Lambda}$ and $a_j(x)1_{G_jv_\Lambda}$ for every $j$,
closed under arbitrary vertical pre/postcomposition and horizontal whiskering
by the allowed $1$-morphisms. For downward words $\mu,\nu$ of the same weight
$\beta$, include their ordinary KLR corner by the PBW/bubble normal form. Then
$$J\cap e(\nu)R(\beta)e(\mu)=e(\nu)I_a(\beta)e(\mu),\qquad I_a(\beta)=\sum_jR(\beta)a_j(x_1)e(j,\beta-\alpha_j)R(\beta).$$
The vacuum bubble specialization is forced by these generators:
$A_\Lambda(t)=1+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}t+\cdots+c_{i,0}t^{\lambda_i}$ and
$\mathsf H_\Lambda=A_\Lambda^{-1}$. Consequently the map from the ordinary
monic cyclotomic corner to the downward-word Hom corner of
$\mathcal P_i(\Lambda)/J$ is an isomorphism, with composition corresponding to
multiplication. This holds over every degree-zero field for the entire
admissible homogeneous $Q$ family, without finite-type or characteristic-zero
restrictions. Inhomogeneous monic specializations assert the ungraded corner
equality, not a graded quantum-action conclusion.

Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], and let
$E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]. For every $i\in I$
and $\beta\in Q_+$:

(a) the bimodule $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)e(\beta,i)$ is a projective right
$R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module, and $e(\beta,i)R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ is a
projective left $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-module;

(b) consequently $E^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_i$ are exact and send finitely
generated graded projectives to finitely generated graded projectives;
moreover $F^\Lambda_i$ preserves all projectives and $E^\Lambda_i$ preserves
finitely generated ones;

(c) there is a functorial exact sequence in
$\mathrm{Mod}(R(\beta+\alpha_i))$
$$0\longrightarrow q^{(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)}\bar F_iM\longrightarrow F_iM\longrightarrow F^\Lambda_iM\longrightarrow 0,\qquad M\in\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta)),$$
where $F_i$ is the right-append and $\bar F_i$ the left-append generic
induction of
[[lem-generic-klr-induction-and-restriction-mixed-relations]], regarded on
$R^\Lambda$-modules through the quotient, and the exponent is the Cartan
pairing $(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)=2(\alpha_i\mid\Lambda)
-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] records the
normalization of the powers of $q$).

Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], let
$E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]], and read the
composites $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i$ as
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$ via the weight bookkeeping
fixed there. Put $\lambda:=\Lambda-\beta$ and $q_i:=q^{d_i}$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

(a) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\ge0$, there is a natural isomorphism of
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{2k}\mathrm{Id}\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i.$$

(b) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\le0$, there is a natural isomorphism of
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{-\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{-2k-2}\mathrm{Id}.$$

Applied to the object $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ the same computation gives an
isomorphism of graded $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-bimodules obtained from
$F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ and
$E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ by the displayed summands
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]] for the shift
conventions).

Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)-(Q4) for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree
$\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the
resulting ordinary quotient. Then: every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic
annihilator in each fixed block; every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over
$k$; and, for fixed $\beta$ and $i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all
sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In
the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is
nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded
functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are
ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

derivations.claim: Conventions and degrees. Work throughout with $\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for every color pair: this is a graded algebra isomorphism preserving $Q$ and all first-strand monic ideals, since quadratic relations carry two signs, the braid defect carries three, and $\kappa_w=(-1)^{\ell(w)}\tau_w$. With $i$ last in a total color order, raw downward flags have shifts $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$, and a degree-$D$ raw map between word shifts $S,T$ has degree $D+T-S$. Hence a source increasing crossing $\pi$ of degree zero and its reverse multiplier $Q$ of degree $-2b_{jk}$ both have actual degree $-b_{jk}$, and basic $E_iG_j$ has the prescribed shifted commutator $-b_{ij}$. The formal $H_i=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\{-d_i(1+h_{\mathrm{input}})\}$ cancels the shift because $h$ increases by $-a_{ij}$ under $G_j$ and $s_j(m-e_i)=s_j(m)+b_{ij}$; it is the formal $H_i$, not the basic $E_i$, that commutes unshiftedly with the spectator flag.

The explicit units and counits. At a vertex with $r$ $i$-roots and total monic degree $N$ put $L=C[e_1,\dots,e_r]/(\text{factor coefficients above }N-r)$, $c_r=\prod(u-x_a)$, $p=a_i\prod_{j\ne i}Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $b=p/c_r$. The $i$-flag algebra is $B=L[z]/b(z)$, free over the old ring on the powers $0\le j<N-r$ and free over the target root-append ring on the powers $0\le j\le r$. The two coefficient traces $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$ and $\tau_{\mathrm{new}}$ extract the respective top powers of the monic remainders, and their Gram matrices in the power/complementary bases are triangular with diagonal $1$, so they have explicit dual bases without factorial denominators. Basic $F_i=B\{-2d_ir\}\otimes-$ and basic reverse $E_i=B\otimes-$ use $\tau_{\mathrm{new}}$ and its dual bases; the second adjunction $E_i\{t_i(\beta)\}\dashv F_i$ uses $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$ in the same way. Restricting the model equations of [F1] through the cap-off identification [F2] gives homogeneous units and counits with both triangle identities, hence $E_i\{t_i(\beta)\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$.

Crossing mates. The model's rank-one rho and cross-and-cap equations of [F1] identify the two adjunction mates of a crossing with the same normalizations used in the formal definition; on the $i,j$ pair the successive rings are $D_1=L_m[y,z]/(b(z)q_{ij}(z,y))$ and $D_0=L_m[y,z]/b(z)$, and the normalized opposite-sideways composites have scalars $t_{ij}$ and $t_{ji}$, with double right mate $(t_{ji}/t_{ij})p_\nu$ in the stated source orientation. Dots, idempotents and equal-color crossings have ratio $1$ by dot-cyclicity and the equal-color mixed relations. Reading these model identities through the cap-off isomorphism [F2] proves the stated mate identities in $R^\Lambda$, and the same transported identities hold verbatim after arbitrary monic specialization with shifts forgotten.

Conclusion. Steps 2.1 and 3.1 establish the graded biadjunction $E_i\{t_i(\beta)\}\dashv F_i\dashv E_i$ and the ordered crossing-mate identities with their exact scalars, using only the model-verified relations, the cap-off identification and the projective comparison of [F3]; no Frobenius, integral Grothendieck-module or crystal statement is used as a premise.

[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], let
$E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]], and read the

Let $R=\bigoplus_\beta R(\beta)$ be a KLR algebra on a symmetrizable Cartan datum
with no imaginary simple roots
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]) and let
$E_i$ denote restriction $e(\beta,i)(-)$ and $F_i$, $\bar F_i$ the right-append
and left-append inductions of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]
(so that $\bar F_i(M)=R(\beta+\alpha_i)e(i,\beta)\otimes_{R(\beta)}M$ with
$e(i,\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(i\ast\nu)$). Let $t_i$ be an indeterminate of
degree $(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)=2d_i$. Then:

(a) for $i\ne j$ there are natural isomorphisms
$E_iF_j\cong q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_j)}F_jE_i$ and
$\bar F_jE_i\cong E_i\bar F_j$;

(b) for $i=j$ there is a natural isomorphism
$E_iF_i\cong q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_i)}F_iE_i\oplus(\mathrm{Id}\otimes_kk[t_i])$,
where $(\mathrm{Id}\otimes_kk[t_i])(M)=M\otimes_kk[t_i]$ with $t_i$ homogeneous
of degree $2d_i$;

(c) the opposite-end corner comparison gives a functorial exact sequence in
$\mathrm{Mod}(R(\beta))$
$$0\longrightarrow \bar F_iE_iM\longrightarrow E_i\bar F_iM\longrightarrow q^{-(\alpha_i\mid\beta)}M\otimes_kk[t_i]\longrightarrow 0,$$
where $\otimes_kk[t_i]$ is understood in the graded sense. For $n\ge1$, the underlying uncolored bimodules have the exact sequence
$0\to R(n)\otimes_{R_1(n-1)}R_1(n)\to R(n+1)\to R(n)\otimes_kk^I[t]\to0$,
where $k^I=\bigoplus_{j\in I}k\epsilon_j$ retains the transferred strand color,
and the right $R(n)$ action is through the shift embedding $\xi_n$.
The quotient grading is the degree of the full transfer word on each labeled
corner; its fixed-color $i$ corner is the shifted polynomial term of (c). All shifts are computed in the fixed grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]; the functors are exact
([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]]).

[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], let
$E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of

(a) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\ge0$, there is a natural isomorphism of

$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{2k}\mathrm{Id}\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i.$$

$E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ by the displayed summands
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]] for the shift
conventions).

Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)-(Q4) for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree
$\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the
resulting ordinary quotient. Then: every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic
annihilator in each fixed block; every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over
$k$; and, for fixed $\beta$ and $i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all
sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In
the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is
nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded
functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are
ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

Let $V=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}V_\mu$ be a label-weight-graded $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector
space with toral operators $K_h$ ($h\in P^\vee$) acting on $V_\mu$ by
$q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}$, and operators $E_i,F_i$ of weights
$\alpha_i,-\alpha_i$ mapping $V_\mu$ to $V_{\mu+\alpha_i}$ and
$V_{\mu-\alpha_i}$. Assume the toral conjugation and mixed relations, and local
nilpotence of each $E_i$ and $F_i$; vectors have finite label support. Then
these operators uniquely define an integrable type-one
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure on $V$ for EVERY real symmetrizable Cartan
datum. Every vector has a finite rank-one $U_i$ orbit and the admissible
Kashiwara $i$-string decomposition applies. Finite weight spaces do not imply
finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ orbits; no such conclusion is asserted.

derivations.claim: The normalized operators. Projectivity of the cyclotomic bimodules supplies exact functors preserving finite projectives, so the displayed shifts define $A$-linear operators on the graded Grothendieck groups, where $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. The torus acts on the root component $\beta$ by $K_a=q^{\langle a,\Lambda-\beta\rangle}$, and each Grothendieck element has finite root support.

The mixed relation on $K_0$. Let $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$ at input root $\beta$. The $E_i$ in $E_iF_i$ has output root $\beta$, so its normalization contributes $q_i^{1-h}$. The $E_i$ in $F_iE_i$ has output root $\beta-\alpha_i$, whose coroot label is $h+2$, so its normalization contributes $q_i^{1-(h+2)}=q_i^{-1-h}$. Multiplying the positive basic commutator of [F1] by $q_i^{1-h}$ therefore turns its $q_i^{-2}F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ term into precisely the normalized $F_iE_i$, and its identity terms into $\sum_{k=0}^{h-1}q_i^{1-h+2k}=[h]_i$. For $h\le0$, the negative basic branch similarly gives $F_iE_i=E_iF_i+\sum_{k=0}^{-h-1}q_i^{-1-h-2k}\mathrm{Id}$, whose sum is $[-h]_i$, so the same signed relation follows. Thus $E_iF_i-F_iE_i=[h]_i\mathrm{Id}=(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ on root $\beta$, with $K_i=q_i^h$; the quantum integer is integral, so no division in the coefficient ring is needed.

The unequal-color relation and the module actions. Write $h_i(\beta)=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$ and $b_{ij}=d_i a_{ij}=(\alpha_i\mid\alpha_j)$ for $i\ne j$. At input root $\beta$, the normalization of $E_i$ in $E_iF_j$ is $q_i^{1-h_i(\beta+\alpha_j-\alpha_i)}$, whereas that in $F_jE_i$ is $q_i^{1-h_i(\beta-\alpha_i)}$. Since $h_i(\beta+\alpha_j-\alpha_i)=h_i(\beta-\alpha_i)-a_{ij}$, their ratio is $q_i^{a_{ij}}=q^{b_{ij}}$. This cancels the basic crossing factor $q^{-b_{ij}}$ in [F2], giving the normalized relation $E_iF_j=F_jE_i$. The canonical $G_0$-action has the same shifts and hence the same computations as $K_0$. For the KK $G_0$-action the shift is instead carried by $F$: its exponent on input root $\beta$ is $1-h_j(\beta)$, so the ratio between $E_iF_j$ and $F_jE_i$ is $q_j^{h_j(\beta-\alpha_i)-h_j(\beta)}=q_j^{a_{ji}}=q^{b_{ij}}$, again cancelling the basic factor. For the KK same-color relation, $E_iF_i$ has shift $q_i^{1-h}$ and $F_iE_i$ has shift $q_i^{-1-h}$, exactly as in step 2.1. Both module actions therefore satisfy the required mixed relations; restriction lowers root height and the weight labels give the toral conjugation relations.

Local nilpotence and integrability. By [F3], $R^\Lambda(\beta+n\alpha_i)=0$ for $n$ large, so the induction operator $F_i$ is locally nilpotent componentwise; restriction lowers height, so $E_i$ is locally nilpotent as well. The toral conjugation, mixed relations and local nilpotence are exactly the hypotheses of the abstract lemma [F3], which then proves both full symmetrizable Serre families and equips the scalar extension to $\mathbb Q(q)$ with the unique integrable type-one $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure. No finite-dimensionality of full weight spaces and no ungraded monic deformation is asserted; no cyclic input from vacuum generation or the integral highest-module identification is used.
