Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta\in Q_+$.
(i) Every finitely generated graded left $R(\beta)$-module has a decomposition into finitely many indecomposable graded modules, unique as a finite multiset of degree-zero graded isomorphism classes, including the actual shifts of their summands; in particular the category $\mathrm{GrMod}_0R(\beta)$ of finitely generated graded modules has the Krull-Schmidt property.
(ii) Every simple graded $R(\beta)$-module is finite-dimensional, killed by the augmentation ideal $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ of the CENTRAL color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$; up to isomorphism and shift there are finitely many, and each has a projective cover which is finitely generated.
(iii) The split Grothendieck group $K_0(R(\beta))$ of finite graded projective modules is a free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module: the classes of the indecomposable finitely generated graded projectives, modulo grading shifts, form a basis with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$; equivalently the classes of all finitely generated indecomposable graded projectives form a shift-orbit basis. Similarly $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of simple modules, and the Hom pairing of projective covers and simples has diagonal entries $\dim_k\operatorname{End}^0(S_b)$, with the selected cover/simple shifts, under the Hom convention of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]].

Let $R$ be any graded KLR datum in this page over any field $k$. For a finite-dimensional graded module $M$ of weight $\beta$ set $\epsilon_i(M)=\max\{r:e(\beta-r\alpha_i,r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$. If $S$ is simple and $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, there is a simple graded $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)$-module $N$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$ such that $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$, where $L(i^r)$ is the unique nil-Hecke simple up to shift. Conversely, for any such $N$, $\mathrm{Ind}(N\boxtimes L(i^r))$ has a unique simple graded head $S$, appearing once as a composition factor, with $\epsilon_i(S)=r$ and $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$; every other composition factor has smaller $i$-tail. The graded simples of every $R(\beta)$ remain simple without grading and are absolutely simple; all ordinary endomorphisms are $k$ and nonzero homogeneous endomorphisms have degree $0$. The classes of normalized simples and their projective covers are therefore unscaled dual shift-orbit bases for the projective/simple Hom pairing. For each $\beta$ there is a finite family of ordered divided-power words $Y_b$ whose normalized projective classes pair triangularly with the simple classes, with diagonal entries $1$ after choosing the simple grading shifts. Thus the selected $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$; arbitrary divided words span, but need not be a basis. The identical statements hold for maximal FIRST-color blocks, with $\epsilon_i^L(M)=\max\{r:e(r\alpha_i,\beta-r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$, restriction $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}$ and induction $\mathrm{Ind}(L(i^r)\boxtimes N)$.

For any graded KLR datum in this page and any field $k$, each finite-dimensional graded simple shift orbit has a unique representative $S_b$ self-dual for $D(M)_d=\operatorname{Hom}_k(M_{-d},k)$ with action $(af)(m)=f(\psi(a)m)$. Its projective cover $P_b$, normalized by $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P_b,S_b)=k$, satisfies $P_b^\#=P_b$ for $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_R(P,R)^\psi$. These are unique normalizations. Induction of two self-dual finite projectives is self-dual. If $\epsilon_i^L(S_b)=r>0$ and $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}S_b=L(i^r)\boxtimes S_a$ with $\epsilon_i^L(S_a)=0$, normalized as above, then
$$[P_{i,r}][P_a]=[P_b]+\sum_{\epsilon_i^L(S_c)>r}m_c(q)[P_c],$$
with $m_c\in\mathbb{N}[q,q^{-1}]$ each invariant under $q\mapsto q^{-1}$. Under $\gamma$ the integral LEFT divided-string ideal $I_{(i,\ge n)}=\sum_{r\ge n}F_i^{(r)}U_A^-$ is the $A$-span of $[P_b]$ with $\epsilon_i^L(S_b)\ge n$. Consequently, if the normalized projective classes are known to be a SIGNED lower-global set, this leading coefficient $1$ identifies them with the POSITIVE lower-global set using the general adapted right-string recursion; no finite-ADE canonical-comparison theorem is needed. For the conclusions compared with the quantum half and the conditional lower-global/LEFT-string recursion, carry the inherited Axiom of Choice of those quantum suppliers; the generic finite module duality/parity/Frobenius arguments themselves are choice-free.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

**Projective duality.** For a finite graded projective left $R(\beta)$-module $P$ put $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$, the $\psi$-twisted graded Hom into the rank-one free module, where $\psi$ is the horizontal-reflection anti-involution. Evaluation $P^\#\to$ (dual of $P$) identifies $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ for finite shifted free modules, and hence for every finite graded projective; the duality reverses internal shifts and fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ after the displayed shift.

Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)-(Q4) for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree
$\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the
resulting ordinary quotient. Then: every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic
annihilator in each fixed block; every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over
$k$; and, for fixed $\beta$ and $i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all
sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In
the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is
nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded
functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are
ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $\psi$ be the horizontal-reflection anti-involution of $R(\beta)$ (reflection of diagrams about a horizontal axis, which reverses the order of crossings); for a finitely generated graded left module $P$ let $P^{\psi}$ be the right module with $p\cdot r:=\psi(r)p$. For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$([P],[Q])_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finitely generated graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]], [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. Both are additive, vanish on different-weight components, and descend to $K_0(R)=\bigoplus_\beta K_0(R(\beta))$: the tensor form is $A$-bilinear and the Hom form is $A$-sesquilinear (first variable conjugate-linear), with values in $\mathbb Q(q)$, more precisely in the localization adjoining all $(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$; the values lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$ because $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a finite free graded module over the central color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$ of [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. Normalization: $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$, where $P_i=R(\alpha_i)$.

derivations.claim: Base change of projectives and covers. A finite graded projective $P$ is a retract of a finite sum of shifted copies of $A$, so $B\otimes_AP$ is a retract of a finite sum of shifted copies of $B$: it is finite graded projective. The quotient adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,B\otimes_AP')=\operatorname{Hom}_B(B\otimes_AP,B\otimes_AP')$, and every degree-zero endomorphism of $B\otimes_AP$ lifts through the canonical map $P\to B\otimes_AP$; endomorphisms preserve $JP$, so the induced map $\operatorname{End}^0_A(P)\to\operatorname{End}^0_B(B\otimes_AP)$ is a surjective ring homomorphism. If $P$ is indecomposable, its finite-dimensional local degree-zero endomorphism ring has no nontrivial idempotent, so a nonzero quotient has none either: $B\otimes_AP$ is zero or indecomposable. If $JS=0$, the old cover map factors through $P/JP$ and remains essential (a submodule of $B\otimes_AP$ mapping onto $S$ pulls back to a submodule of $P$ mapping onto $S$; essentiality of the old cover makes it all of $P$), so $B\otimes_AP$ is the projective cover of $S$ with the same head. If $JS\ne0$ and $B\otimes_AP\ne0$, finite dimension [F3] supplies a simple quotient, which must be the unique head $S$; as a $B$-module that quotient is annihilated by $J$, forcing $JS=0$ and contradicting the assumption, so $B\otimes_AP=0$.

Every $B$-orbit arises and heads do not merge. Every simple $B$-module is a simple $A$-module by inflation, and its descended cover $B\otimes_AP(S)$ is a nonzero cover, so every $B$-simple/projective orbit arises this way. Distinct surviving heads remain distinct after quotienting because an isomorphism of the descended covers induces an isomorphism of their simple heads as $B$-modules, hence also as $A$-modules after inflation; hence the surviving projective-cover shift orbits cannot merge, and extension of scalars is surjective on projective $K_0$.

Dualities. For finite $P$, evaluation on shifted free modules and restriction to retracts identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B\otimes_AP,B)=\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,A)\otimes_AB$, and applying the generator-fixing anti-involution $\psi$ gives $(B\otimes_AP)^\#=B\otimes_AP^\#$. Inflation does not change the finite vector duality $D_\psi$ of a simple, since the underlying vector space and the $\psi$-action are unchanged. The choice-free normalization clauses of [F2] therefore carry the unique $\#$-self-dual generic covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual simples to unique normalized $B$-covers and simples.

The two pairings. For normalized labels, $h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)=q^a$ in a single shift $a$ because $\operatorname{End}(S)=k$ absolutely, while distinct heads give zero; assigning the simple's shift makes $h=\delta_{P,S}$. Similarly $T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)=\delta_{P,S}$ by finite-projective evaluation and $D(P^\psi\otimes S)=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,D_\psi S)$ for evaluation of a tensor functional; $T$ is bilinear in the two arguments and $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ is first-bar sesquilinear. Extension of scalars induces the surjection on projective $K_0$ by step 2.1. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal statement is used.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set $I$ and no imaginary
simple roots, a KLR datum $Q=(Q_{ij})_{i\ne j}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4), and a
field $k$ placed in degree zero
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]); let
$R=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R(\beta)$ be the resulting graded KLR algebra, with
its idempotents $e(\nu)$, dots $x_a$, crossings $\tau_a$ and degrees
$\deg x_a=2d_{\nu_a}$, $\deg\tau_a=-b_{\nu_a\nu_{a+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). Let $\Lambda$ be a
dominant integral weight and put $\lambda_i:=\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle\ge0$
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

**Cyclotomic data.** For every color $i$ choose a monic polynomial
$a_i(u)\in k[u]$ of degree exactly $\lambda_i$
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]); the standard choice made
below is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. For $n\ge1$ write
$$a(x_s)=\sum_{\nu\in I^n}a_{\nu_s}(x_s)e(\nu)\qquad(1\le s\le n),$$
the element of $R_n(Q)$ that acts on the $\nu$-component by the monic
polynomial $a_{\nu_s}$ in the dot at position $s$.

**The cyclotomic quotient.** For $\beta\in Q_+$ define $J_a(\beta)$ to be the
two-sided ideal of $R(\beta)$ generated by the first-strand elements
$a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)$, $\nu\in I^\beta$; equivalently
$$J_a(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}R(\beta)\,a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)\,R(\beta),$$
and put
$$R_a^\Lambda(\beta):=R(\beta)/J_a(\beta),\qquad R_a^\Lambda(0):=k .$$
The **cyclotomic KLR algebra** is the direct sum
$R_a^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$; it carries the
local units $e(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu)$, which act as the identity
on $R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$ and annihilate the other summands, and it is a
$k$-algebra with these orthogonal idempotents.

**Standard choice and grading.** The STANDARD choice $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$ is
used throughout the graded categorification, duality-normalization and based
statements below; for it we write $R^\Lambda:=R^\Lambda_a$. Under the standard
choice each individual first-strand generator
$x_1^{\lambda_{\nu_1}}e(\nu)$ is homogeneous of degree
$2d_{\nu_1}\lambda_{\nu_1}$ in the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], so the ideal $J_a(\beta)$
and the quotient $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ are graded, and $R^\Lambda$ is a
$\mathbb Z$-graded algebra with local units. The sum $a(x_1)$ itself need not
have one common degree across different colors, and no single degree is
assigned to it.

**Boundary of the definition.** Arbitrary monic polynomials with lower
coefficients in degree-zero $k$ give an UNGRADED deformation $R_a^\Lambda$;
nilpotent dots, homogeneous trace degree and the highest-weight graded $K_0$
identification are not asserted for that branch, and the ungraded branch is
used only where a statement explicitly says so. Finite dimension, finite root
strings, ordinary projectivity and symmetry of the standard quotient have the
separately stated monic conclusions below. The cyclotomic relation is imposed
on the FIRST strand, and cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]); this convention
fixes the side on which the quotient map acts throughout the page.

This definition uses no choice.

Use the standard graded cyclotomic quotient of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], and keep the conventions
fixed there: the cyclotomic relation is imposed on the FIRST strand and
cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT. Fix $\beta\in Q_+$ and a
color $i$; put
$$A:=R^\Lambda(\beta),\qquad B:=R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i),\qquad e:=e(\beta,i),$$
where $e(\beta,i)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu i)\in R(\beta+\alpha_i)$ is the
idempotent of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]
supported on the sequences ending in $i$.

**The right-append corner homomorphism.** Right append defines a
$k$-algebra homomorphism
$$\iota_i:A\longrightarrow eBe,\qquad 1_A\longmapsto e,\quad e(\nu)\longmapsto e(\nu i),\quad x_a\longmapsto x_a,\quad \tau_a\longmapsto\tau_a ,$$
sending each old dot or crossing to the same-named generator at the same
position in the first $|\beta|$ strands of $R^\Lambda(\beta+\alpha_i)$ and
each old idempotent to the longer idempotent obtained by appending $i$. It is
a graded homomorphism of degree zero: each generic relation (1)-(7) of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] is preserved
under right append, and the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $A$ maps to
the first-strand cyclotomic generator of $B$, so the cyclotomic relation is
preserved and $\iota_i$ is well defined on the quotient. The unit is sent to
the corner unit $e$, not to a global unit of $B$; it is **not** asserted that
$\iota_i$ is injective, and $e$ is allowed to be zero.

**The functors.** On graded left modules define
$$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M):=Be\otimes_A M,\qquad E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N):=eN,$$
the tensor over the graded balanced tensor product of
[[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]] and the idempotent
restriction of the graded $B$-module $N$
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). Both are additive
$k$-linear functors between the graded module categories, they preserve
degree-zero maps, and they extend to direct sums over the root degrees
$\beta\in Q_+$.

**Adjunction, weights and shifts.** Evaluation at $e$ identifies
$\operatorname{HOM}_B(Be,N)$ with $eN$ by the degree-zero tensor--Hom
adjunction, giving $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ with its
actual grading. The functor $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ increases ROOT degree by
$\alpha_i$, taking modules at root $\beta$ to modules at root
$\beta+\alpha_i$, and decreases the module weight $\Lambda-\beta$ by
$\alpha_i$; restriction does the reverse. Both composites are endofunctors at
a fixed root degree. Grading shifts satisfy
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M\{r\})\cong F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(M)\{r\}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N\{r\})\cong E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(N)\{r\}$, using the
internal shifts of [[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]].

specialization $a_j(u)$ the quotient $R^\Lambda_a(\beta)$ of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]] carries no grading, and
the same formulas define the ungraded functors $F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$; no graded statement is asserted on that branch.

shifted second adjunction are theorems below, not part of this definition; in
particular no unshifted right adjunction $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv
F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is asserted here, and the explicit shift of the second
adjunction is supplied by the coherent-biadjunction lemma of this page. This
definition uses no choice.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

**Projective duality.** For a finite graded projective left $R(\beta)$-module $P$ put $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$, the $\psi$-twisted graded Hom into the rank-one free module, where $\psi$ is the horizontal-reflection anti-involution. Evaluation $P^\#\to$ (dual of $P$) identifies $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ for finite shifted free modules, and hence for every finite graded projective; the duality reverses internal shifts and fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ after the displayed shift.

Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient.
For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$,
$B\otimes_AP(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is
zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises
this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom
duality commutes with this base change, and finite vector duality commutes with
inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual
simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels
$h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and
$T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is
bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on
projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise
is used.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] over any field $k$. Then the homomorphism $\gamma:Af\to K_0(R)$ of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]] is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebras and of $\mathbb N[I]$-graded twisted bialgebras:
(i) **Surjectivity.** Every class in $K_0(R(\beta))$ is a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear combination of classes of divided-power projectives $[P_\theta]$, $\theta$ a sequence of divided powers of weight $\beta$; hence $\gamma$ is onto.
(ii) **Injectivity.** $\gamma$ is injective, because it preserves the forms by [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]] and the source form $B_L$ (equivalently $B_K$) is nondegenerate on each finite weight component.
(iii) **Compatibility.** $\gamma$ intertwines the multiplications ($[\mathrm{Ind}]$ against the product in $Af$), the comultiplications ($[\mathrm{Res}]$ against $r$), the bar involutions and the forms; the free $A$-rank of $K_0(R(\beta))$ equals the free $A$-rank of $Af_\beta$; no rank or dimension comparison of the infinite-dimensional algebra $R(\beta)$ itself with $f_\beta$ is asserted.
Equivalently, $K_0(R)$ is a free $A$-module with the classes of the indecomposable graded projective $R$-modules as a shift-orbit basis ([[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]), and the divided-power classes span; the triangularly selected classes $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis, whereas the family of all divided-power words is generally redundant.

derivations.claim: The vacuum is a nonzero highest-weight vector. The rank-zero block is $R^\Lambda(0)=k$, so $1_\Lambda=[k]$ is nonzero; restriction from root zero has zero target, so $E_i1_\Lambda=0$ for every $i$; and the torus acts on the root-zero component by $q^{\langle a,\Lambda\rangle}$, so its weight is $\Lambda$.

Divided generation. The quotient-cover lemma [F3] makes extension of scalars surjective on split $K_0$, so it suffices to generate the generic $K_0$ by extensions of divided words. The generic negative-half categorification identifies generic $K_0$ with $U_A^-$ and its divided-power projectives with the divided generators; their extensions are the cyclotomic divided functors applied to the vacuum, so the classes $F_{i_r}^{(a_r)}\cdots F_{i_1}^{(a_1)}1_\Lambda$ span $K_0(R^\Lambda)$ over $A$. This does not divide by a quantum factorial: $F_i^a=[a]_{q_i}!F_i^{(a)}$ has a generally nonunit coefficient, which is exactly why the stronger generation statement must use divided words. Combining this generation with the independent normalized-action result of [[lem-cyclotomic-normalized-functors-give-an-integrable-quantum-action]] gives $U_A^-1_\Lambda=K_0(R^\Lambda)$ without a circular appeal to the integral highest-weight theorem.

derivations.claim: The two normalizations agree with the actions. The normalized-action supplier [F1] gives, for $E_i$ applied to input root $\beta+\alpha_i$, the exponent $-1-h_i(\beta+\alpha_i)=1-h_i(\beta)$, exactly the target-weight normalization; the same computation with the factor on $F$ gives the Kang--Kashiwara normalization. Both satisfy the mixed relations, the full Serre families and local nilpotence, and $K_i|_\beta=q_i^{h_i(\beta)}$ in all cases; hence all four displayed operator families are integrable weight module structures after scalar extension to $\mathbb Q(q)$, with no assertion of finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules in affine or indefinite type.

Bilinearity and perfectness of $T$. Tensor products of finite modules are finite, so $T$ has Laurent-polynomial values. The quotient-cover lemma [F2] gives absolutely simple normalized heads and $T(P(S),S')=\delta_{S,S'}$, proving weightwise perfectness in normalized bases; shifting either tensor factor multiplies by the same power of $q$, which is exactly $A$-bilinearity. Finite-projective evaluation identifies $\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$ with $(P^\#)^\psi\otimes M$, so $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$, which is first-bar-sesquilinear rather than bilinear.

Adjointness of the two normalized actions. For the corner $A_\beta\to eB_{\beta+i}e$, associativity of the balanced tensor over the corner gives $T_B(F^{\mathrm{basic}}P,M)=T_A(P,E^{\mathrm{basic}}M)$: both sides are the dimension of the same balanced tensor. The generator-fixing anti-involution flips balanced tensors, so $T_B(P,F^{\mathrm{basic}}M)=T_A(E^{\mathrm{basic}}P,M)$ as well, the corner factors becoming $eB$ and $Be$ in opposite order with multiplication giving the evaluation isomorphism. Multiplying the second identity by $q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}$ gives the first normalized adjoint statement, and the first identity gives the other; neither the Frobenius theorem nor the highest-weight $K_0$ theorem is used.

The defect rescaling. Adding an $i$ changes the defect by $d_i(h_i(\beta)-1)$, so the two module actions of step 1.1 are conjugate by the weight rescaling $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$ with $\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$; the same computation applies on projective $K_0$ with the roles of $E$ and $F$ exchanged. Hence the canonical and Kang--Kashiwara normalizations define the same quantum structure up to the stated conjugation, completing the proof.

For the standard graded quotient, $1_\Lambda=[k]\in K_0(R^\Lambda(0))$ is a
nonzero highest-weight vector of weight $\Lambda$ for the normalized action.
Every finite projective is a finite retract of a sum of shifted word
projectives $P_\nu=R^\Lambda(\beta)e(\nu)$, and
$[P_\nu]=F_{\nu_n}\cdots F_{\nu_1}1_\Lambda$ for right append. The stronger
integral generation statement is by DIVIDED words: the classes
$F_{i_r}^{(a_r)}\cdots F_{i_1}^{(a_1)}1_\Lambda$ span $K_0(R^\Lambda)$ over
$A$. Thus $U_A^-1_\Lambda=K_0(R^\Lambda)$. The retract statement alone is not
claimed to make ordinary word classes an $A$-spanning set.

For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any field and any real
symmetrizable Cartan datum with admissible graded KLR parameters, put
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $h_i(\beta)=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$, and
$q_i=q^{d_i}$. On projective $K_0$ use $F_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i|_\beta=q_i^{-1-h_i(\beta)}E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$; on module $G_0$ use
either the SAME canonical normalization, or the Kang--Kashiwara normalization
$E_i^{\mathrm{KK}}=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$,
$F_i^{\mathrm{KK}}|_\beta=q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$. In all cases
$K_i|_\beta=q_i^{h_i(\beta)}$. These operators satisfy the full quantum mixed
and Serre relations and are locally nilpotent; their scalar extensions to
$\mathbb Q(q)$ are integrable weight modules. No decomposition into
finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules is asserted in affine or
indefinite type.

$T_\beta(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}M)$ is
$A$-BILINEAR and weightwise perfect in normalized projective-cover/simple
bases. The Hom pairing $h(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$
instead satisfies $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ and is first-bar-sesquilinear. For $T$,
projective $E_i$ is adjoint to module $F_i^{\mathrm{KK}}$ and projective $F_i$
to module $E_i^{\mathrm{KK}}$. The two module actions are conjugate by the
weight rescaling $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$, where
$\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

**Projective duality.** For a finite graded projective left $R(\beta)$-module $P$ put $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$, the $\psi$-twisted graded Hom into the rank-one free module, where $\psi$ is the horizontal-reflection anti-involution. Evaluation $P^\#\to$ (dual of $P$) identifies $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ for finite shifted free modules, and hence for every finite graded projective; the duality reverses internal shifts and fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ after the displayed shift.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $G_\infty(b)$, $G_\lambda(\beta)$ be the lower global bases of $U_A^-$ and $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. Then:

(i) $\pi_\lambda:U_A^-\to V_A(\lambda)$ is a based quotient over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$: $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=0$ if its crystal image $\pi_\lambda(b)\in\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ is $0$, and $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$ otherwise; consequently the kernel of $\pi_\lambda$ on $U_A^-$ is the $A$-span of exactly the killed lower global elements, the surviving elements map bijectively onto the integral highest-module basis $G_\lambda(\mathcal B(\lambda))$, the module weight components are finite free over $A$, and the compatible zero/infinity chart and residue projections have the crystal compatibility of the completed grand loop, all for every symmetrizable datum with the explicit label and auxiliary-realization convention;

(ii) more precisely, the integral kernel is
$$\ker\bigl(\pi_\lambda|_{U_A^-}\bigr)=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda(h_i)}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}=\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(U_A^-\cap U_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}\bigr),$$
so the integral highest-module presentation uses all divided right powers beyond each highest limit, not just an ordinary power with a nonunit factorial.

Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, with rational discrete valuation rings $A_0$ at $q=0$ and $A_\infty$ at $q=\infty$. Put $M_A=U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, $L=\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$, and $L^-=\psi(L)$, the bar lattice, as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]].

The **integral residue lattice** is $L_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L$, a $\mathbb Z[q]$-module, and its **bar lattice** is $L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M_A\cap L^-$, a $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$-module. The **balanced intersection** is $E_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$, a $\mathbb Z$-module. Since $q^{-1}M_A=M_A$, one has $M_A\cap qL=qL_{\mathbb Z}$; consequently the residue map $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}\to L/qL$ is injective and is $\mathbb Z$-linear. Its image is an integral subgroup of the rational crystal space, not the entire $\mathbb Q$-space. No Laurent-$A$-linearity is asserted on the residue lattice or on the residue map.

The field projection $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, restricts to an $A$-linear surjection $U_A^-\to V_A(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), and it sends $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)$ into $L_{\mathbb Z}(\lambda)$ by the already-proved grand-loop lattice projection ([[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]). The module $V_A(\lambda)$ is $U_A$-stable: the divided-power and toral reordering identities of [[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] reduce the action on $v_\lambda$ to negative divided powers and Gaussian scalars in $A$, with all positive generators killing the highest vector except through the unit, and the residue compatibility of the projection is [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]]. No global freeness, residue spanning or balancedness is assumed here. The integral residue subgroup for the negative half is proved below to be $\mathbb Z B(\infty)$; the module subgroup $\mathbb Z B(\lambda)$ is a consequence of globalization.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support contained in
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient.
For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$,
$B\otimes_AP(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is
zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises
this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom
duality commutes with this base change, and finite vector duality commutes with
inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual
simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels
$h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and
$T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is
bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on
projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise
is used.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $\psi$ be the horizontal-reflection anti-involution of $R(\beta)$ (reflection of diagrams about a horizontal axis, which reverses the order of crossings); for a finitely generated graded left module $P$ let $P^{\psi}$ be the right module with $p\cdot r:=\psi(r)p$. For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$([P],[Q])_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finitely generated graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]], [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. Both are additive, vanish on different-weight components, and descend to $K_0(R)=\bigoplus_\beta K_0(R(\beta))$: the tensor form is $A$-bilinear and the Hom form is $A$-sesquilinear (first variable conjugate-linear), with values in $\mathbb Q(q)$, more precisely in the localization adjoining all $(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$; the values lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$ because $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a finite free graded module over the central color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$ of [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. Normalization: $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$, where $P_i=R(\alpha_i)$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The **linear
contravariant anti-involution** $\sigma$ of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is defined on
generators by

$$\sigma(q)=q,\qquad\sigma(K_h)=K_h,\qquad\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1},\qquad\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i,$$

extended as an anti-algebra map, $\sigma(xy)=\sigma(y)\sigma(x)$. It is
$\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the torus (it does not invert it), and is an
involution (Verification, step 1.1). It is distinct from the semilinear
contravariant anti-involution $\tau$ with $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$,
$\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 2.2), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
label-weight spaces of $L(\lambda)$ are orthogonal and the restriction of $B$
to each finite-dimensional label-weight space is nondegenerate (Verification,
step 4.1). The
existence, the identification of the radical on the Verma module and the
descent to $L(\lambda)$ are proved in the local Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`, which
is the declared justification of this definition. That lemma is proved on this
page, and its statement is the supplier of the existence and nondegeneracy
clauses above; establishing those clauses is its content rather than a claim of
this definition.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

derivations.claim: By F1 the map $U_A^-\to K_0(R^\Lambda)$, $u\mapsto u1_\Lambda$, is surjective. For every $s>\lambda_i$, the staircase idempotent in F3 is divisible on the left by $x_1^{\lambda_i}$, since $s-1\ge\lambda_i$, and therefore is zero in the standard quotient. The generator-fixing anti-involution preserves its cyclotomic ideal, so the dual projector defining the divided-power projective is zero as well. Hence $F_i^{(s)}1_\Lambda=0$ without dividing by a quantum factorial. All translates $U_A^-F_i^{(s)}$ therefore lie in its kernel. The exact integral projection presentation in F3 gives a well-defined surjective $A$-linear map $f:V_A(\Lambda)\to K_0(R^\Lambda)$ sending $v_\Lambda$ to $1_\Lambda$ and every divided word to the corresponding divided-functor class.

The anti-involution identifies $P^\psi\otimes Q$ with $Q^\psi\otimes P$ by interchanging the factors, so the projective tensor form $T$ is symmetric and $A$-bilinear. Different root blocks pair by zero. The basic corner identities of F2 give $T(F_iP,Q)=T(P,E_i^{\rm basic}Q)$ and $T(E_i^{\rm basic}P,Q)=T(P,F_iQ)$. At input $\beta+\alpha_i$ and output $\beta$, put $h=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$. Projective $E_i=q_i^{1-h}E_i^{\rm basic}$ and $q_i^{-1}K_iE_i=q_i^{h-1}E_i=E_i^{\rm basic}$ on this target. Thus the first identity is $T(F_iP,Q)=T(P,\sigma(F_i)Q)$.

The integral positive operators are defined as well. On $n$-fold basic restriction the last $n$ equal-color dots and crossings give a nil-Hecke action commuting with the target algebra. Its graded matrix-column decomposition in F3 expresses this restriction as $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of an idempotent summand, with the symmetric centering of the polynomial column. Restriction preserves finite projectives by F2, so this summand is finite projective. Multiplying it by the integral grading shift from the $n$ successive $E_i$ normalizations realizes the rational operator $E_i^n/[n]_i!$ on $K_0$; thus it preserves $K_0$ without inverting the factorial in $A$. Negative divided powers are realized by the analogous induction idempotents of F3. A toral binomial acts on an integral weight by $\prod_{s=1}^t[m+c-s+1]_i/[s]_i$. For $m+c\ge0$ this is the integral Gaussian binomial (or zero), and for $m+c<0$ it is $(-1)^t\binom{-(m+c)+t-1}{t}_i$, again integral by [[lem-quantum-pascal-recurrence-and-gaussian-integrality]]. Hence the full $U_A$ acts on $K_0$; its relations follow from the rational action because the cover basis in F4 makes $K_0$ torsion-free.

The quotient-cover bases in F4 make $K_0$ free over $A$; in particular its nonzero vacuum stays nonzero after tensoring with $\mathbb Q(q)$. By F2 the rationalized target is an integrable cyclic highest-weight module of weight $\Lambda$. The universality and ordinary simplicity in F3 identify it with $V(\Lambda)$ by the unique map preserving the highest vector. This map is the rationalization of $f$, since both agree on every divided word. Thus $f$ becomes an isomorphism after localization.

An element $z\in\ker f$ maps to zero on localization, so some nonzero $a\in A$ kills $z$. The source $V_A(\Lambda)$ is an actual submodule of the vector space $V(\Lambda)$ over the fraction field, by F3, and is consequently torsion-free. Hence $z=0$, proving $f$ injective. Its inverse $\phi$ is the required integral isomorphism; the original vacuum map has exactly the integral projection kernel in the Statement. The rational isomorphism intertwines all normalized positive, negative and toral operators. Each difference of their integral operator maps has zero localization, and the target $K_0$ is torsion-free by F4, so the equality holds integrally, including the actual divided powers. Uniqueness follows from divided-word generation.

For the second identity, take $P$ at root $\beta+\alpha_i$ and $Q$ at root $\beta$. Its normalization yields $T(E_iP,Q)=q_i^{1-h}T(P,F_iQ)$. On $Q$, $q_iF_iK_i^{-1}=q_i^{1-h}F_i$, so this is $T(E_iP,Q)=T(P,\sigma(E_i)Q)$. The torus is scalar on each root component and preserves its label, giving toral contravariance. The vacuum tensor product is $k$, of norm one. Transported by $\phi$, these identities and symmetry give exactly the normalized highest-weight contravariant form; uniqueness in F4 identifies it. This uses the highest-weight form, rather than the generic negative-half form or a supposed new radical of that form.

Steps 1.1, 2.1 and 3.1 prove the unique integral highest-weight isomorphism and its exact divided right-power kernel in the full stated general-field/general-Cartan scope. Steps 1.2 and 4.1 prove the tensor-form assertion. Projective-cover shift orbits give the independent free $A$-basis, without treating all divided words as a basis or making a quantum factorial invertible. AC is inherited only through the declared generic categorification and quantum highest-weight suppliers; the localization, torsion-free kernel and finite corner computations introduce no further choice.

risk_review.notes: Read all seven proof steps and all twenty-two exact direct prerequisites. The staircase projector is killed for s>lambda_i, as is its psi image, so the divided vacuum map factors through the exact integral right-power presentation without factorial inversion. Quotient-cover bases make K0 free and the vacuum survives localization; normalized integrable cyclic highest-weight universality gives the rational isomorphism, and the source lattice inside V(Lambda) is torsion-free, proving integral injectivity. For n-fold E, last n dots/crossings commute with the old target and the nil-Hecke matrix column yields [n]_i! times an idempotent summand; all E normalization shifts are integral, so positive divided powers preserve projectives/classes. Toral binomials with negative upper index are (-1)^t times the nonnegative Gaussian binomial; zero/positive indices are integral as stated. Rational relations descend into the free cover basis. Tensor corner identities give the exact linear sigma adjunctions and vacuum norm 1, hence the highest-weight form. AC is inherited, not used by finite splitting or localization. No held diagram, symmetry or categorified crystal theorem is needed.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 4.1), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
label-weight spaces of $L(\lambda)$ are orthogonal and the restriction of $B$
to each finite-dimensional label-weight space is nondegenerate (Verification,
step 5.1). The
existence, the identification of the radical on the Verma module and the
descent to $L(\lambda)$ are proved in the local Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`, which
is the declared justification of this definition. That lemma is proved on this
page, and its statement is the supplier of the existence and nondegeneracy
clauses above; establishing those clauses is its content rather than a claim of
this definition.

Let $M=\bigoplus_\mu M_\mu$ be $U_q^-$ or an integrable highest weight module $V(\lambda)$, with finite root or label components, lower global $A$-lattice $M_A=\bigoplus_\mu(M_A)_\mu=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}AG(b)$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] with rational lower charts $L_0$, $L_\infty=\psi(L_0)$ of the balanced triple [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]], and let $B$ be the normalized homogeneous Kashiwara half form, respectively the contravariant polarization of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] and [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

The **restricted graded integral form-dual** of $M_A$ is
$$M_A^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(M_A)_\mu)\subseteq A\},$$
the direct sum being taken over weight components so that ordinary (not product) duals of the infinite-dimensional pieces are used; the **dual rational charts** are
$$L_0^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_0)_\mu)\subseteq A_0\},\qquad L_\infty^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_\infty)_\mu)\subseteq A_\infty\}.$$
The **upper global family** is the unique homogeneous field family $G^{\mathrm{up}}(b)$ ($b\in\mathcal B$) determined by the inverse Gram system
$$B(G(b'),G^{\mathrm{up}}(b))=\delta_{b,b'}\qquad(b,b'\in\mathcal B_\mu);$$
it is defined componentwise by finite-dimensional linear algebra because each component form is nondegenerate. The **upper bar** $\psi^\vee$ is the $B$-adjoint semilinear involution characterized by $B(\psi u,\psi^\vee v)=\overline{B(u,v)}$, and the **upper Kashiwara operators** are the adjoints $\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$ and $\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$, defined componentwise by the same nondegenerate finite-dimensional forms; they are in general distinct from the lower operators.

The upper zero chart is the dual chart $L_0^\vee$, and after the grand loop its perfection identifies it with $L_0$; the upper infinity chart $L_\infty^\vee$ is not automatically the lower bar chart $L_\infty$, and no such identification is asserted. Existence of the upper family in the integral lattices, weightwise perfect $A$-duality, dual globalization in these genuine dual charts and crystal compatibility for the adjoint operators are the exact conclusions of [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]; adjacent divided-string formulas of the next lemma supply the adjoints of the lower string shifts with their weights, so no unweighted adjunction, no full product identification $M_A^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M_A,A)$, no lower $A$-self-duality, no ordinary-bar fixedness and no unqualified upper/lower operator equality is assumed here.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $\psi$ be the horizontal-reflection anti-involution of $R(\beta)$ (reflection of diagrams about a horizontal axis, which reverses the order of crossings); for a finite graded left module $P$ let $P^{\psi}$ be the right module with $p\cdot r:=\psi(r)p$. For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$([P],[Q])_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finite graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]], [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. Both are additive, vanish on different-weight components, and descend to $K_0(R)=\bigoplus_\beta K_0(R(\beta))$: the tensor form is $A$-bilinear and the Hom form is $A$-sesquilinear (first variable conjugate-linear), with values in $\mathbb Q(q)$, more precisely in the localization adjoining all $(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$; the values lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$ because $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a finite free graded module over the central color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$ of [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. Normalization: $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$, where $P_i=R(\alpha_i)$.

derivations.claim: Perfectness and the dual isomorphism. By [F1] each weight component has finitely many absolutely simple graded shift orbits and normalized projective covers, and the exactness of projective tensor pairing together with the unscaled diagonal values gives perfectness over $A$ on each weight. Hence $G_0$ is free on the simple classes and the functional map $\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$ is an isomorphism from $G_0(R^\Lambda)$ to the weightwise dual $\bigoplus_\beta\operatorname{Hom}_A(V_A(\Lambda)_{\Lambda-\beta},A)$, i.e. the restricted weight dual and not a full unrestricted product dual.

Intertwining with the canonical action. Transport $K_0$ by $\phi$; its tensor form is the actual highest-weight contravariant form with $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$ ([[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]). From tensor adjunction, $T(P,F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}M)=T(E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}P,M)=T(\sigma(F_i)P,M)$, and the analogous normalized identity is $T(P,E_i^{\mathrm{can}}M)=T(\sigma(E_i)P,M)$; these are precisely the restricted contravariant-dual action relations, so $\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}$ intertwines the canonical module action with the dual action and sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis.

The KK normalization and the Hom pairing. The Kang--Kashiwara action differs from the canonical one by the weight rescaling $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$ on root $\beta$, so its intertwiner is $\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}|_\beta$; in particular the unrescaled KK identification is not asserted to send simples to the upper global basis. The Hom pairing satisfies $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ by [F1] and is first-bar-sesquilinear, which concerns the other duality and does not alter the bilinear tensor-dual identification. The Axiom of Choice is inherited only through the integral projective identification [F2] and the contravariant-form suppliers [F3].

citations.quote:
Let $k$ be any field and $R(Q)$ the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum and any homogeneous $Q$ satisfying the standing symmetry and
nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared
up to internal shift. For a simple $S$ of root weight $\beta$ and
$r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, its ordinary one-step last-$i$ restriction has a single
simple graded socle and a single simple graded head, each once and of the same
shift orbit, with $\epsilon_i=r-1$; its maximum-$\epsilon$ composition part has
coefficient a grading shift of $[r]_i$. The last-dot nilpotence index on that
restriction is exactly $r$. The first-end statements hold with
$\epsilon_i^L$ and the first dot. For every $n\ge1$,
$\operatorname{Ind}(S\boxtimes L(i^n))$ has a unique simple graded head
$f_i^nS$, occurring once in its whole composition series, with
$\epsilon_i=r+n$ (also when $r=0$); all other constituents have smaller
$\epsilon_i$. One-step simple socle and simple induction head are partial
inverses. A simple $S$ survives the first-strand cyclotomic quotient with
exponents $\lambda_i$ exactly when $\epsilon_i^L(S)\le\lambda_i$ for all $i$.
Right restriction preserves surviving simples, while projected right induction
has the same simple head when that generic head survives and is zero
otherwise. These are shift-orbit assertions and do not assert factorial socle
multiplicity.

Let $k$ be any field and $R(Q)$ the graded KLR algebra for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum and any homogeneous $Q$ satisfying the standing symmetry and
nonzero extremal-coefficient conditions. Graded simple modules are compared up
to internal shift. Set $c_i(S)=\epsilon_i^L(S)$ and
$J_i(S)=\max\{n\ge0:c_i(f_i^nS)=c_i(S)\}$. This maximum is finite and
$J_i(S)=\epsilon_i(S)+c_i(S)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$ for
$\beta=\operatorname{wt}(S)$. For $i\ne j$ one has $c_i(f_jS)=c_i(S)$; for
$j=i$ it stays constant or increases by $1$, and increase is equivalent to
$f_iS=f_i^LS$ and to simplicity of $\operatorname{Ind}(S,L(i))$. Once it
increases, it increases at every later right-$i$ step. Put
$\operatorname{wt}(S)=-\beta$ and $\phi_i=\epsilon_i+\langle h_i,
\operatorname{wt}\rangle$. The maps
$\Psi_i(S)=(e_i^L)^{c_i(S)}S\otimes b_i(-c_i(S))$ are strict injective
elementary-crystal maps, and every nonvacuum simple has positive extraction at
some $i$. The simple graph is lowering-generated with every generic $f_i$
nonzero. In any first-strand cyclotomic quotient containing $S$ the actual
surviving lowering length is
$\lambda_i+\epsilon_i(S)-\langle h_i,\beta\rangle$. All containing-weight
arguments take place in the auxiliary primitive-coroot finite-support datum,
leaving $R,A,D,Q$ unchanged, so no positive-dominant-label assumption on the
original $P$ is added. Linear divided restriction/$G_0$ operators satisfy the
quantum Serre relation; the simple-socle crystal operators are not asserted to
satisfy a linear Serre identity.

For every real symmetrizable Cartan datum, the canonical negative-half crystal
has strict elementary embeddings
$\Psi_i(b)=\bar b\otimes b_i(-c_i(b))$, where $c_i(b)=\epsilon_i(*b)$,
$\bar b=(e_i^*)^{c_i(b)}b$, $c_i(\bar b)=0$, and every nonvacuum vertex has
positive extraction for some $i$. The negative-half reversal $*$ permutes
$B(\infty)$ without signs; this unsigned conclusion is proved from the existing
signed lattice theorem and positive highest-weight tensor residues, not
assumed. The survivors of $\pi_\lambda$ are exactly $c_i(b)\le\lambda_i$ for
all $i$; with weight $\lambda+\operatorname{wt}(b)$, inherited raising and
surviving lowering, and $\epsilon/\varphi$, they are $B(\lambda)$. Any two
lowering-generated, everywhere-lowerable negative crystals with strict
nonpositive elementary extractions and positive extraction at every nonvacuum
vertex are uniquely isomorphic by their lowering words; the proof uses finite
color cycles and terminates after a height bound. Consequently for any field
and any general homogeneous nondegenerate $Q$ of the first two lemmas, the
shift-orbit simple-module crystal is canonically $B(\infty)$, its first-strand
cyclotomic simple graph is $B(\lambda)$, and the graph labeled by
indecomposable projective COVERS $P(S)$ is the same graph under the unscaled
cover--simple pairing. Projective crystal operators here mean operators
transported on cover labels; no arbitrary $\#$-dual-of-simple identification,
generic global-basis theorem, or independent linear Kashiwara action on the
projective class is used.

Let $(L,B)$ be a crystal basis of an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module $M$ ([[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]) with the induced operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $L/qL$ ([[def-kashiwara-crystal-operators]]). For $b\in B$ write $\mathrm{wt}(b)=\mu$ when $b\in B_\mu$, and define
$$\varepsilon_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde e_i^{\,n}b\neq0\},\qquad \varphi_i(b):=\max\{n\ge0:\tilde f_i^{\,n}b\neq0\}.$$
Then (see below) both numbers are finite and
$$\varphi_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle .$$
The top of the $i$-string through $b$ is the vertex $\tilde e_i^{\,\varepsilon_i(b)}b$, of weight $\mathrm{wt}(b)+\varepsilon_i(b)\alpha_i$; its highest rank-one integer is $\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(b)\rangle+2\varepsilon_i(b)=\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)$.

In the crystal graph of $(L,B)$ the arrows $b\to\tilde f_ib$ are the inverse raising edges: on an existing edge, $\varepsilon_i$ increases by $1$, $\varphi_i$ decreases by $1$ and the weight decreases by $\alpha_i$, and the $i$-chains of $B$ are the finite strings with $\varepsilon_i(b)+\varphi_i(b)+1$ vertices.

For a crystal basis of the negative half $U_q^-$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]) one uses the same arrows and the same finite $\varepsilon_i$, but defines the **formal** $\varphi_i:=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$ as an integer of the abstract root-graded crystal; it may be negative, and it is not the lowering-chain length. The actual lowering-chain length of a negative-half vertex is denoted $\ell_i^-$ and equals $+\infty$, because $\tilde f_i$ is injective there; the negative half is not asserted to be an integrable finite-string module. No choice principle is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. For the standard homogeneous graded quotient over any field, with arbitrary real symmetrizable Cartan datum and admissible graded KLR parameters, there is a unique $U_A$-module isomorphism $\phi:K_0(\mathrm{Proj}\,R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ sending $1_\Lambda$ to $v_\Lambda$ and intertwining all normalized $E_i,F_i,K_i$ and divided powers. In particular $K_0$ is free over $A$. On the NEGATIVE half the vacuum map has exact kernel
$$\ker(U_A^-\to K_0(R^\Lambda))=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda_i}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}.$$
This is the integral negative-half presentation; neither a full-$U_A$ quotient by only $F_i^{(\lambda_i+1)}$ nor invertibility of divided-power factorials is asserted.
For projectives, the tensor form $T(P,Q)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes Q)$ transports to the highest-weight contravariant form normalized by $(v_\Lambda,v_\Lambda)=1$ and $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$, $\sigma(K_i)=K_i$. It is not the generic negative-half Lusztig form with a newly alleged radical.

For the same standard homogeneous general-field/general-Cartan parameters as
the integral projective theorem, the tensor pairing
$T(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes M)$ is weightwise perfect and
$A$-bilinear, with normalized cover/simple dual bases. Its associated map
$$\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow V_A(\Lambda)^\vee=\bigoplus_\beta\operatorname{Hom}_A (V_A(\Lambda)_{\Lambda-\beta},A),\qquad \Psi_{\mathrm{can}}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$$
is an isomorphism to the RESTRICTED weight dual, identified inside
$V(\Lambda)$ using the highest-weight contravariant form. It intertwines the
CANONICAL module action having the same normalization as projective $K_0$, and
sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis. The KK
module action is also sound, but its intertwiner is
$\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}
\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}|_\beta$. Thus an unrescaled KK identification is not
asserted to send simples to the upper global basis. The Hom pairing is instead
first-bar-sesquilinear, $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$; this does not alter the bilinear
tensor-dual identification.

derivations.claim: The simple graph. Inflate a cyclotomic simple to the generic algebra; by [F1] the one-step restriction has a single simple socle and head once and induction has the unique simple head, giving well-defined operators $\widetilde e_i,\widetilde f_i$ on shift orbits with $\varepsilon_i$ decreasing by one under $\widetilde e_i$ and increasing by one under $\widetilde f_i$. By [F2] the graph is lowering-generated with strict elementary extractions and positive extraction at every nonvacuum vertex, over every field including positive characteristic.

Identification with $B(\Lambda)$. Apply the canonical elementary extraction of [F3]: the generic simple graph is canonically $B(\infty)$ and the first-strand cyclotomic survivors are exactly the vertices with $c_i(b)\le\lambda_i$ for all $i$, which is the crystal $B(\Lambda)$ with vacuum $u_\Lambda$; the survivor criterion is $\varepsilon_i^{\mathrm{LEFT}}(S)\le\lambda_i$ for every $i$ by the first-dot index of [F1]. The one-step socle/head is one shifted copy, so no quantum-factorial multiplicity enters.

Projective labels. The normalized indecomposable projectives carry the same crystal by their normalized simple heads and covers: the quotient-cover lemma pairs each projective cover with its simple head without scaling and preserves the label under the quotient, while the two Grothendieck identifications of [F3] record the same labels on $K_0$ and $G_0$. The projective graph is therefore explicitly transported from the simple labels, not obtained by applying linear Kashiwara operators to an unspecified projective basis. The Axiom of Choice is inherited only through the canonical extraction and crystal-existence suppliers of [F3].

citations.quote: Assume the Cartan datum of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] has symmetric Cartan matrix $a_{ij}=a_{ji}$ and uses the quiver normalization $d_i=1$ for every $i$, the field $k$ has characteristic $0$, and the KLR parameters are the quiver-geometric ones (the specialization attached to a finite quiver without loops, with arbitrary arrow multiplicities $h_{ij}$ and $a_{ij}=-(h_{ij}+h_{ji})$: $Q_{ij}(u,v)=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ for $i\ne j$, in the fixed native crossing-sign convention; arbitrary parameter changes, including a global replacement by $u+v$, require their own proved gauge equivalence). Then, normalizing each indecomposable finitely generated graded projective $R(\beta)$-module to be self-dual for the contravariant graded projective duality $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$ ($P\cong P^\#$ after the unique normalizing shift), the map $b\mapsto[P_b]$ is a bijection between the lower global basis $B(\infty)$ of the negative half ([[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]], [[thm-existence-bar-invariance-and-uniqueness-of-the-lower-global-basis]]) and the shift-orbit basis of $K_0(R)$ by self-dual indecomposable projectives; under the isomorphism $\gamma$ of [[thm-klr-categorification-of-the-negative-quantum-half]] one has $\gamma(G(b))=[P_b]$ for the lower global lift $G(b)$, and the identification is compatible with the based quotient of [[thm-global-basis-projection-from-the-negative-half-to-a-highest-weight-module]]. No extension to arbitrary KLR parameters or to non-symmetric Cartan data is asserted here; any such extension requires its own parameter-change invariance theorem.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$, let $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, and let $G_\infty(b)$, $G_\lambda(\beta)$ be the lower global bases of $U_A^-$ and $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. Then:

(i) $\pi_\lambda:U_A^-\to V_A(\lambda)$ is a based quotient over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$: $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=0$ if its crystal image $\pi_\lambda(b)\in\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$ is $0$, and $\pi_\lambda(G_\infty(b))=G_\lambda(\pi_\lambda(b))$ otherwise; consequently the kernel of $\pi_\lambda$ on $U_A^-$ is the $A$-span of exactly the killed lower global elements, the surviving elements map bijectively onto the integral highest-module basis $G_\lambda(\mathcal B(\lambda))$, the module weight components are finite free over $A$, and the compatible zero/infinity chart and residue projections have the crystal compatibility of the completed grand loop, all for every symmetrizable datum with the explicit label and auxiliary-realization convention;

(ii) more precisely, the integral kernel is
$$\ker\bigl(\pi_\lambda|_{U_A^-}\bigr)=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda(h_i)}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}=\sum_{i\in I}\bigl(U_A^-\cap U_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}\bigr),$$
so the integral highest-module presentation uses all divided right powers beyond each highest limit, not just an ordinary power with a nonunit factorial.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] over any field $k$. Then the homomorphism $\gamma:Af\to K_0(R)$ of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]] is an isomorphism of $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebras and of $\mathbb N[I]$-graded twisted bialgebras:
(i) **Surjectivity.** Every class in $K_0(R(\beta))$ is a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear combination of classes of divided-power projectives $[P_\theta]$, $\theta$ a sequence of divided powers of weight $\beta$; hence $\gamma$ is onto.
(ii) **Injectivity.** $\gamma$ is injective, because it preserves the forms by [[thm-klr-cartan-pairing-agrees-with-lusztigs-bilinear-form]] and the source form $B_L$ (equivalently $B_K$) is nondegenerate on each finite weight component.

([[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]) and let $\psi$ be the
descended anti-involution fixing $e(\nu),x_a,\tau_a$; it is well defined

finite graded $B$-module, reverses internal shifts, and $D_\psi^2M\cong M$.

$$P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi,$$

it reverses internal shifts, and $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ on finite graded
projectives ([[def-finitely-generated-graded-projective-module]]).

simple to produce its cover; $D_\psi$ and $\#$ differ already in rank one,

Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient.
For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$,
$B\otimes_AP(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is
zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises
this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom
duality commutes with this base change, and finite vector duality commutes with
inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual
simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels
$h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and
$T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is
bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on
projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise
is used.

characteristic-zero field, and the SAME finite loopless quiver with arbitrary
edge multiplicities and $Q_{ij}=(-1)^{h_{ij}}(u-v)^{h_{ij}+h_{ji}}$ as the
generic global theorem, use the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand quotient and
RIGHT append. The vacuum-normalized isomorphism
$\phi:K_0(\mathrm{Proj}\,R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ maps the classes of
normalized $\#$-self-dual indecomposable cyclotomic projectives bijectively
onto the lower global basis. The normalization is by projective HOM duality and
normalized simple heads, not by finite vector duality or a half-trace shift.
The projective with RIGHT crystal label $c\in B(\Lambda)$ maps to
$G^-_\Lambda(c)$. Every such projective is the surviving extension of a

classes; this is not an assertion that its generic lift is unique. No
arbitrary-parameter based extension is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. For the standard homogeneous graded quotient over any field, with arbitrary real symmetrizable Cartan datum and admissible graded KLR parameters, there is a unique $U_A$-module isomorphism $\phi:K_0(\mathrm{Proj}\,R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ sending $1_\Lambda$ to $v_\Lambda$ and intertwining all normalized $E_i,F_i,K_i$ and divided powers. the integral projective theorem, the tensor pairing
$T(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes M)$ is weightwise perfect and
$A$-bilinear, with normalized cover/simple dual bases. Its associated map

The **restricted graded integral form-dual** of $M_A$ is
$$M_A^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(M_A)_\mu)\subseteq A\},$$
the direct sum being taken over weight components so that ordinary (not product) duals of the infinite-dimensional pieces are used; the **dual rational charts** are

Let $B=R^\Lambda(\beta)$ be a standard graded cyclotomic block
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]) and let $\psi$ be the
descended anti-involution fixing $e(\nu),x_a,\tau_a$; it is well defined

([[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]]). Write shifts internally as $(M\{r\})_m=
