$$D_\psi M:=\operatorname{HOM}_k(M,k)^\psi,$$
the finite $k$-linear dual with $B$-action $(af)(m)=f(\psi(a)m)$. It is a
finite graded $B$-module, reverses internal shifts, and $D_\psi^2M\cong M$.

**Projective Hom duality.** For a finite graded PROJECTIVE $P$ define instead
$$P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi,$$
with the $\psi$-twisted $B$-action. This is again a finite graded projective,
it reverses internal shifts, and $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ on finite graded
projectives ([[def-finitely-generated-graded-projective-module]]).

**They are different dualities.** Hom duality is not applied to a nonprojective
simple to produce its cover; $D_\psi$ and $\#$ differ already in rank one,
where $B=k[x]/x^\lambda$ has $B^\#=B$ while $D_\psi B\cong B\{-2d_i
(\lambda-1)\}$.

[[lem-cyclotomic-projective-covers-and-dualities-descend-through-the-quotient]],
each simple shift orbit has a unique $D_\psi$-self-dual representative $S$, and
its unique normalized cover $P$ with $\operatorname{Hom}^0(P,S)=k$ is
$\#$-self-dual; these normalized representatives are the ones used in the based
statements below. The symmetric theorem
[[thm-cyclotomic-klr-algebras-are-finite-dimensional-graded-symmetric]]
additionally gives $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)\}$;

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and fix a reduced-expression system: for each $w\in S_n$ one reduced word $w=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_r}$, and for $
u\in I^n$ put $	au_w:=	au_{i_1}\cdots	au_{i_r}\in R_n(Q)$. Then the monomials $	au_wx_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}e(
u)$, over all $w\in S_n$, $a_1,\dots,a_n\ge0$ and $
u\in I^n$, form a $k$-basis of $R_n(Q)$; equivalently $R_n(Q)$ is a free $k$-module on these monomials, and $R( eta)$ has the corresponding basis. Moreover each $R( eta)$ has finite-dimensional homogeneous components, and the graded dimension of the summand $e(
u)R_n(Q)e(
u')$ is the formal Laurent Hilbert series counting the monomials (bounded below, equivalently the finite sum of the corresponding rational geometric series), so the graded ranks are independent of the parameters $Q$: for each fixed $ eta$, $\dim_kR( eta)_m<\infty$ for all $m$ and $R( eta)_m=0$ for $m\ll0$; if $I$ is finite the same holds for $R_n(Q)$. In particular $R( eta)$ is a locally finite graded algebra; its degree-zero part need not be one-dimensional (already $x_1	au_1\in R(2\alpha_i)_0$ is a nontrivial idempotent).

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

**Projective duality.** For a finite graded projective left $R(\beta)$-module $P$ put $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$, the $\psi$-twisted graded Hom into the rank-one free module, where $\psi$ is the horizontal-reflection anti-involution. Evaluation $P^\#\to$ (dual of $P$) identifies $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ for finite shifted free modules, and hence for every finite graded projective; the duality reverses internal shifts and fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ after the displayed shift.

Let $k$ be any field and let $Q$ satisfy (Q1)-(Q4) for a real symmetrizable
Cartan datum with finite color set. For monic $a_j(u)\in k[u]$ of degree
$\lambda_j\ge0$, impose $a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)=0$ and write $R^a(\beta)$ for the
resulting ordinary quotient. Then: every dot has a scalar-coefficient monic
annihilator in each fixed block; every $R^a(\beta)$ is finite dimensional over
$k$; and, for fixed $\beta$ and $i$, $R^a(\beta+m\alpha_i)=0$ for all
sufficiently large $m$. Thus right-append induction has finite $i$-strings. In
the standard homogeneous specialization $a_j(u)=u^{\lambda_j}$, every dot is
nilpotent and these are statements about the induced graded algebra and graded
functors. For an inhomogeneous monic specialization the assertions are
ungraded; no graded highest-weight Grothendieck identification is included.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with finite color set $I$ and no imaginary
simple roots, a KLR datum $Q=(Q_{ij})_{i\ne j}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4), and a
field $k$ placed in degree zero
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]],
[[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]); let
$R=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R(\beta)$ be the resulting graded KLR algebra, with
its idempotents $e(\nu)$, dots $x_a$, crossings $\tau_a$ and degrees
$\deg x_a=2d_{\nu_a}$, $\deg\tau_a=-b_{\nu_a\nu_{a+1}}$
([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). Let $\Lambda$ be a
dominant integral weight and put $\lambda_i:=\langle h_i,\Lambda\rangle\ge0$
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

**Cyclotomic data.** For every color $i$ choose a monic polynomial
$a_i(u)\in k[u]$ of degree exactly $\lambda_i$
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]]); the standard choice made
below is $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. For $n\ge1$ write
$$a(x_s)=\sum_{\nu\in I^n}a_{\nu_s}(x_s)e(\nu)\qquad(1\le s\le n),$$
the element of $R_n(Q)$ that acts on the $\nu$-component by the monic
polynomial $a_{\nu_s}$ in the dot at position $s$.

**The cyclotomic quotient.** For $\beta\in Q_+$ define $J_a(\beta)$ to be the
two-sided ideal of $R(\beta)$ generated by the first-strand elements
$a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)$, $\nu\in I^\beta$; equivalently
$$J_a(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}R(\beta)\,a_{\nu_1}(x_1)e(\nu)\,R(\beta),$$
and put
$$R_a^\Lambda(\beta):=R(\beta)/J_a(\beta),\qquad R_a^\Lambda(0):=k .$$
The **cyclotomic KLR algebra** is the direct sum
$R_a^\Lambda:=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$; it carries the
local units $e(\beta)=\sum_{\nu\in I^\beta}e(\nu)$, which act as the identity
on $R_a^\Lambda(\beta)$ and annihilate the other summands, and it is a
$k$-algebra with these orthogonal idempotents.

**Standard choice and grading.** The STANDARD choice $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$ is
used throughout the graded categorification, duality-normalization and based
statements below; for it we write $R^\Lambda:=R^\Lambda_a$. Under the standard
choice each individual first-strand generator
$x_1^{\lambda_{\nu_1}}e(\nu)$ is homogeneous of degree
$2d_{\nu_1}\lambda_{\nu_1}$ in the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], so the ideal $J_a(\beta)$
and the quotient $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ are graded, and $R^\Lambda$ is a
$\mathbb Z$-graded algebra with local units. The sum $a(x_1)$ itself need not
have one common degree across different colors, and no single degree is
assigned to it.

**Boundary of the definition.** Arbitrary monic polynomials with lower
coefficients in degree-zero $k$ give an UNGRADED deformation $R_a^\Lambda$;
nilpotent dots, homogeneous trace degree and the highest-weight graded $K_0$
identification are not asserted for that branch, and the ungraded branch is
used only where a statement explicitly says so. Finite dimension, finite root
strings, ordinary projectivity and symmetry of the standard quotient have the
separately stated monic conclusions below. The cyclotomic relation is imposed
on the FIRST strand, and cyclotomic induction appends strands on the RIGHT
([[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]]); this convention
fixes the side on which the quotient map acts throughout the page.

This definition uses no choice.

derivations.claim: The empty word gives $R^\Lambda(0)=k$. One strand has no crossings, so its presentation is $k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ with $\deg x=2d_i$. For $\lambda_i>0$ the monomials $1,x,\ldots,x^{\lambda_i-1}$ give the stated Hilbert series. The unique graded simple is $k$ at degree zero, and the regular module is its indecomposable projective cover. Evaluation identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B,B)^\psi$ with $B$, so this is the projective Hom-self-dual normalization, without a vector-dual centering shift. The coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda_i-1}$ functional pairs the monomial basis anti-diagonally with unit entries; it is a nondegenerate symmetric Frobenius functional of degree $-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$. If $\lambda_i=0$, its defining relation is $1=0$, so the block is zero and has no simple; if $\lambda_i=1$, it is $k$.

For $n\ge1$, put $S=S_n$ and $C=S[z]/(z^n-e_1z^{n-1}+\cdots+(-1)^ne_n)$, embedded in $P_n$ by $z=x_1$. Let $e'_a$ be the elementary symmetric functions of $x_2,\ldots,x_n$. The identities $e_a=e'_a+ze'_{a-1}$, $e'_0=1$, express the $e'_a$ recursively in $z,e_1,\ldots,e_a$; the final $e'_n=0$ is precisely the displayed monic relation. Hence $C=k[x_1,e'_1,\ldots,e'_{n-1}]$, and the Artin basis for the remaining $n-1$ variables makes $P_n$ free of rank $(n-1)!$ over $C$. On its $S$-basis $1,z,\ldots,z^{n-1}$, multiplication by $z^{\lambda_i}$ is repeated $(n-1)!$ times in multiplication by $x_1^{\lambda_i}$ on $P_n$. In a full matrix algebra over $S$, left and right matrix units isolate each matrix entry and insert it into any chosen entry. Therefore its two-sided ideal is the matrix ideal of exactly those scalar entries, so the cyclotomic quotient is the polynomial-column matrix algebra over their quotient of $S$.

Define $\epsilon:C\to S$ to be the coefficient of $z^{n-1}$ in the power basis. The matrix $\epsilon(z^{a+b})$ for $0\le a,b<n$ is zero for $a+b<n-1$ and one for $a+b=n-1$, hence anti-triangular with unit anti-diagonal and invertible over $S$. Its dual basis is therefore integral over $S$. Pairing multiplication by $z^{\lambda_i}$ with this invertible trace matrix shows that its entry ideal is exactly the ideal generated by $\epsilon(z^{\lambda_i+a+b})$, $0\le a,b<n$. Put $h_r=0$ for $r<0$ and $h_0=1$; the monic equation gives the recurrence $h_r=e_1h_{r-1}-e_2h_{r-2}+\cdots+(-1)^{n-1}e_nh_{r-n}$. Induction on the power gives $\epsilon(z^{n-1+r})=h_r$, including the stated initial values. All indices in the entry list are between $\lambda_i-n+1$ and $\lambda_i+n-1$. The first consecutive $n$ indices $h_{\lambda_i-n+1},\ldots,h_{\lambda_i}$ occur, and the recurrence expresses every higher one using them. Thus the exact corner ideal is $(h_{\lambda_i-n+1},\ldots,h_{\lambda_i})$.

If $n>\lambda_i$, the consecutive list contains $h_0=1$, and the quotient is zero. If $1\le n\le\lambda_i$, every index in that list is positive, so the ideal is contained in the augmentation ideal of $S$ and the corner quotient is nonzero. It is finite dimensional by F2 and the full matrix description of step 1.2. Its degree-zero part is $k$, and its positive-degree ideal is nilpotent because the graded vector space is finite and positively graded. It is therefore graded local with exactly one simple up to shift, its augmentation quotient. Matrix equivalence gives exactly one graded simple column in each nonzero root block. For $n=0$ there is the vacuum, so the total number of normalized rank-one simples is exactly $\lambda_i+1$.

The augmentation simple column is $P_n\otimes_S k$, the ordinary coinvariant polynomial representation with its Artin basis, centered by $-d_i\binom n2$. Its Hilbert series is $q_i^{-\binom n2}\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})=[n]_{q_i}!$. The integral perfect Artin trace in F1 pairs complementary degrees, so this centering makes its generator-fixing finite vector dual isomorphic to itself. This yields the unique normalized simple in every nonzero block. The same matrix model retains the symmetric corner of step 2.1 and its polynomial-column projectives, proving all ranks of part (c), rather than identifying the whole algebra with a commutative quotient.

At $n=\lambda_i=2$, the corner is $k[e_1,e_2]/(h_1,h_2)=k$, since $h_1=e_1$, $h_2=e_1^2-e_2$. The polynomial column is $C_2=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$, with basis $1,x_1$ and $x_2=-x_1$, $x_1^2=0$, so its centered column $S_2=C_2\{-d_i\}$ has Hilbert series $q_i^{-1}+q_i$. The block is $\operatorname{End}_k(S_2)$; its unique simple column is also its normalized indecomposable projective. The regular left module is $S_2\otimes S_2^*$, with the second factor giving shifts $\pm d_i$, and thus its class is $[2]_{q_i}[P_2]$ in projective $K_0$ and $[2]_{q_i}[S_2]$ in module $G_0$. The matrix identification and these formulas hold in characteristic two as well. A one-dimensional zero-dot module would violate the equal-colour mixed relation with unit right side, so no such simple exists.

Finally the coprime polynomials $u,u-1$ give $k[u]/(u(u-1))=k\oplus k$, with two ordinary simples at root $\alpha_i$. This is the ungraded monic deformation: ordinary finiteness and symmetry retain their stated scope, but it is not the standard homogeneous graded rank-one highest-weight identification. Parts (a)–(d) follow from steps 1.1–5.1 with arbitrary symmetrizer and every field, and part (e) from this finite coprime-factor calculation.

For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any degree-zero field and
admissible graded real symmetrizable KLR datum, every block
$B=R^\Lambda(\beta)$ is finite-dimensional, all dots are nilpotent, and
$R^\Lambda(\beta+n\alpha_i)=0$ for large $n$. Put
$\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$. A nonzero
block has a perfect symmetric homogeneous functional
$\operatorname{tr}_\beta:B\to k$ of degree
$t_\beta=-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)$; on a zero block perfectness is
vacuous and the functional is zero. Thus $DB\cong B\{t_\beta\}$ as graded
bimodules. For finite projective $P$, with
$P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,B)^\psi$, one has
$D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{t_\beta\}$, so vector duality preserves projectives.
This does not assert $P^\#=P$ for every shifted projective, nor self-duality
of every indecomposable finite module. For arbitrary monic deformation
polynomials the separate conclusion is finite-dimensional and symmetric
UNGRADED, with finite root strings and monic dot annihilators; nilpotence and
homogeneous trace degree are not asserted. In rank one the standard trace is
the top coefficient on $k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ and has degree
$-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$.

derivations.claim: Projective Hom self-duality. Evaluation $\operatorname{HOM}_B(B,B)\cong B$ gives $P^\#=\operatorname{HOM}_B(B,B)^\psi\cong B=P$ directly, the generator-fixing anti-involution producing the same left module; hence the canonical normalized projective is $P$ with no shift.

Vector duality and the shift. The functional $\epsilon(x^a)=0$ for $a<\lambda-1$ and $\epsilon(x^{\lambda-1})=1$ is the coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda-1}$ trace; it has degree $-2(\lambda-1)$ and its anti-diagonal pairing $\epsilon(x^ax^b)=\delta_{a+b,\lambda-1}$ is perfect over every field, so $D_\psi B\cong B\{-2(\lambda-1)\}$. Since $D_\psi(P\{s\})=D_\psi P\{-s\}$, vector self-duality of $P\{s\}$ solves $-2(\lambda-1)-s=s$, namely $s=-(\lambda-1)$, while projective Hom self-duality solves $-s=s$, namely $s=0$.

The general defect shift and the boundary. For a general normalized cyclotomic projective the same computation with the symmetric theorem gives $D_\psi P\cong P^\#\{-2\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)\}$, which is a comparison of the two dualities and does not redefine the projective normalization. At $\lambda=1$ the two centers agree; at $\lambda=2$ they differ by $1$ as computed; at $\lambda=0$ the defining relation is $1=0$ and the block vanishes, so there is no indecomposable projective here. The trace is never halved to pick the lower-basis class.

citations.quote:
Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

**Projective duality.** For a finite graded projective left $R(\beta)$-module $P$ put $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$, the $\psi$-twisted graded Hom into the rank-one free module, where $\psi$ is the horizontal-reflection anti-involution. Evaluation $P^\#\to$ (dual of $P$) identifies $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ for finite shifted free modules, and hence for every finite graded projective; the duality reverses internal shifts and fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ after the displayed shift.

Work over any field $k$ with a real symmetrizable Cartan datum, arbitrary symmetrizers $d_i$, dominant $\Lambda$ and the STANDARD homogeneous polynomials $a_i=u^{\lambda_i}$.
(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$ has one normalized simple and projective, the vacuum.
(b) For every color $i$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ with $\deg x=2d_i$ and graded dimension $\sum_{r=0}^{\lambda_i-1}q^{2d_ir}$ when $\lambda_i\ge1$. Its unique normalized simple is $k$, its normalized projective HOM-self-dual cover is the regular module, and the coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda_i-1}$ Frobenius FUNCTIONAL has degree $-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$. If $\lambda_i=0$ the block is zero and has NO simple; if $\lambda_i=1$ it is $k$.
(c) In rank one $I=\{i\}$, at EVERY $n\ge0$ the algebra is the cyclotomic nil-Hecke quotient $NH_n/(x_1^{\lambda_i})$. It is nonzero precisely for $0\le n\le\lambda_i$. At each such root it has exactly one normalized self-dual simple, and zero blocks have none; hence there are $\lambda_i+1$ normalized simple classes in total, matching the rank-one highest-weight module. For $1\le n\le\lambda_i$ its symmetric corner is $k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]/(h_{\lambda_i-n+1},\ldots,h_{\lambda_i})$, the graded Grassmannian coinvariant ring, and the algebra is the associated graded polynomial-column matrix algebra. The normalized simple column has graded dimension $[n]_{q_i}!$, where $q_i=q^{d_i}$.
(d) Explicitly at $\lambda_i=2,n=2$, the block is $\operatorname{End}_k(C\{-d_i\})$ with $C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$, its basis $1,x_1$ in degrees $0,2d_i$. Its unique self-dual simple $S_2=C\{-d_i\}$ has graded dimension $q_i^{-1}+q_i$ and is also the normalized indecomposable projective $P_2$. It is NOT a one-dimensional module with both dots zero. The regular class is $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=[2]_{q_i}[P_2]$ in $K_0$ and $[2]_{q_i}[S_2]$ in $G_0$.
(e) Arbitrary monic $a_i$ gives the ungraded deformation: $\lambda_i=2$, $a_i=u(u-1)$ gives $k\oplus k$ at root $\alpha_i$. Ordinary finiteness/symmetry remain true, but this is not the standard graded $V(2)$ identification.

Let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$, let $L^-:=\psi(L)$ be the bar lattice, all as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]] and [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], and let $E_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ be the balanced intersection. Let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$.

By [[thm-the-highest-weight-crystal-triple-is-balanced]] the integral triple $(M_A,L,L^-)$ is balanced componentwise: for every root or label degree the canonical map $E_{\mathbb Z}\to(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is an isomorphism onto the free $\mathbb Z$-span $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}\mathbb Zb$ of the crystal classes of that degree. For $b\in\mathcal B$ define the **lower global lift** $G(b)$ to be the unique element of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ whose residue class in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$. The family $G(\mathcal B)$ is the **lower global basis** of $M_A$ (of $U_A^-$ or of $V_A(\lambda)$).

With these definitions, the theorem's extensions give the basis assertions: the $A$-span of $G(\mathcal B)$ is $M_A$, its $A_0$-span is $L$, its $A_\infty$-span is $L^-$, and its $\mathbb Z$-span is $E_{\mathbb Z}$, while after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ the residue classes of the $G(b)$ are the full rational crystal spaces; in particular $G(\mathcal B)$ is an $A$-basis of $M_A$. Each $G(b)$ is bar fixed, $G(0)$ is not defined, and no equality of $E_{\mathbb Z}$ with the whole Laurent module $M_A$ is implied; the identification of the integral residue subgroup with $\mathbb Z\mathcal B(\lambda)$ for highest modules is the corresponding part of the same theorem. The lifts are characterized by the simultaneous balanced intersection, not by an unproved unitriangular word-basis condition, and all definitions apply componentwise on finite root or label components and are extended by their direct sums.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Let $\lambda\in P^+$ and let $L(\lambda)$ be the simple integrable highest weight module with highest weight vector $v_\lambda$ ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]); in this page we write $V(\lambda):=L(\lambda)$, following the notation of the crystal sources. Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half with its Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), and let $A_0$ be the crystal limiting ring ([[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]]).

Define $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $V(\lambda)$ generated by all vectors $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda$ ($r\ge0$, $i_1,\dots,i_r\in I$), where for $r=0$ the vector is $v_\lambda$; and $\mathcal L(\infty)$ to be the $A_0$-submodule of $U_q^-$ generated by all $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ ($r\ge0$), where $\mathbf 1$ is the unit of $U_q^-$. Here $\tilde f_i$ on $V(\lambda)$ are the module Kashiwara operators and $\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ are the negative-half operators. Define
$$\mathcal B(\lambda):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}v_\lambda+q\mathcal L(\lambda):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)/q\mathcal L(\lambda),$$
$$\mathcal B(\infty):=\{\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1+q\mathcal L(\infty):r\ge0\}\setminus\{0\}\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty).$$

Then, with $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$:

(a) $\mathcal L(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu$ with $\mathcal L(\lambda)_\mu=\mathcal L(\lambda)\cap V(\lambda)_\mu$, and $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ with $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}=\mathcal L(\infty)\cap U_q^-[-\nu]$; correspondingly $\mathcal B(\lambda)=\bigsqcup_\mu\mathcal B(\lambda)_\mu$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)=\bigsqcup_\nu\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}$.

(b) $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal L(\lambda)$ and $\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)$.

(c) (Recursive spanning.) For $\alpha\in Q_+\setminus\{0\}$,
$$\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\sum_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i},\qquad \mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}=\Bigl(\bigcup_{i\in I}\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha+\alpha_i}\Bigr)\setminus\{0\},$$
and the same formulas with $\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty)$. Each $\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha}$ is generated over $A_0$ by finitely many monomials of total length at most $\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)$, hence is a finitely generated $A_0$-module.

No basis property, scalar-extension spanning or crystal-lattice property of $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ or $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is asserted here; these are conclusions of the grand loop. The script letters avoid the collision with the simple module $L(\lambda)$. No choice principle is used. Each fixed component is torsionfree inside a field vector space and generated by finitely many words of its fixed height, so it is free over the DVR $A_0$; its full field-span is proved later. The field map $\pi_\lambda$ is surjective, but exact equality on Kashiwara monomial generators is not asserted.

Let $M$ be an integrable chosen $P$-graded type-1 module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and fix $i\in I$. By [[thm-unique-kashiwara-i-string-decomposition]] every $u\in M_\lambda$ has a unique admissible decomposition
$$u=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}u_n,\qquad u_n\in H_{\lambda+n\alpha_i}=\ker(E_i)\cap M_{\lambda+n\alpha_i},$$
with $u_n=0$ whenever $n>\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle$. Define the **Kashiwara operators**
$$\tilde e_i u:=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}u_n,\qquad \tilde f_i u:=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}u_n .$$
Both are linear maps on $M$, shifting the label weight by $+\alpha_i$, respectively $-\alpha_i$. Along each string, $\tilde e_i$ moves $F_i^{(n)}u_n$ to $F_i^{(n-1)}u_n$ and kills the top position $n=0$, while $\tilde f_i$ moves it to $F_i^{(n+1)}u_n$ and kills a string exactly at its bottom, where $n=\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}(u_n)\rangle$.

Let $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$ be the projections onto the top positions and the bottom positions of these strings:
$$p_{\mathrm{top}}u:=u_0,\qquad p_{\mathrm{bottom}}u:=\sum_{n:\,n=\langle\lambda+n\alpha_i,h_i\rangle}F_i^{(n)}u_n .$$
Then
$$\ker\tilde e_i=\ker E_i,\qquad \ker\tilde f_i=\ker F_i,\qquad \tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{top}},\qquad \tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}-p_{\mathrm{bottom}},$$
so $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$ are inverse to each other on each existing string edge. Module homomorphisms commute with both operators, $p_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $p_{\mathrm{bottom}}$. On $\ker E_i$ one has $\tilde f_i=F_i$, and on $\ker F_i$ one has $\tilde e_i=E_i$. At interior positions the operators differ from the generators: in the rank-one module $L_i(2)$ with highest vector $v$ and $u=F_iv$, one has $F_iu=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$ while $\tilde f_iu=F_i^{(2)}v$, and $[2]_i\neq1$. No choice principle is used. The analogous Kashiwara operators on the negative half $U_q^-$ are the shifts of its unique $e_i'$-string decomposition ([[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]]), constructed using the skew derivation of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]. Their strings have no bottom: $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ and $\tilde f_i\tilde e_i=\mathrm{id}-P_i$, where $P_i$ projects onto $\ker e_i'$; the second identity follows by subtracting the position-zero coefficient $u_0=P_iu$ from the string expansion. These string-shift operators are distinct from the skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$. No negative-half operator is used in the module verification below.

Fix $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ and the crystal limiting ring $A_0\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$ of [[def-the-local-ring-at-q-zero]], and put $A_\infty:=\psi(A_0)$, the image of $A_0$ under the semilinear involution $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, i.e. the ring of rational functions regular at $q=\infty$; $A_0$ and $A_\infty$ are the rational local rings at $0$ and at infinity, and the integral affine chart coordinate rings are $\mathbb Z[q]$ and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$.

Let $M$ be one of $U_q^-$ or $V(\lambda)=L(\lambda)$ for $\lambda\in P^+$. Equip $M$ with the bar involution $\psi$ of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]: on $U_q^-$ the semilinear algebra involution with $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$; on $V(\lambda)$ the induced semilinear involution determined by $Pv_\lambda\mapsto\psi(P)v_\lambda$, well defined by the highest-module presentation: its negative-half kernel is $\sum_iU_q^-F_i^{\lambda(h_i)+1}$, preserved by $\psi$ because every $F_i$ is fixed ([[thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique]]). Equivalently the full highest-vector relations are bar stable: $E_i$ is fixed, the singular divided powers are fixed, and $\psi(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})=-q^{-\langle\lambda,h\rangle}K_{-h}(K_h-q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle})$. Hence the quotient involution is compatible with the algebra action and fixes $v_\lambda$. Let $M_A\subseteq M$ be the divided-power integral form: $M_A=U_A^-$ for $M=U_q^-$, and $M_A=V_A(\lambda):=U_A^-v_\lambda$ for $M=V(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]); both are $\psi$-stable. Let $L$ be the Kashiwara crystal lattice of $M$ over $A_0$: $L=\mathcal L(\infty)$ for $U_q^-$ and $L=\mathcal L(\lambda)$ for $V(\lambda)$ ([[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]).

Define the **bar lattice** $L^-:=\psi(L)$, an $A_\infty$-submodule of $M$, and the **balanced part** $E:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$.

The definition keeps three structures on the same $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space strictly separate: the $A$-module $M_A$, which is not assumed free and not claimed to be contained in $L$; the free $A_0$-module $L$; and the free $A_\infty$-module $L^-$. No equality $L^-=L$, no inclusion $M_A\subseteq L$, no freeness of $M_A$ and no identification $E=M_A$ are asserted; freeness is a conclusion of the balanced-triple construction on this page, whereas $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module of global lifts and is not equal to the Laurent lattice $M_A$. The bar lattice is not the form-dual (upper) lattice, which is defined later on this page. The intersections $M_A\cap L$ and $M_A\cap L^-$ are respectively $\mathbb Z[q]$- and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$-modules, generally not $A$-modules. The balanced part $E$ is a $\mathbb Z$-module; its Laurent extension $A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E$ is the full integral module once globalization is proved.

More generally a **based integrable module** $(M,B)$ here means exactly: $B$ is a homogeneous field basis; $M_A=\bigoplus_bAb$ is $U_A$-stable; the semilinear involution fixing $B$ is compatible with the algebra action; and $L_0=\bigoplus_bA_0b$ with residue $B$ is a crystal local basis at $0$. These are the four conditions of Lusztig 27.1.2(a)–(d) after the transport $v=q^{-1}$, together with the integrable extension used by Bao–Wang. Such data do not automatically imply an integral $\Theta$-action on an arbitrary based pair. A **based subobject** is a $U$-submodule spanned by a subset of $B$; a **based quotient** is its quotient with the complementary basis images. Based morphisms send $B$ to the target basis or to $0$, and have kernels spanned by the killed basis subset. These exact integral and bar-compatible maps, not arbitrary field summands, are used in tensor inheritance.

derivations.claim: The word class. By [F1] the word projective decomposes as $(q+q^{-1})$ copies of $P_{i,2}$, so $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=(q+q^{-1})[P_{i,2}]$; under the K_0 isomorphism of the integral projective theorem this is the class of the ordinary product $F_i^2v_{2\Lambda_1}$.

In the rank-one module $V(2\Lambda_1)$, the Kashiwara string is $v,F_iv,F_i^{(2)}v$. These vectors generate its zero chart; they are bar fixed and generate the corresponding infinity chart. In weight $2\alpha_i$ the divided-power integral lattice is $AF_i^{(2)}v$: any divided word of that weight is an $A$-multiple of $F_i^{(2)}v$, since $F_i^2v=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$. Since an integral Laurent polynomial regular at both $0$ and infinity is an integer constant, the balanced intersection in that weight is $\mathbb ZF_i^{(2)}v$, and its positive string residue selects $F_i^{(2)}v$ as the lower global lift.

By [F2], $F_i^2v=[2]_iF_i^{(2)}v$. The coefficient $[2]_i=q+q^{-1}$ is a nonunit: evaluation at $q=1$ sends it to $2$, while an invertible Laurent polynomial must evaluate to a unit of $\mathbb Z$. Hence the word class cannot be the lower global vector identified in step 1.2.

This refutes the assertion that word-projective classes are automatically lower global vectors. citations.quote:
Work over any field $k$ with a real symmetrizable Cartan datum, arbitrary symmetrizers $d_i$, dominant $\Lambda$ and the STANDARD homogeneous polynomials $a_i=u^{\lambda_i}$.
(a) $R^\Lambda(0)=k$ has one normalized simple and projective, the vacuum.
(b) For every color $i$, $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)=k[x]/x^{\lambda_i}$ with $\deg x=2d_i$ and graded dimension $\sum_{r=0}^{\lambda_i-1}q^{2d_ir}$ when $\lambda_i\ge1$. Its unique normalized simple is $k$, its normalized projective HOM-self-dual cover is the regular module, and the coefficient-of-$x^{\lambda_i-1}$ Frobenius FUNCTIONAL has degree $-2d_i(\lambda_i-1)$. If $\lambda_i=0$ the block is zero and has NO simple; if $\lambda_i=1$ it is $k$.
(c) In rank one $I=\{i\}$, at EVERY $n\ge0$ the algebra is the cyclotomic nil-Hecke quotient $NH_n/(x_1^{\lambda_i})$. It is nonzero precisely for $0\le n\le\lambda_i$. At each such root it has exactly one normalized self-dual simple, and zero blocks have none; hence there are $\lambda_i+1$ normalized simple classes in total, matching the rank-one highest-weight module. For $1\le n\le\lambda_i$ its symmetric corner is $k[e_1,\ldots,e_n]/(h_{\lambda_i-n+1},\ldots,h_{\lambda_i})$, the graded Grassmannian coinvariant ring, and the algebra is the associated graded polynomial-column matrix algebra. The normalized simple column has graded dimension $[n]_{q_i}!$, where $q_i=q^{d_i}$.
(d) Explicitly at $\lambda_i=2,n=2$, the block is $\operatorname{End}_k(C\{-d_i\})$ with $C=k[x_1,x_2]/(x_1+x_2,x_1x_2)$, its basis $1,x_1$ in degrees $0,2d_i$. Its unique self-dual simple $S_2=C\{-d_i\}$ has graded dimension $q_i^{-1}+q_i$ and is also the normalized indecomposable projective $P_2$. It is NOT a one-dimensional module with both dots zero. The regular class is $[R^\Lambda(2\alpha_i)]=[2]_{q_i}[P_2]$ in $K_0$ and $[2]_{q_i}[S_2]$ in $G_0$.
(e) Arbitrary monic $a_i$ gives the ungraded deformation: $\lambda_i=2$, $a_i=u(u-1)$ gives $k\oplus k$ at root $\alpha_i$. Ordinary finiteness/symmetry remain true, but this is not the standard graded $V(2)$ identification.

Let $R^\Lambda$ be the cyclotomic KLR algebra of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]], let
$E^\Lambda_i,F^\Lambda_i$ be the functors of
[[def-cyclotomic-klr-induction-and-restriction-functors]], and read the
composites $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i$ as
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$ via the weight bookkeeping
fixed there. Put $\lambda:=\Lambda-\beta$ and $q_i:=q^{d_i}$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]).

(a) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\ge0$, there is a natural isomorphism of
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{2k}\mathrm{Id}\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i.$$

(b) If $\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle\le0$, there is a natural isomorphism of
endofunctors of $\mathrm{Mod}(R^\Lambda(\beta))$
$$q_i^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\;\cong\;E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i\oplus\bigoplus_{k=0}^{-\langle h_i,\lambda\rangle-1}q_i^{-2k-2}\mathrm{Id}.$$

Applied to the object $R^\Lambda(\beta)$ the same computation gives an
isomorphism of graded $R^\Lambda(\beta)$-bimodules obtained from
$F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ and
$E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_iR^\Lambda(\beta)$ by the displayed summands
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]] for the shift
conventions).

For the STANDARD graded cyclotomic quotient over any field and any real
symmetrizable Cartan datum with admissible graded KLR parameters, put
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, $h_i(\beta)=\langle h_i,\Lambda-\beta\rangle$, and
$q_i=q^{d_i}$. On projective $K_0$ use $F_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i|_\beta=q_i^{-1-h_i(\beta)}E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$; on module $G_0$ use
either the SAME canonical normalization, or the Kang--Kashiwara normalization
$E_i^{\mathrm{KK}}=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$,
$F_i^{\mathrm{KK}}|_\beta=q_i^{1-h_i(\beta)}F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$. In all cases
$K_i|_\beta=q_i^{h_i(\beta)}$. These operators satisfy the full quantum mixed
and Serre relations and are locally nilpotent; their scalar extensions to
$\mathbb Q(q)$ are integrable weight modules. No decomposition into
finite-dimensional full-$\mathfrak g$ submodules is asserted in affine or
indefinite type.

The tensor pairing
$T_\beta(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_{R^\Lambda(\beta)}M)$ is
$A$-BILINEAR and weightwise perfect in normalized projective-cover/simple
bases. The Hom pairing $h(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}(P,M)$
instead satisfies $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$ and is first-bar-sesquilinear. For $T$,
projective $E_i$ is adjoint to module $F_i^{\mathrm{KK}}$ and projective $F_i$
to module $E_i^{\mathrm{KK}}$. The two module actions are conjugate by the
weight rescaling $q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}$, where
$\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)=(\Lambda,\beta)-(\beta,\beta)/2$.

derivations.claim: The blocks. The rank-zero block is $k$ and the rank-one quotient is $k[x]/(x^2)$ with basis $1,x$ and degrees $0,2$. Restriction of the vacuum has zero target. Thus the relevant functor values on the vacuum are $F^\Lambda_ik=R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ and $F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_ik=0$.

The commutator. The relation of [F2] evaluated on the vacuum gives $E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_ik\cong k\oplus k\{2\}$, which is $R^\Lambda(\alpha_i)$ by [F1], so $q^{-2}F^\Lambda_iE^\Lambda_i\oplus\mathrm{Id}\oplus q^2\mathrm{Id}\cong E^\Lambda_iF^\Lambda_i$ holds at the first nontrivial weight.

The Grothendieck commutator. With the normalizations of [F3]: projective $E_iF_i[1_\Lambda]=q^{-1}(1+q^2)[1_\Lambda]=(q+q^{-1})[1_\Lambda]$ and $F_iE_i[1_\Lambda]=0$; KK module $F$ from the vacuum also carries $q^{-1}$ while KK $E$ is raw, and the canonical module action shifts $E$ and leaves $F$ raw, giving the same result in both module conventions. All agree with $(q^2-q^{-2})/(q-q^{-1})$, the mixed relation evaluated at $K_i=q^2$. This verifies the commutator identity at the first nontrivial weight and is a finite rank-one computation using no choice.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]. For $i\in I$ and $n\ge1$ the subalgebra $R(n\alpha_i)$ is generated by the polynomial subalgebra $k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ and the crossings $\tau_1,\dots,\tau_{n-1}$ with $\tau_a^2=0$ (because $Q_{ii}=0$), the braid and far commutation relations, and the nil-Hecke dot moves, i.e. it is the nil Hecke algebra of rank $n$; its PBW basis is $\{x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_n^{a_n}\tau_w\}_{a\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}^n,w\in S_n}$ ([[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]). Fix a reduced expression $w_0=s_{i_1}\cdots s_{i_{\binom n2}}$ of the longest element and put $\partial_{w_0}:=\tau_{i_1}\cdots\tau_{i_{\binom n2}}$ (independent of the reduced expression). The **divided-power idempotent** is
$$e_{i,n}:=x_1^{n-1}x_2^{n-2}\cdots x_{n-1}\,\partial_{w_0}\in R(n\alpha_i),$$
and its horizontal reflection is $\psi(e_{i,n}):=\partial_{w_0}x_1^{n-1}\cdots x_{n-1}$. Both are nonzero idempotents of degree $0$, and $e_{i,n}\ne0$ because the PBW basis separates the monomials involved. The **divided-power projective** is
$$P_{i,n}:=R(n\alpha_i)\,\psi(e_{i,n})\{-d_i\tbinom n2\},$$
where the shift is the one fixed by the source normalization: as a graded left module $R(n\alpha_i)\psi(e_{i,n})$ is the polynomial representation, it is indecomposable projective, and with this shift $R(n\alpha_i)$ is a finite direct sum of $[n]_i!$ shifted copies of $P_{i,n}$, where $[n]_i!=\prod_{a=1}^n\frac{q_i^{a}-q_i^{-a}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}$ is the $q_i$-factorial of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] (at $q_i=1$ it is $n!$); hence $P_{i,n}$ is the unique indecomposable projective summand up to shift and $\mathrm{End}_{R(n\alpha_i)}(P_{i,n})_0=k$. For a divided-power sequence $\theta=i_1^{(n_1)}\cdots i_r^{(n_r)}$ put $\beta=\sum_an_a\alpha_{i_a}$ and $P_\theta:=\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})$ along the ordered concatenation of the blocks of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; then $[P_\theta]$ represents the ordered product of these divided powers; one may reorder only by the proved commuting/Serre relations, adjacent colours need not commute, and for a single colour $\theta=i^{(n)}$ one has the indecomposability above.

**Projective duality.** For a finite graded projective left $R(\beta)$-module $P$ put $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$, the $\psi$-twisted graded Hom into the rank-one free module, where $\psi$ is the horizontal-reflection anti-involution. Evaluation $P^\#\to$ (dual of $P$) identifies $(P^\#)^\#\cong P$ for finite shifted free modules, and hence for every finite graded projective; the duality reverses internal shifts and fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ after the displayed shift.

Let $A=R(\beta)$ and $B=A/J$ be the standard homogeneous cyclotomic quotient.
For an indecomposable finite graded projective generic cover $P(S)$,
$B\otimes_AP(S)$ is its same-head indecomposable $B$-cover if $JS=0$, and is
zero otherwise. Every graded simple/indecomposable projective $B$-orbit arises
this way, and distinct surviving heads do not merge. Finite projective Hom
duality commutes with this base change, and finite vector duality commutes with
inflation. Thus generic normalized $\#$-self-dual covers and $D_\psi$-self-dual
simples supply unique normalized $B$-covers/simples. For these labels
$h(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}\operatorname{HOM}_B(P,S)$ and
$T(P,S)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes_BS)$ are both $\delta_{P,S}$; $T$ is
bilinear and $h$ first-bar sesquilinear. Extension induces a surjection on
projective $K_0$. No Frobenius, geometric basis or cyclotomic crystal premise
is used.

Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. For the standard homogeneous graded quotient over any field, with arbitrary real symmetrizable Cartan datum and admissible graded KLR parameters, there is a unique $U_A$-module isomorphism $\phi:K_0(\mathrm{Proj}\,R^\Lambda)\to V_A(\Lambda)$ sending $1_\Lambda$ to $v_\Lambda$ and intertwining all normalized $E_i,F_i,K_i$ and divided powers. In particular $K_0$ is free over $A$. On the NEGATIVE half the vacuum map has exact kernel
$$\ker(U_A^-\to K_0(R^\Lambda))=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_{s>\lambda_i}U_A^-F_i^{(s)}.$$
This is the integral negative-half presentation; neither a full-$U_A$ quotient by only $F_i^{(\lambda_i+1)}$ nor invertibility of divided-power factorials is asserted.
For projectives, the tensor form $T(P,Q)=\mathrm{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes Q)$ transports to the highest-weight contravariant form normalized by $(v_\Lambda,v_\Lambda)=1$ and $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$, $\sigma(K_i)=K_i$. It is not the generic negative-half Lusztig form with a newly alleged radical.

For the same standard homogeneous general-field/general-Cartan parameters as
the integral projective theorem, the tensor pairing
$T(P,M)=\operatorname{gdim}(P^\psi\otimes M)$ is weightwise perfect and
$A$-bilinear, with normalized cover/simple dual bases. Its associated map
$$\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}:G_0(R^\Lambda)\longrightarrow V_A(\Lambda)^\vee=\bigoplus_\beta\operatorname{Hom}_A (V_A(\Lambda)_{\Lambda-\beta},A),\qquad \Psi_{\mathrm{can}}(M)(\phi(P))=T(P,M)$$
is an isomorphism to the RESTRICTED weight dual, identified inside
$V(\Lambda)$ using the highest-weight contravariant form. It intertwines the
CANONICAL module action having the same normalization as projective $K_0$, and
sends normalized simple classes to the form-dual projective basis. The KK
module action is also sound, but its intertwiner is
$\Psi_{\mathrm{KK}}|_\beta=q^{\operatorname{def}_\Lambda(\beta)}
\Psi_{\mathrm{can}}|_\beta$. Thus an unrescaled KK identification is not
asserted to send simples to the upper global basis. The Hom pairing is instead
first-bar-sesquilinear, $h(P,M)=T(P^\#,M)$; this does not alter the bilinear
tensor-dual identification.

derivations.claim: The blocks and their composition structure. By [F1] the three nonzero blocks have graded dimensions $1$, $1+q^2$ and $(q+q^{-1})^2$; the first regular module $B_1$ has two composition factors $S_1,S_1\{2\}$ with graded dimensions $1+q^2$, and the second block is the endomorphism matrix algebra of the graded column $S_2$, whose regular left module is the column tensored with its graded vector dual of dimension $q+q^{-1}$.

The Cartan pairing. The normalized cover-to-head Hom space is $k$ in degree zero and there are no other simple types in a block, so quotient-cover evaluation of [F2] identifies the tensor pairing with $T(P_r,S_s)=\delta_{rs}$, with distinct roots paired by zero. The integral identification of [F3] maps $P_0,P_1,P_2$ to $v,Fv,F^{(2)}v$ and $[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[P_2]$ to $F^2v$, and in $G_0$ the regular classes are $[B_1]=(1+q^2)[S_1]$ and $[B_2]=(q+q^{-1})[S_2]$.

The restricted dual. The canonical restricted-dual map sends $S_r$ to the form-dual of the corresponding divided lower vector, and since $T$ pairs $P_r$ with $S_s$ by $\delta_{rs}$ it does not identify $B_1$ with $S_1$; the scalar $q+q^{-1}$ is not removed by the pairing. This is a cover/simple pairing computation, not a claim that the Cartan matrix is all ones or that a trace removes a denominator, and it is a finite computation using no choice.
